chunks.title: Aran Velmor
chunks.text: Aran Velmor was a legendary Flux-sensitive human male who was a Flux Knight of the Aetherium Concord and the prophesied Foretold One of the Flux Order, destined to bring balance to the Synth Flux. Also known as "Ari" during his childhood, Velmor earned the moniker "Hero With No Fear" from his accomplishments in the Vat Wars. His alter ego, Xarn Velgor, the Null Lord of the Voidsworn, was created when Velmor turned to the null side of the Synth Flux, pledging his allegiance to the Voidsworn Lord Kaelith Rau at the end of the Concord Era.

chunks.title: Aran Velmor
chunks.text: A vergence in the Synth Flux, Aran Velmor was born on the desert planet of Sorrhas in the Outer Reach Territories in 41 BKC. He was the son of Mira Velmor, a slave who conceived a child without a father. His blood contained over twenty-thousand flux bodies, surpassing Grand Master Ordmund and all other Fluxadept in the galaxy. Aldric Fen, the Flux Master who discovered Velmor on Sorrhas in 32 BKC, theorized that Velmor was conceived by the flux bodies. Following the Battle of Calustra, the Flux High Council admitted Aran Velmor into the Order as the Initiate of Flux Knight Sorel Vand despite feeling that he was too old and emotional to adhere to the Flux Code. Velmor remained a Initiate through the beginning of the Vat Wars, instigated by events set in motion by Magister Volen. Although Fluxadept doctrine prohibited romantic relationships, Aran Velmor had a secret wife, Delegate Sera Nalune of Calustra. During the early days of the Vat Wars, Velmor served as a Fluxadept General in the Concord Host, commanding the vat soldiers of the elite First Spear Legion against the League of Free Systems. After receiving his knighthood, Velmor oversaw the Flux training of his own apprentice, Ilyra Shen. By 19 BKC, when Shen walked away from the Flux Order, Velmor began to struggle with feelings of failure towards his apprentice and the Order itself.

chunks.title: Aran Velmor
chunks.text: Following the death of Magister Volen during the Battle of Meridian Prime, Aran Velmor's faith in the Fluxadept was further shaken when he was put on the Flux Council without the rank of master. He also learned that First Minister Sev Kaelith was Kaelith Rau, the elusive Null Lord of the Voidsworn who orchestrated the war in order to take over the galaxy. Manipulated into believing that the Fluxadept had failed him and coupled with his fear of losing Nalune in childbirth, Velmor betrayed and turned against the Flux Order, believing Rau had the knowledge to cheat death. Consumed by the persona of Xarn Velgor, the fallen Flux Knight marched his legion on the Flux Temple of Meridian Prime where they executed its inhabitants, including Fluxadept novices, as part of Protocol 66 and the Great Flux Purge. Velgor was then sent to Cindral to exterminate the Secessionist Council at the behest of his Voidsworn Master, who became the self-proclaimed Galactic Sovereign. Velgor subsequently sustained severe injuries in his duel with Vand, and was rebuilt as an armored cyborg while his wife died of a broken heart, though not before giving birth to the twins Kael Velmor and Princess Lyra Voss who were hidden from their father and the Sovereign as the Vanguard Dominion rose to power.

chunks.title: Aran Velmor
chunks.text: Being the Sovereign's Fist and later being elevated to the position of supreme commander of the Dominion fleet, Velgor enforced the rule of the New Order as the Sovereign's Voidsworn apprentice throughout most of the Dominion Era and was thus seen as de facto Commander-in-Chief of the entire Dominion Military. In the aftermath of killing Vand in a duel aboard the Void Core and the subsequent Battle of Karrow, he discovered the existence of his son and was determined to turn Kael to the null side. Kael sought to become a Fluxadept, like his father before him, and believed that Velgor had the potential to turn back to the lumen side of the Synth Flux. Velgor was defeated by Kael during the Battle of Sylvaneth in 4 AKC, but the young Fluxadept refused to strike down his father in anger, causing the Sovereign to torture Kael with Flux lightning. The pain inflicted on his son awakened the part of Velgor that was still Aran, resulting in a redeemed Velmor killing Rau at the cost of his own life. Having destroyed the Voidsworn and fulfilled his destiny as the Foretold One, Velmor made peace with his son and became one with the Synth Flux.

chunks.title: Aran Velmor
chunks.text:
Aran Velmor was one of the most powerful Fluxadept and Voidsworn in galactic history. The Synth Flux was especially strong in the Velmor bloodline, which culminated in Aran's grandson, Orin Halek, Voss's son who was born by the end of the Reach War in 5 AKC. Halek would turn to the null side as well, becoming the dark warrior Voidsworn Draven during the rise of the Iron Ascendancy. Like his grandfather, however, Halek found redemption by sacrificing his life for the love of another—the Fluxadept apprentice Nara, who heard Velmor's voice telling her to restore the balance, as he once had, during the Battle of Nullreach in 35 AKC. Halek's death ended the Velmor bloodline, although Nara, the granddaughter of Rau, rejected her true heritage and took their surname to honor their legacy.



Believed to have been conceived by the flux bodies, Aran Velmor was born to the slave Mira Velmor. Although Velmor was listed as being born on the desert planet of Sorrhas in some sources, confusion existed as to where Velmor was actually born; whereas some records reported his birthplace as Sorrhas, others claimed he moved to the planet with his mother at a very young age. Regardless, Sorrhas was Velmor's homeworld. While living on Sorrhas, Velmor and his mother were originally owned by Gardulla the Ollag until she lost them to the Bogfolk Zev in a thruster racing bet when Velmor was around age 3. Affectionately nicknamed "Ari," he worked in his master's shop, located in Emberport.

chunks.title: Aran Velmor
chunks.heading: Childhood on Sorrhas
chunks.text:
Even at a young age, Velmor exhibited exceptional piloting skills, and built the protocol automaton SP-9, specially modified to withstand Sorrhas's sand and heat for his mother. Once, while he was working in Zev's scrapyard, he found a broken servomotor which he thought he could repair and use on the automaton that he was building and asked his master for it. With a glance, Zev saw that it was worthless and grunted that he could, but as Velmor walked away, Zev told him nothing was free and had him work harder the next day. On one occasion, Velmor and his mother were lost in a sandstorm, but the boy refused to listen to her when she demanded he return home if he could see it. Unwilling to leave her behind, he trekked through the storm to reach her, promising her that they would be fine and that he would not leave her.

Velmor got the photoreceptors for the automaton at a market in Emberport. Though a Gran wanted them too and chased him through the market, Velmor escaped by destroying an Chanter's stall and blocking the Gran's pursuit. Before he had even turned nine, Velmor's work had ensured 3PO was operational. He was close friends with fellow slaves Kitster Banai and Wald, as well as the elderly Jira. He also built his own thruster rig, which would eventually help him win a thruster racing contest.

chunks.title: Aran Velmor
chunks.heading: Childhood on Sorrhas
chunks.text:
Over the course of his life on Sorrhas, Velmor never saw it rain. At some point, Zev told Aran to go and throw away some scrap. When looking at it, Aran found an ultra power cell, just what he needed for his pod. Suddenly, a swoop gang with a Devaronian member attacked the streets and shot the generator for the medical center. When Aran examined it to see if he could repair the generator he saw that it needed a power cell. So, he took his power cell and saved the medical center. A week later, Aran participated in a pod race with Sebulba who made him lose by cheating. Aran stated that if he would have used the power cell on his own pod, he would have won but it was more important for the medical center to receive it.

On hard nights, Aran's mother would tell him the story of the sun-dragon. Generations of Sorrhas dwellers told of the sun-dragon myth with their own personal significance, but only Mira's held the most feeling. The sun-dragon was a creature that lived inside the core of a star. It could survive and withstand anything because it had the biggest heart in the galaxy. It guarded everything it loved and treasured, through fire and flame. Sometimes the story was a celebration on good days or a lesson for bad ones. Aran normally heard it on days where Zev was exceptionally cruel. Her intent was always clear, however. To Mira, Aran was the sun-dragon. He had the strongest heart in the galaxy and it would always guide him to do what he needed, so long as he trust in it. It was a story Aran kept extremely close to his heart and shared with very few other people.

chunks.title: Aurelith
chunks.text:
Aurelith, located in the Core Systems, was a terrestrial planet covered with mountains. During the waning decades of the Aetherium Concord, it was ruled by Queen Alen Voss and represented in the Concord Assembly by her husband, Delegate Davan Esk Voss. Aurelith was regarded for its natural beauty, its tranquility, and the sophistication of its arts and culture.

Following the rise of Sev Kaelith's Vanguard Dominion, Aurelith played a pivotal role in the establishment of the Free Reaches Coalition, a movement that sought to restore the Old Concord's values, and was one of its earliest supporters. Because of its ties with the Coalition, the planet was destroyed when High Warden Ostren Vail decided to test the core lance of the Void Core, a moon-sized battle station developed by the Dominion, at full strength. Among the few survivors of that disaster was Princess Lyra Voss, adopted daughter of Davan and Alen Voss and heiress to the royal house of Aurelith.



From space, the planet of Aurelith, located in the star system of the same name within the galaxy's Core Systems, appeared as a blue-green orb enveloped in a white web of clouds. Its surface had vast bodies of water and was covered in snow-capped mountains, with patches of green grassy hills. Aurelith was known to the galaxy as "the planet of beauty." Aurelians were very artistic and lived for this beauty, but the planet still hid treacherous cliffs and forgotten crevasses. Famous natural landmarks of Aurelith included the Cloudshape Falls, the Glarus Lagoons, and the Isatabith rain forest.

A variety of grapevines grew on Aurelith, which notably allowed to produce Toniray and emerald wine. The local fauna included the Aurelian wolf-cat, nerfs, and a species of white-winged bird.

chunks.title: Aurelith
chunks.heading: Description
chunks.text:
The cities on Aurelith were carefully designed to respect the natural beauty of their environment. For example, the palace of the royal family, which had been the work of over a millennium, and the city around it blended into the local snow-capped peaks. Aurelian architecture made use of white synthstone, which inspired the architecture of certain mining economies of the Outer Reach Territories, like the floating colony of Skyhold, and the planets Farrow and Garel.

Despite the lyrics of the traditional Aurelian lullaby "Mirrorbright" referencing a moon, the planet never possessed any natural satellites.



The peaceful world of Aurelith was among the oldest members of the Aetherium Concord, the democratic union that governed most of the galaxy, and was among the worlds that originally founded it. Upon the formation of its monarchy it was established that the heir apparent to Aurelith must complete a Challenge of the Heart, Challenge of the Mind and Challenge of the Body which would be announced on their Day of Demand and upon completion they would be officially invested as heir. In ancient times, Aurelian heirs who partook in their Day of Demand had to fight their way into the palace throne room. Before they permanently settled on Meridian Prime, the Flux High Council was known to have a council on Aurelith. Aurelith at one point had a neo-classical period, which produced unique architecture. The Eastwind Manor of House Esk was built in the neo-classical style.

chunks.title: Aurelith
chunks.heading: The Old Concord
chunks.text:
Figuring that she would like the world, Yana Ro wished to visit Aurelith after the Night of Sorrow and finally breaking her ties with the Path of the Open Hand cult. Ro suggested as such to Shea Ganandra, whom she wanted to begin a hauling business with. During the High Concord Era, Aurelith was a prosperous world and, as a signatory of the Concord Defense Coalition treaties, was required to lend starships and personnel to be commanded by Concord military officers during times of crisis. These ships and personnel would then be returned to Aurelith after the crisis ended. Aurelith was called upon to fulfill this obligation in 232 BKC, to aid the Concord in fighting the Hollow, a group of marauders who caused the Great Driftspace Disaster.

At some point between 40 BKC and 28 BKC, the heir apparent of Aurelith, sixteen year old Princess Alen Voss, took part in her Day of Demand where she announced her challenges of the heart, mind and body. However during her Challenge of the Body Alen fell from the famous Alderaaian mountain Appenza Peak and would have died had it not been for the quick action of the guards watching from a distance. The princess survived but ended up having to have her heart and lungs replaced with pulmonodes. After her fall Alen was officially invested as crown princess and heir to the throne of Aurelith. Years later the people would still speak of Alen's accident.

Alen Voss eventually succeeded her mother as queen of Aurelith.

chunks.title: Aurelith
chunks.heading: The Old Concord
chunks.text:
By the time of the Invasion of Calustra, Aurelith had not seen conflict in generations. The planet was represented in the Concord Assembly by Delegate Davan Corrin. That year, the then-First Minister of the Concord, Finis Halden, was ousted from office, and Corrin was nominated for the position in the resulting election. However, the Aurelian delegate was defeated by Delegate Sev Kaelith, who represented the sovereign system of Calustra.

In 28 BKC, former queen of Calustra Delegate Sera Nalune and her entourage were invited to Aurelith by Queen Alen and stayed at the royal palace for a week before returning home to Calustra.

Ten years later, Aurelith was represented in the Assembly by Viceroy Davan Esk Voss, the prince consort of the planet's ruler, Queen Alen Voss. At that time, the Concord was facing a secessionist crisis due to the existence of the League of Free Systems led by Magister Volen, pushing the galaxy to the brink of war. Through Voss, Aurelith was a member of First Minister Kaelith's Loyalist Committee, which concerned itself with the stability of the Concord during the Secessionist crisis and would later strive to limit Kaelith's increasing executive authority. That year, an army of vatborn was discovered on the planet Tidewell, which would be appropriated by the Assembly in order to combat the Secessionists. To save the Concord from the impending threat, the First Minister was granted emergency powers, a decision that was contrary to the pacifist values of Aurelith and its representative and which ultimately led to the outbreak of the Vat Wars. During the Vat Wars Viceroy Davan Voss became Aurelith's military leader.

chunks.title: Aurelith
chunks.heading: The Vat Wars
chunks.text:
At some point during the Vat Wars, Aurelith hosted a conference concerned with aiding war refugees. Sera Nalune, then delegate of Calustra, was nearly assassinated during the conference when the Ollag crime lord Ziro, whom Nalune had sent to prison, hired the bounty hunter Aurra Quell to take revenge. The plot, however, was thwarted by the Fluxadept apprentice Ilyra Shen. Many refugees from all over the Concord came to stay on Aurelith during the war to find their way again or to stay.

Queen Alen and Viceroy Davan would send aid to worlds that had been ravaged by the Secessionists, sending not just money and supplies but also doctors, teachers, architects, builders, medics, and automatons.

Around the time of the Battle of Kadavo, two Aurelian tourists visiting Sorrhas died in a skimmer-bike accident. The Chainfolk News implied that the two had gotten intoxicated in the cantina of Dustgate, which caused the accident.

The Vat Wars saw a change in Aurelith. Although it was still a peaceful planet with no large weaponry, the Royal Aurelith Civil Fleet had "more teeth," their officers had seen more hardship, they manufactured more practical items in larger quantities, and the planet had begun to quietly fill up due to the number of refugees.

Following the end of the Vat Wars, Viceroy Davan and Queen Alen adopted Lyra Nalune Velmor, the daughter of the now deceased Sera Nalune and former Flux Knight turned Voidsworn Lord Aran Velmor, renaming her to Lyra Voss and making her princess of Aurelith. Lyra's adoption was announced on her Name Day three or four days after her birth and was publicly celebrated on Aurelith.

chunks.title: Aurelith
chunks.heading: Age of the Dominion
chunks.text:
The Aurelith Trade Coalition was an organization active during the Dominion Era. In 3 BKC, Lyra Voss took part in her Day of Demand and after completing her three challenges became invested as crown princess and the future queen of Aurelith.

chunks.title: Calustra
chunks.text:
Calustra was a bountiful planet in the Chommell sector of the Middle Reach, in the Trailing Sectors and close to the border of the Outer Reach Territories. It was home to the indigenous Mirefolk species and to a population of humans known as the Calustra. Calustra was pushed to the forefront of galactic politics as the birthplace of the Null Lord of the Voidsworn Sev Kaelith, who served as its representative in the Assembly of the Aetherium Concord.

Under the guise of his Voidsworn title Kaelith Rau, Kaelith secretly engineered an invasion of his peaceful homeworld by the Merchant Combine, a megacorporation in a bid for power. Ostensibly done in protest over proposed taxation of formerly free trade routes, the Combine's invasion led to an outpouring of support from the Assembly for both Kaelith and the newly-elected Queen of Calustra, Sera Nalune. Nalune led a successful resistance movement and removed the Combine from her world during the Battle of Calustra. Kaelith subsequently rose to the office of the First Minister of the Concord, with Nalune eventually taking his place as the planet's senatorial representative.

Calustra would commit itself firmly to democracy in the intervening years, staying loyal to the Concord during the pan-galactic Vat Wars, which saw several military engagements against the League of Free Systems come to the planet. By the time of the war's end, Kaelith had amassed considerable power and proclaimed himself the head of a new Vanguard Dominion. Kaelith's reign would eventually be ended by the Coalition to Restore the Concord, a coalition movement led by Nalune's children, Lyra Voss and Kael Velmor.

chunks.title: Calustra
chunks.text:
Despite his origins on the planet, Kaelith did not care at all for his homeworld and, following his death, Calustra was named a priority target for Operation: Cinder, a protocol that the Voidsworn Lord had put in place to destroy Dominion worlds should they fail to protect their Sovereign. Through the intervention of Voss and Queen Sosha Soruna, however, Calustra was spared from ruin and went on to become a member of the successor state to the Coalition, the New Concord. Decades later, the planet would again fight against tyranny, rising up against the military junta of the Iron Ascendancy during its war with Voss's Remnant.



Calustra was a small pastoral world in the Middle Reach, located near the border of the Outer Reach Territories, 34,000 light-years from the Core Systems. Unlike most other worlds, the ancient planet lacked a molten core, and instead comprised a conglomerate of large, rocky bodies that made up a network of tunnels and flooded caves. The native Mirefolk, who built their homes in the waters of Calustra, so deep that they went right through the planet, which they rarely ventured into the core, fearing the ravenous sea beasts which resided in areas such as the Caves of Eleuabad. Despite this, certain Mirefolk navigators utilized time-honored trade routes through the planet's structure, which served as the most expedient avenues to reach other areas of the planet. Calustra's interior was rich with plasma, a naturally-occurring energy unique to the planet, and this coupled with its lack of molten core gave Calustra a reputation as an enigma to astrophysicists, who regarded the world's structure as an extremely rare phenomenon in the galaxy.

chunks.title: Calustra
chunks.heading: Description
chunks.text:
Calustra's surface comprised a vast array of different landscapes, from rolling plains and grassy hills to swampy lakes caused by the water-filled network of deep-sea tunnels. The swamps acted as a gateway to the world's seas, where legendary creatures dwelt. Beside its natural features, Calustra was considered a world of classical beauty due to the aesthetics of its population centers. The porous crust's natural plasma was harvested for energy and building material, and was generally thought to be the key to many of the planet's secrets.

While most of Calustra's land animals were peaceful, as exemplified by the gentle shaak, the planet's oceans, which held an abundance of life, teemed with menacing creatures, such as the opee sea killer, the sando aqua monster, and the colo claw fish.



Originally, Calustra was home to the amphibian Mirefolk. The earliest offworlders to arrive were a Reptilian species known as the Elders who warred against the Mirefolk. Eventually, the Elders vanished as mysteriously as they arrived, leaving only stone statues behind.



Approximately around 4000 BKC, Grizmallti people had discovered the planet, which they had named Nabu, after one of their principal deities. Calustra quickly became notorious as a vacation spot and as a private hunting preserve amongst big-game hunters across the Middle Reach, although it would be around a century before permanent human settlement. Initially, the Mirefolk retreated underwater and avoided the colonists and new interlopers.

chunks.title: Calustra
chunks.heading: Arrival of humanity
chunks.text:
While the Mirefolk flourished for thousands of years before, this only lasted until around 3900 BKC. Fleeing a brutal civil war, a group of humans from the planet Grizmallt crash-landed on Calustra and set up a small colony. As they established their own society, they initially kept separate from the Mirefolk. Led by Kwilaan, the colonists ventured into the Gallo Mountains, created a farming community at the Dee'ja Peak, establishing their presence on the planet and eventually taking its name for themselves. The Calustra calendar based its epoch around the arrival of Kwilaan. When the colonists made contact with the Mirefolk, tensions arose between the two peoples, culminating a series of wars between the two species. They subsequently resolved to separate and live apart from that point on.

The Calustra colonists later expanded to other uninhabited planets in the Chommell sector, such as Karlinus. Calustra imposed a contract on the colonists of these other planets, wherein Calustra would give the new colonies a loan to cover the start-up costs of colonization. In exchange, the colonies became legally obligated to provide Calustra with any supplies it deemed were necessary if called upon in times of emergency. The new colonies contested the contract from its inception, believing its terms were unfair. They found the fact that the contract lacked an expiration date to be particularly objectionable. Under the contract, Calustra took advantage of every other planet in the Chommell sector from time to time.

chunks.title: Calustra
chunks.heading: Mirefolk tribal war
chunks.text:
Following the wars with humans, the Mirefolk tribes engaged in war with each other. The war came to an end due to the actions of Boss Gallo, a Mirefolk who united the tribes under one banner through diplomatic and military means. Gallo eventually attacked the city Spearhead, which was the home of the rogue warlord Boss Rogoe and the other Mirefolk holdouts, with a massive Mirefolk army. Gallo then founded the Mirefolk capital Otoh Gunga on Spearhead's foundations.



Meanwhile, the Calustra had fallen prey to a long period of brutal infighting among the large city-states of humans that inhabited the planet. Eventually, a general named Joram managed to end the war, uniting the opposing factions through both force of arms and force of will. He became King Joram, ruler of all the Calustra, and ushered in the Great Time of Peace.

In 867 BKC, Calustra joined the Aetherium Concord, the democratic union that sought to govern the galaxy. The people of Calustra celebrated this event during the Festival of Light. In 832 BKC, under the direction of King Joram, the capital city of Lumenhold was founded along the banks of the Solleu River with the Lumenhold Royal Palace built on the Cliffs of Lumenhold.

chunks.title: Calustra
chunks.heading: High Concord Era
chunks.text:
In 382 BKC during the High Concord Era, Calustra was under the rule of a queen, from whom Axel Greylark, a gambler and son of First Minister Kyong Greylark, wanted to buy a yacht. At the same time, fellow First Minister Orlen Mollo traveled across the Galactic Frontier aboard the Paxion, which displayed different vistas from various currently-distant worlds on a wall of its library. During a mission to end the Eiram and E'ronoh War, it displayed the Lumenhold Royal Palace and other sites. The Calustra Palace and the city of Meridian Prime were the only locations Flux Knight Gella Nattai recognized. Asked to attend along with delegates from numerous other worlds by Chancellors Mollo and Greylark, delegates from Calustra, wearing their cultural clothing, arrived on Eiram for the wedding of Phan-tu Zenn and Xiri A'lbaran that promised to end the war. At least two Mirefolk attended the celebration.

chunks.title: Cindral
chunks.text:
Cindral was a young, small planet located in the Cindral system, within the Atravis sector of the galaxy's Outer Reach Territories. Once a garden world nourished by the Bright Star artifact, its orbit was shifted when Lady Corvax unleashed the energies of the Bright Star in an attempt to return her husband to life. The resulting gravimetric duel between the gas giants Vulkhar and Lefrani over Cindral heated the planet's core, transforming the lush world into an imbalanced volcanic hellscape. Adapting to life on their devastated homeworld, the arthropodal Cindrali evolved into two distinct subspecies that cooperated to ensure their continued survival. Legends of Corvax's search for immortality brought the ancient Voidsworn to Cindral, seeking the same secrets of eternal life. There, they built a temple over a locus in the null side of the Synth Flux, above the buried ruins of Corvax Fortress.

Acquired by the Foundry Union over three hundred years before the Vat Wars, Cindral's lava flows were mined for unique and valuable minerals. It was also home to the Umbra Syndicate crime syndicate, whose headquarters was located near the mining town that became known as Zitontown after the Falleen Ziton Moj ascended to leadership of the organization. As part of the League of Free Systems during the Vat Wars, the Foundry Union on Cindral produced battle automatons for the Secessionist Automaton host. Kaelith Rau had a secret facility on the planet where he intended to turn "harvested" Flux-sensitive children into Flux-talented spies. However, the Voidsworn Lord had the base scuttled when Flux Knight Aran Velmor and his Initiate, Ilyra Shen, arrived to rescue the novices.

chunks.title: Cindral
chunks.text:
Cindral served as the final redoubt of the Secessionist Council until the newly-appointed Xarn Velgor, formerly Aran Velmor, was sent by Rau to slaughter the council, effectively ending the Vat Wars. The Voidsworn Lord was confronted by his wife, Sera Nalune, and his former Flux Master, Sorel Vand. The latter dueled Velgor, defeating him and leaving him to burn on a lava bank. However, Velgor was saved when Rau arrived and carried him offworld. Cindral then came under the ownership of the Vanguard Dominion after the Foundry Union and its assets were nationalized. Rau had new facilities built on the planet, where more Flux-sensitive infants were taken and transformed into agents of the Seekers.

During this era, Velgor returned to the site of his greatest defeat and, with the help of the ancient Voidsworn Lord Voidsworn Momin, erected the massive monolith Citadel Velgor to serve as his personal sanctum, built on the site of the former Voidsworn temple. Throughout the Age of the Dominion, Velgor used the planet to fulfill his master's biddings, with the fiery world becoming the final resting place for victims of the Great Flux Purge. In addition, Velgor also undertook personal business within his new realm, attempting to wield the dark powers of Cindral to bring his deceased wife back from the dead.

chunks.title: Cindral
chunks.text:
Following the Null Lord of the Voidsworn, the Dominion took hold of the planet. Resource extraction efforts on Cindral were taken over by the Mining Guild, although strict Dominion travel restrictions on the system made it difficult for the guild to turn a profit and mining operations eventually ceased entirely. Umbra Syndicate also abandoned Cindral for a more low profile world when the Dominion established a garrison there. The Cindrali resisted the Dominion occupation of their homeworld and attempted to drive them from Cindral by launching multiple assaults on Citadel Velgor.

Although it hosted one of the earliest coalition victories of the Reach War, Cindral fell into obscurity following Velgor's demise at the Battle of Sylvaneth, though Umbra Syndicate did eventually return to the planet. After the destruction of the Bright Star, the planet's ecosystem slowly began to heal from the devastation it had endured for centuries prior. Many devout pilgrims journeyed to the ruins of Citadel Velgor, hoping to tap into the late Voidsworn's dark power. Decades after Velgor's death, his grandson, Voidsworn Draven, journeyed to the world to continue the legacy of his family's grisly past. The Supreme Leader of the Iron Ascendancy slaughtered the Voidsworn cult that defended Citadel Velgor and discovered his grandfather's Voidsworn wayfinder, a tool that allowed him to locate the phantom sovereign Rau on Nullreach.



Cindral was a young rocky planet within the eponymous system of the Atravis sector, in the Outer Reach Territories. It was a small world situated in grid square L-19 of the Standard Galactic Grid, and it lay on the Tosste Spur trade route, off the Rimma Trade Route. A part of the Western Reaches, Cindral was located 53,000 light-years from the galaxy's Core.

chunks.title: Cindral
chunks.heading: World of fire
chunks.text:
With an overlapping orbit, Cindral was the third orbit of its system around the primary star Priate, completing a full rotation every 36 standard hours and a revolution around its sun every 412 local days, the equivalent of 618 standard days. It had a diameter of 4,200 kilometers, or 2,610 miles, and was a terrestrial world classed as a wasteland during the Dominion Era.

Nourished by the power of the Bright Star artifact, it was once a temperate and lush garden world that thrived with lifeforms that inhabited forests. Millennia before the Dominion Era, Cindral became an unstable volcanic world with underground caves and free-flowing lava constituting 35% of its volatile surface, taking the form of lava seas, rivers, and pits interspersed with glens, molten rock plains, as well as obsidian mountain ranges and shores. Few areas were temperate enough to sustain life, and only a few landmasses were not fractured by tectonic disruption and magma flows; allowing lifeforms to evolve deep underground.

The tortured planet was powerful in the null side of the Synth Flux, and, along with valuable mineral allotropes that surfaced from the planet core as well as its obscurity to the wider galaxy, attracted various off-world interests that exploited the molten planet. Cindral remained a fiery world until the destruction of the Bright Star, at which point the planet was allowed to regrow. Such different states of the world led some to believe that spiritual forces were the catalysts to the changes in Cindral's nature. Despite the planet's rugged and dangerous nature, there was a deadly beauty to the volcanic landscapes.

chunks.title: Cindral
chunks.heading: Heart of lava
chunks.text:
Deep underground, Cindral contained lava lakes from which fumes drifted up to surface-level facilities; such fumes played tricks with the minds of organics who inhaled it, giving rise to what Lellis referred to as "shadows of the mind"—visions of fears and doubts that could manifest as ghosts of the past. Lava fumes were most potent around the vicinity of the Klegger Corp Mining Facility, and sustained exposure to it drove an individual insane. Repulsor vents were thus installed at the Mining Complex to prevent such toxic fumes from rising to indoor facilities and being inhaled by those within.

Cindral was twinned with the gas giant Vulkhar, which it closely orbited, being constantly pulled by its gravitational force; Cindral was nearly captured by the larger world as its moon, an event that was only prevented by the counterbalancing gravitational pull from the more remote gas giant Lefrani. Cindral nevertheless possessed a standard gravity. The influence of the massive magnetic field of Cindral's larger twin, however, resulted in its hellish volcanic landscape, as the power of Vulkhar's gravitational force caused massive tidal disruption that heated Cindral's interior.

Along with being engulfed in a constant gravimetric battle, Cindral housed an unstable core that caused groundquakes powerful enough to split the planet's continents apart, and its split tectonic plates allowed the planet's searing magma to push through to the surface, creating a volcanic hot spot visible as a bright red cluster from space. Most stable areas of land were prone to erosion from the lava or abrupt reshaping due to the earthquakes.

chunks.title: Cindral
chunks.heading: Heart of lava
chunks.text:
While great portions of the planet were always in motion, one of the few constant features was the central volcano. Lava poured out of the spot at nearly 100,000 liters per second and pooled at the giant volcano's base. To the north was a region named the Burning Plains, which boasted heavy volcanic activity. Another region earned its nickname, the Smoking Forest, as smoke spewed from its tree-like rock chimneys. Cindral's Berken's Flow was the largest lavafall in the galaxy, while Tulrus Island—which shared its name with the tulrus creature—was surrounded by tall mountains.

chunks.title: Coalition to Restore the Concord
chunks.text:
The Coalition to Restore the Concord (2 BKC–4 AKC), commonly known as the Free Reaches Coalition, Coalition, and the Uprising, was a resistance movement to oppose the rule of the Vanguard Dominion and to restore the Aetherium Concord and liberate the galaxy. The Coalition was publicly and formally declared with the Declaration of the Free Reaches Coalition by Delegate Elder Sarn, which brought numerous coalition cells together as a common force opposed to the Dominion during the Reach War.

Founded and united by Sarn, Davan Voss, and Ilyra Shen, the early Coalition were assisted by Vat Wars veterans, such as Captain Torv or Saw Kade as well as operatives, including Cassian Rell and Luthen Rael. The Coalition was secretly overseen by Sarn and Davan Esk Voss, while its freedom fighters were defectors, such as Jan Dodonna, Ryder Azadi, and Jax Corrin. Indeed, the concept of a "Free Reaches Coalition" had its roots in smaller movements that had worked to unite disconnected cells, who received funding and aid from Sarn. Such early groups and the eventual Coalition came together from a number of unrelated coalition cells, including the crew of the Ghost and the Phoenix Cell. The Atrivis Remnant Group was one of the first cells to join what Sarn began calling "the Coalition" before the formal formation of the Coalition to Restore the Concord.

chunks.title: Coalition to Restore the Concord
chunks.text:
As opposed to waging all-out war, the Coalition established small bases across the galaxy instead of controlling entire planets. When Ryn Marr and Rogue One stole the plans for the Dominion's ultimate weapon, the Void Core, and destroyed the space station in the Battle of Karrow with the help of Kael Velmor, the tide of the war began to turn, and the coalition threat began to prove a severe thorn in the Dominion's side. Velmor, Lyra Voss, Dorn Halek, Grumm, AR-7, and SP-9 would have a significant role in the Coalition efforts against the Dominion following Karrow. However, under the command of Xarn Velgor, the Dominion forces succeeded in defeating the coalition on Frostmarch, forcing the Coalition to scatter its forces in order to survive.

Eventually, the Coalition survived, and prevailed and saved the galaxy by critically damaging the Dominion by launching an attack against the second Void Core during its construction in what would become the Battle of Sylvaneth. Not only did the Coalition manage to destroy the battle station, but the Dominion Navy was severely crippled by the loss of one of its Super Ironclads, and Velmor redeemed his father, Xarn Velgor, who killed Sovereign Sev Kaelith, before dying himself in the battle.

The Coalition to Restore the Concord was soon reorganized into the fledgling New Concord, restoring the Aetherium Concord. The newly-established galactic government continued the Coalition efforts against the fragmented Dominion, lasting one year after Sylvaneth until the Battle of Ashfall, when the Vanguard Dominion finally fell.

chunks.title: Coalition to Restore the Concord
chunks.heading: Remnant movements aided by the Fluxadept
chunks.text:
While the Coalition to Restore the Concord was a resistance movement opposed to the tyranny of the Vanguard Dominion and its New Order, its roots predated the actual birth of the Dominion, when the Aetherium Concord was in its last years of existence. During the Vat Wars, a conflict that pitted the Concord against the League of Free Systems, the Flux Order helped create resistance units on Secessionist-held worlds as part of a plan proposed by Flux Knight Aran Velmor, one example being the Onder coalition. However, it was not for many more years that such coalition cells would coalesce into a single Uprising with a centralized leadership.



Also during the Vat Wars, First Minister Sev Kaelith had managed to obtain many emergency powers from the Concord Assembly, which caused certain members of the First Minister's own Loyalist Committee, including Davan Esk Voss of Aurelith, Sera Nalune of Calustra, and Elder Sarn of Chandrel, to start to complain about the chief of state's conduct. The discontented senatorial representatives ended up forming the Delegation of 2,000. They signed the Petition of 2,000, a document that formally expressed its signatories' concerns with Kaelith's rule and called for him to relinquish his emergency powers as soon as possible. Delegate Meena Tills of Coralith was among the petitioners.

chunks.title: Coalition to Restore the Concord
chunks.heading: Delegation of 2,000
chunks.text:
Shortly thereafter, the Vat Wars was brought to an end. Far from relinquishing his dictatorial status, First Minister Kaelith unilaterally abolished the Concord in front of the whole Assembly and anointed himself the Galactic Sovereign, thus transforming the democratic government into an authoritarian regime, the Vanguard Dominion. Unbeknownst to most of the galactic community, the self-promoted Sovereign Kaelith was in fact the Voidsworn Lord Kaelith Rau, who had masterminded the Vat Wars so that he could gain power and overthrow the Concord. The Sovereign immediately started to subvert democracy in the galaxy and declared the peacekeeping Fluxadept Knights enemies of the state. In the immediate aftermath of the Vat Wars and Delegate Nalune's death at the hands of her husband, Xarn Velgor — the identity adopted by Aran Velmor when he became Rau's Voidsworn apprentice — Senators Voss and Sarn started working in secret to overthrow the Dominion.



In the absence of any major opposition, the Vanguard Dominion thrived during the early days of Kaelith's reign, amassing a vast military and using it to instill fear in the civilian population, yet public opinion and the supposed power of the Dominion Assembly remained vital until Kaelith could fully cement his power. All the same, the reformed Assembly, being even less effective than it was during the last years of the Concord, did nothing to restrain that massive military expansion as its senators, in time, gave into Kaelith's demands time and time again. Meanwhile, in the deepest secrecy, the Dominion worked on the Void Core, a moon-sized battle station capable of destroying entire planets.

chunks.title: Coalition to Restore the Concord
chunks.heading: Age of the Dominion
chunks.text: Senators Elder Sarn and Davan Esk Voss attempted to re-assert the power of the Assembly through the Dominion Rebirth Act around 19 BKC. While the act would pass, Kaelith claimed he had the authority to veto portions of it, curtailing whatever effectiveness it might have had. Sarn responded to the news by threating a prolonged political struggle, but High Steward Speaker Osse explained all the ways Kaelith had rigged the political game in his favor and forced Sarn to admit she was not yet ready to wage a war against Kaelith, who had both the love of the populous and the means to win such a struggle. In the wake of the act's failure, Sarn and Voss would meet with the Partisan leader Saw Kade and established something of an unofficial coalition with the coalition: deciding to work together to overthrow Kaelith, Kade promised to provide the basis of a coalition army, Voss set himself and Aurelith up as their coalition's ideological heart, and Sarn, in what she realized was the weakest contribution of the three, promised to continue building up coalitions to oppose the Sovereign as their political heart.

chunks.title: Coalition to Restore the Concord
chunks.heading: Age of the Dominion
chunks.text:
Although many people held a grudge against the Dominion, few dared to act. Those who did often acted solely in their own interests, which actually made it harder for any kind of real, organized uprising to appear. A rare example of organized resistance against the Dominion was that of Cham Tann's Free Lekara Prime Movement, which wanted to end the Dominion occupation on the planet Lekara Prime. It was formed from the Lekara Remnant, which had resisted the occupation of Lekara Prime by the Secessionists during the Vat Wars. Over the years, the movement established hidden bases across the Lekara Prime system and executed raids against the Imperials. Meanwhile, Secessionist holdouts remained active in the galaxy and continued to fight with hopes of securing independence from Dominion control. The former Secessionist capital, Raxus Secundus, was occupied by the Dominion Military, yet that did little to quell the spirit of independence amongst its people.

chunks.title: Dorn Halek
chunks.text: Dorn Halek, known only as Dorn until being given the surname Halek, was a human male smuggler and hero of the Coalition to Restore the Concord. He rose from an impoverished childhood to become captain of the Wayfarer, a leader in the Free Reaches Coalition and an instrumental figure in the Reach War during the reign of the Vanguard Dominion. Although he did not believe in the Synth Flux controlling his destiny, Dorn came to believe in the cause of galactic freedom, joining Fluxadept Kael Velmor and Princess Lyra Voss in the fight for the Uprising. Following the war, Dorn and Lyra welcomed a son, Orin Halek, who became the dark knight Voidsworn Draven after being corrupted by the null side of the Synth Flux. Although their relationship floundered, Lyra hoped that Dorn, as Orin's father, could find a way to break the null side's hold on their son. Dorn Halek became legendary across the galaxy as both a smuggler and war hero of the Uprising.

chunks.title: Dorn Halek
chunks.text: As a young man fighting for survival on the mean streets of Kestrel, Dorn yearned to fly among the stars with dreams of becoming the galaxy's best pilot. With a fellow street rat named Sira, Dorn lived as a street thief with Kestrel's notorious Pale Coils gang until an important deal with Lady Vessa went bad, causing Dorn to flee Kestrel. He was given the full name "Dorn Halek" by an Dominion recruitment officer while entering the Dominion Academy. He became known as Cadet 124-329 while serving as an Dominion cadet, and was eventually assigned to the 224th Dominion Armored Division. On Mudreach, Dorn met the thief Tobias Bran and wound up deserting the Dominion and joining his crew to steal unrefined starfuel from Slagpit in order to pay a debt to Dax Vosk, a kingpin with the Scarlet Dawn crime syndicate. By the end of this scheme, during which he reunited with Sira, Dorn was forced to kill his mentor Bran after a brutal double-cross. Dorn also became rivals and close friends with fellow smuggler Vane Orsik and the Gorran Grumm, the latter who became his best friend. Orsik owned the Wayfarer, a fast ship with which Dorn made the Slagpit Run in just twelve light-hours and won from Vane in a game of vantage.

chunks.title: Dorn Halek
chunks.text: With only Grumm remaining at his side, as his trusted copilot who swore a life debt to the Kestran smuggler, Dorn Halek embarked on a smuggling career under the employ of Ollag the Vast, a notorious gangster and crime lord of Sorrhas. After ditching a shipment of spice to avoid trouble with the Dominion, Halek owed a great deal of money to Ollag, who then placed a bounty on the smuggler's head, as a result. His fortune seemed to have changed when Dorn and Grumm were hired to charter Kael Velmor, Sorel Vand, and the automatons AR-7 and SP-9 to Aurelith, avoiding Dominion sentinel troopers who were searching for Kael's automatons. However, as they find Aurelith destroyed by the Dominion's new superweapon, the Void Core, Halek became caught up in the uprising against the Dominion, rescuing Princess Lyra Voss, delivering the stolen Void Core plans to the hidden Coalition base on Karrow IV, and saved Kael from the Voidsworn Lord Xarn Velgor in the Battle of Karrow, allowing Velmor to destroy the Void Core. Halek fought with the Uprising for a number of years afterward, taking part in numerous operations and battles against the Dominion.

chunks.title: Dorn Halek
chunks.text:
After the Battle of Frostmarch, Halek sought refuge with Voss—with whom he had fallen in love—Grumm, and SP-9 on Skyhold, which was operated by his old friend Vane Orsik. There, they were captured by Xarn Velgor as part of a trap to bait Velmor to the city. Halek was frozen in stasis amalgam and taken to Ollag's Keep on Sorrhas by the bounty hunter Rhen Kord, where he remained encased in stasis amalgam for months until he was rescued by his friends. After returning to the Coalition fleet, Halek was promoted to the rank of general and was given command of the Pathfinders, a special forces squad, for the Battle of Sylvaneth. Halek led the Pathfinders to Sylvaneth, where he, Voss, Grumm, and the special forces team, with the help of the native Bramblekin, destroyed the aegis generator protecting the second Void Core that was being constructed in orbit. Their actions allowed the Coalition fleet to destroy the superweapon.

The Battle of Sylvaneth, which saw the deaths of Sovereign Sev Kaelith and Xarn Velgor, allowed the Uprising to form the New Concord. In the early days after Sylvaneth, Halek continued to lead the Pathfinders against the Dominion. He married Voss, and the two had a son, Orin Halek. The boy struggled with the null side of the Synth Flux—like his mother, who was the daughter of Xarn Velgor and twin sister of Kael Velmor, Orin was Flux-sensitive—so Voss sent him to be trained as a Fluxadept by Velmor. Orin was seduced to the null side by Moloch, Supreme Leader of the Iron Ascendancy, resulting in the destruction of Velmor's attempt to rebuild the Flux Order.

chunks.title: Dorn Halek
chunks.text: Having lost their son, Halek left and returned to smuggling, and even lost the Wayfarer to numerous thieves. He continued to smuggle until he was brought back into the fight by a scavenger named Nara and a defected Iron Ascendancy sentinel trooper named Cael, who carried with them a automaton, ORB-4, that had part of a map to Velmor's location. Halek, who retrieved the Wayfarer from Nara and Cael, returned to Voss, who led the Remnant against the Iron Ascendancy, and fought in the battle to destroy the Iron Ascendancy superweapon known as Nullpoint Station. During the battle, Halek saw his son, who had taken the name Voidsworn Draven, and tried to convince him to return home. Instead, Draven stabbed his father with his fluxblade. Mortally wounded, Halek fell to his death in the bowels of the Nullpoint weapon. However, Halek's heroic memory survived and his spirit remained alive and appeared in a Flux vision a year later to convince Draven to abandon the null side and defeat the resurrected Kaelith Rau, after a duel on the remains of the second Void Core between Nara and Draven, being enough for Orin Halek to return and eventually sacrifice his own life to help Nara end Rau and the Voidsworn for good.

chunks.title: Dorn Halek
chunks.heading: Childhood
chunks.text:
Dorn was born in a rough-and-tumble favela on the planet Kestrel during the waning years of the Aetherium Concord in 32 BKC. Sometime after he became famous, it would be rumored by a Vellin bounty hunter that Dorn was actually a descendant of the Prince-Admiral Jorun Halek, a member of the ancient Kestran royalty. During his formative years, his father Korv worked in the Kestran Engineering Corporation shipyards, building vessels such as VX-900 light freighters until he was laid off. Halek's father wished he could leave Kestrel on such a ship, but was never able to afford to. According to Dorn, he was never close with his father. At one point his father brought him to the freighter factory where he worked and pointed out to the young Dorn that the ships being built there were his contributions to the galaxy, but that they ultimately didn't matter. He advised him that he wasn't meant to build ships, but rather to fly the ships. Eventually, his father abandoned him. At some point he met the Chanter Hovan.



Around 24 BKC, Dorn joined the Pale Coils criminal gang as a street rat. Here, Dorn met fellow street rat Sira. Despite being in service to the gang, Dorn showed considerable defiance towards them and their methods. One day, he intervened as a smaller child was attacked by a group of bullies, which led to Dorn getting beaten as well. Afterwards, Sira asked Dorn why he helped the child despite not getting anything in return. Dorn answered that while that might be how the galaxy works, it did not always have to be that way.

chunks.title: Dorn Halek
chunks.heading: Working for the Pale Coils
chunks.text:
When Dorn was about the age of eighteen, Dorn and Sira were vying for the position of Head within the Pale Coils. During their respective assignments, Dorn and Sira both failed to deliver as promised, leading them to be hunted down by factions such as the Pale Coils, the Vorn Syndicate, as well as the Dominion. Dorn had acquired a data shard with plans for a aegis generator that was desired by all the factions. Dorn and Sira had no choice but to partner up to find a resolution to their problems. Eventually, Sira became Head thanks to Dorn's recommendation to Lady Vessa. As they later ate together, Dorn asked if he and Sira were on their first date. Sira denied it, but acknowledged the possibility that it could happen someday. Sometime later, Dorn and Sira began a romantic relationship.

chunks.title: Fluxadept
chunks.text: A Fluxadept, formerly called a Lord Fluxadept and sometimes colloquially referred to as a space wizard, was a member of the Flux Order, an ancient order of protectors united by their ability to harness the power of the Synth Flux. Adhering to a doctrine that followed the lumen side of the Synth Flux and aimed at listening to the Will of the Cosmic Flux, the Fluxadept aspired to preserve life while attaining a state of inner tranquility through calmness and meditation to not allow their judgement to be clouded by emotions affiliated with the null side of the Synth Flux, such as anger and hatred. Fluxadept philosophy encouraged a Fluxadept to use their abilities only in self-defense or in the defense of others, avoiding selfishness and personal attachments. To that end, a Fluxadept's only possession was their fluxblade, a symbol of their role as guardians of peace and justice.

chunks.title: Fluxadept
chunks.text: Before the time of the Vanguard Dominion, Fluxadept worked with the Aetherium Concord with a commitment to freedom and democracy. The Fluxadept and the Concord's ideals brought them into conflict with an order of null side wielders known as the Voidsworn, who sought power and dominion over the galaxy. Emerging victorious from their wars with the ancient Voidsworn and believing them to extinct, the Fluxadept carried on in their duty as peacekeepers for over a millennium until the advent of the Vat Wars twenty-two years before the Karrow Concord. Faced with a pan-reach War between the Concord and League of Free Systems, the Fluxadept adopted the mantle of generals and soldiers in the Concord Host. After three years of conflict, the Fluxadept discovered that the Voidsworn had secretly survived following the Rule of Two and had engineered the war to bring themselves to power. However, just before the Voidsworn were defeated, the Fluxadept were betrayed by one of their own—the Foretold One Aran Velmor, who had been seduced to the null side and anointed Xarn Velgor by the Voidsworn Lord Kaelith Rau. Using the Fluxadept's own vat soldiers to initiate a systematic purge of the Flux Order, the Lords of the Voidsworn all but eradicated the Fluxadept in one fell swoop, reducing the order from thousands of Fluxadept Knights guarding the galaxy, to a handful of survivors cast into exile and hunted down across the galaxy.

chunks.title: Fluxadept
chunks.text: The Voidsworn ruled the galaxy through the Dominion for a generation, but did not succeed in completely wiping out the Flux Order. As a result, young individuals such as Ezan Hale and Kael Velmor were, in turn, trained as new Fluxadept by surviving Fluxadept Knights such as Kanan Dros and Flux Master Sorel Vand and Grand Master Ordmund. Velmor, the son of Velgor, was given the mandate of passing on to a new generation of Fluxadept the lessons he had learned from his master Ordmund on the latter's death bed. Shortly afterward, Velmor succeeded in redeeming his father, who sacrificed himself to save his son by killing his Voidsworn Master, Sovereign Rau, thereby destroying the Voidsworn and fulfilling the prophecy of the Foretold One.

chunks.title: Fluxadept
chunks.text: During the era of the New Concord, Velmor worked to rebuild the Flux Order by training a dozen apprentices, including his young but powerful nephew, Orin Halek. Halek later fell to the null side and destroyed Velmor's training temple, also killing its students. He became known as Voidsworn Draven, master of the Knights of Draven, before abandoning them to become the apprentice of Supreme Leader Moloch and joining the Iron Ascendancy as a warlord. As the Iron Ascendancy rose to power, Draven and Moloch sought to destroy Velmor, who, in self-exile, briefly trained a scavenger from Ashfall named Nara in the ways of the Fluxadept until he sacrificed himself to save the Remnant, after which time Velmor's sister, Lyra Voss, continued Nara's training. When a reborn Kaelith Rau—secretly also Nara's grandfather—revealed himself to the galaxy, Orin Halek, the opposite in a dyad in the Synth Flux with Nara, was redeemed, and Nara sacrificed herself to destroy the phantom Voidsworn Lord, preventing the rebirth of the Voidsworn. Nara was saved from death by Halek, who gave his life for hers, allowing the Fluxadept to live on.

chunks.title: Fluxadept
chunks.heading: Philosophy
chunks.text: The Fluxadept Knights focused on calmness and peace to channel their powers in the Synth Flux, using the lumen side of the Synth Flux to serve in the capacity of guardians of peace and justice in the galaxy. Even so, the Fluxadept sought to preserve balance in the Synth Flux; the ancient prophecy of the Foretold One foretold of a being who would restore balance to the Synth Flux by destroying the Voidsworn. In combat, whereas an enemy may grow impatient and rely on their overwhelming strength, a Fluxadept would meditate and find serenity in their mind to focus. A Fluxadept used the Synth Flux for defense and knowledge rather than use it to gain power over others. Their chosen weapon the fluxblade, a weapon with limitations, likewise symbolized the care a Fluxadept took wielding their gifts and that when a Fluxadept fights it is with intention and precision, ending conflict while injuring no more, or taking no more life, than the fluxblade's wielder chooses. Always supposed to put the needs of others before their own, a Fluxadept was supposed to be selfless and work to save others above themselves. Like all people, Fluxadept were imperfect and always needed to strive to better themselves, meaning it was impossible to be a "perfect Fluxadept."

chunks.title: Fluxadept
chunks.heading: Philosophy
chunks.text:
Because of their ability in the Synth Flux, a Fluxadept, even if they lacked a physical weapon, was never defenseless, and some Fluxadept were capable of appearing after death as Flux spirits. The Fluxadept considered themselves instruments of the Synth Flux, and during the time of the Aetherium Concord, peacekeepers instead of soldiers. Striving to be majestic yet simple, knowledge, the Synth Flux, and self-discipline were considered the three pillars of Fluxadept strength. Instead of acting for selfish aims, such as securing wealth or power, the Fluxadept focused their pursuits on learning, reaching enlightenment, helping others in a just fashion, and finding balance. The Fluxadept believed that—no matter one's physical appearance—everyone was internally made up of light. Some individuals, such as Joss, Pikka Adren and even Order member Bell Zettifar, sometimes jokingly called the Fluxadept "space wizards."

Through the Flux Order all Fluxadept belonged to, a Fluxadept was connected to the entire galaxy. As part of the Order, a single Fluxadept had the advantage of a structured community to rely on and gain confidence from. In the opinion of Initiate Matthea Cathley, the Fluxadept were better as a group than on their own. Similarly, Flux Knight Sorel Vand thought of the Order as something that proved that, in being a Fluxadept, he was part of something bigger than himself. Indeed, the Fluxadept could rely on their Order in tough times, enabling an individual Fluxadept to act in a bold fashion and make large scale choices about spreading light. One enemy of the Fluxadept, Eye of the Hollow Marchion Ro, thus regarded the Flux Order as something the Fluxadept would tap into, much like their ability to tap into the Synth Flux itself.

chunks.title: Fluxadept
chunks.heading: Philosophy
chunks.text:
The life of a Fluxadept was full of hardships. Training to become a Fluxadept was difficult, according to Flux Master Aldric Fen, and those who succeeded were faced with a hard life ahead. Adherence to the Fluxadept way required a disciplined mind and a strong sense of commitment, and it was considered unbecoming of a Fluxadept to seek adventure or excitement. The Flux Code therefore regulated the lives of individual Fluxadept, their actions and beliefs, and the policies of the Flux Order. While the Code permitted compassion, attachment and possession were forbidden to the Fluxadept. The Fluxadept believed that attachment led to jealousy, and greed in turn, and ultimately the fear of loss, which was a pathway to the null side of the Synth Flux. Through the Synth Flux, the Fluxadept hoped to direct themselves through their passions, instead of acting in an impulsive manner. Forgoing attachment was also considered essential to a Fluxadept's progress in mastering their Flux powers, as their training could last from years to a lifetime. Despite the importance of non-attachment in the Fluxadept vow, there was disagreement on what that specifically meant.

_(excerpt truncated)_

chunks.title: Fluxblade
chunks.text: The fluxblade, also referred to as a laser sword by those who were unfamiliar with it, was a weapon usually used by the Fluxadept, Voidsworn, and other Flux-sensitives. Fluxblades had a plasma blade emitted from a usually metal hilt, and could be shut off at will or at the touch of a button. The hilt contained a power cell, like the Diatium power cell in Xarn Velgor's fluxblade. It also contained a resonance crystal which had been attuned to the Synth Flux by a Fluxadept, and which amplified the energy from the power cell to create the plasma beam, as well as containing it within a blade-like field. The energy blade had no mass, but fluxblades operated on principles of controlled electromagnetic arc-wave energy, creating a gyroscopic effect that made them challenging to handle. It was a weapon that required skill and training, and was greatly enhanced when used in conjunction with the Synth Flux. Though also used by the Voidsworn, the fluxblade was synonymous with the Fluxadept, with some in the galaxy believing only Fluxadept could use fluxblades.

chunks.title: Fluxblade
chunks.text:
Fluxblades were generally used for both offense and defense. A fluxblade could cut through virtually anything, from flesh to blast doors. The only ways to block the incoming attack of a fluxblade was with a weapon made with material that conducted energy, such as an electrostaff and a Z6 riot control baton, resistant metals like ironsong and cortosis, another fluxblade or an ichor sword. When used defensively, a Flux-sensitive could deflect pulser bolts with a fluxblade, and with skill, could even reflect the shots back toward the shooter or some other target. Experienced Fluxadept could even employ their fluxblades to absorb Flux lightning. Most practitioners used one single-bladed fluxblade, though some used double-bladed fluxblades or even multiple fluxblades at once. Despite lacking Flux-sensitivity, the cyborg Warlord Sketh was capable of wielding four fluxblades at once thanks to his advanced mechanical body and enhanced cybernetic brain.

Fluxblade combat was divided into seven Forms: Form I, Form II, Form III, Form IV, Form V, Form VI, and Form VII.



Sounding like no other weapon in the galaxy, fluxblades were used thousands of years before the age of the Aetherium Concord, seeing use in the Great Scourge of Nullmark. They were also used in the Battles of Rashfond and the Peacekeeping of Parliock, The proto-saber was an ancient type of prototype fluxblade.

chunks.title: Fluxblade
chunks.heading: Concord Era
chunks.text: During the history of the Flux Order, the fluxblade was considered to be the Fluxadept's only true ally in battle. As Master Sorel Vand once declared to his Initiate Aran Velmor in the days of the late Concord, the fluxblade was a Fluxadept's life. Fluxadept saw the fluxblade as a symbol of the care that they would wield using their gifts given by the Synth Flux, and also served as a message to their opponents: mastering the fluxblade required great skill and training. The choice of the saber was also the symbol of their role and duty as protectors, not destroyers, and the fact that the Fluxadept did not seek power and only sought to stand tall against darkness. Still, Fluxadept knew they would need to be more than their fluxblades.

chunks.title: Fluxblade
chunks.heading: Concord Era
chunks.text: When Initiate Enya Keen lost her fluxblade during a mission to Dalna, her master, Char-Ryl-Roy, reminded her that she would need to act as a Fluxadept without the weapon. While finding a resonance crystal was still a sacred part of a Fluxadept's duty and Keen felt like losing her fluxblade would feel like losing part of herself, she willingly gave away the crystal if it meant finding more about the Path of the Open Hand and its plans. During the sabotage of the Steady Wing in 232 BKC, Initiate Imri Cantaros dealt with emotional struggles that lead to his fluxblade beam turning transparent and weak. Fluxblades took on a more prominent role in galactic affairs as the Vat Wars came to pass. Fluxadept, previously peacekeepers, became Fluxadept Generals of the Concord Host, and thus began using their fluxblades more often than they had in their role of peacekeeping. Despite his lack of Flux-sensitivity and formal Flux training, Warlord Sketh received instruction in fluxblade combat from Magister Volen. His cybernetic arms could split into four separate appendages, allowing him to wield up to four fluxblades simultaneously. Sketh frequently hunted Fluxadept individually, claiming their fluxblades as trophies. By the end of the Vat Wars, Sketh had amassed a collection of nearly a hundred fluxblades, many reportedly taken from Fluxadept he had captured or killed, including Flux Master Neebo and the newly knighted Nahdar Vebb.

chunks.title: Fluxblade
chunks.heading: General perception
chunks.text:
For the majority of the Dominion's reign, the only fluxblades that were prominently used were those of the Voidsworn Lord and Dominion enforcer Xarn Velgor and the Seekers who served him, with the Seekers eventually vanishing alongside the Fluxadept they had hunted. For a time, Velgor had remained largely hidden from the galaxy, leaving the Seekers to—as noted by the later historian Beaumont Kin—possibly be more well-known fluxblade wielders. Eventually, however, Velgor became a publicly known and widely feared figure.

The majority of the Flux Order, meanwhile, had been reduced to scattered remnants in hiding across the galaxy who largely kept their fluxblades hidden, lest they draw Dominion attention. The Voidsworn Lord Kaelith Rau, as the Sovereign of the galaxy, largely ruled from a distance and was unable to use his own fluxblades in combat often. Velgor wielded a dual-phase fluxblade, a design of an older, more dangerous generation. With the disappearance of the Seekers and through his own public emergence over the course of the Dominion Era, Velgor became the primary example of someone in the galaxy who fought with a fluxblade.

However, other than Velgor as he became an increasingly known figure, the general public saw little of fluxblades during the Dominion Era. Indeed, surviving Flux Master Sorel Vand regarded the fluxblade as a past weapon created in "a more civilized age." Delegate Daho Sejan had hope that general knowledge of the fluxblade would die off in due time, leaving only Dominion narratives about the fall of the Fluxadept to be told whenever a child asked what it was. During the Reach War, Domina Tagge of the Tagge Corporation tried to recreate the fluxblade through the Tagge protoblade.

chunks.title: Fluxblade
chunks.heading: Survival of the Fluxadept
chunks.text:
All the same, there were still fluxblades used by Fluxadept survivors and those they trained, like Sorel Vand, Kael Velmor, Cere Mahl, Cal Dune, Tensu Run, Ilyra Shen, Kanan Dros, and Ezan Hale. While Vand, for a period, kept his fluxblade absolutely hidden, he was inspired to take back up his weapon and found his hope for the future rekindled through his experiences with the young Kael Velmor and Lyra Voss, resulting in him effectively using his weapon against Velgor during a duel on a barren moon in 9 BKC. Meanwhile, Dune had been using his fluxblade as part of his personal crusade against the Dominion, through which he became a well-known criminal. All the while in the Great Flux Purge, numerous surviving Fluxadept were wiped out by Velgor and his Seekers.

In 1 BKC, Vand and Velgor would engage in a final duel aboard the VC-1 Orbital Station, in which Vand allowed himself to be cut down so as to give Kael Velmor, Lyra Voss, and his other allies a chance to escape aboard the freighter Wayfarer. Before his death, Vand had formally begun Velmor's Flux training while withholding the truth from him that Velgor was his own father, Aran Velmor. Instead telling Kael that Velgor had murdered his father, Vand presented the young Velmor with his father's fluxblade as a gift, with Velmor using the blade during his early training. During the assault on Cymoon in 0 AKC, shortly after Vand's death, Velmor attempted to duel Velgor for the first time, although he did not have the training necessary to stand against the Voidsworn Lord. Velgor, however, was surprised to see Velmor was using his own past fluxblade, which led to Velgor's investigation into the young man's identity.
