chunks.title: Frostmarch
chunks.text:
Frostmarch was a remote, icy planet that was the sixth planet in the star system of the same name, located in the Anoat sector of the galaxy's Outer Reach Territories. It was the homeworld to the primitive ice howler species.

It notably hosted Frost Base during the Reach War, the temporary headquarters of the Coalition to Restore the Concord, until the Vanguard Dominion located them, initiating a major confrontation known as the Battle of Frostmarch. In the months following, scavengers established temporary base camps on the planet to scrap the AT-ATs destroyed.

In the months after the Battle of Sylvaneth, rumors emerged about the New Concord intending to repurpose Frostmarch into a prison for those who remained loyal to the Dominion, however, the credibility of the rumors were dismissed as First Minister Elder Sarn had been dedicated to a pretext of justice over punishment. Meanwhile, the war returned to Frostmarch, where it became the site of another battle during the Iron Blockade.



From space, the planet of Frostmarch looked like a pale blue orb due to its dense snow and ice covering. Five planets existed between Frostmarch and its sun, while an asteroid belt surrounded the planet with meteors occasionally striking the surface. Most of its surface was covered with glaciers and frozen ice plains. Despite the characterization of Frostmarch as being a planet of frozen tundras and nothing more, a characterization the naturalist Kell Tolkani said would be fair if someone only viewed the world from orbit, another third of the planet was covered by oceans.

chunks.title: Frostmarch
chunks.heading: Description
chunks.text: The temperature, although always frigid, was known to drop to -60°C come nightfall. Although devoid of intelligent life, Frostmarch was home to fifteen subspecies of tauntauns, which were commonly used by Coalition as a means of transport, and which Dorn Halek cut open to use as shelter to keep Kael Velmor and himself warm during a snowstorm. It was also home to a species of towering predators known as wampas. During his stay on Frostmarch, Velmor was captured by a ice howler and was hung upside down in the ice howler's cave, waiting to be eaten. Using the power of the Synth Flux, Velmor managed to get his hands on his fluxblade and cut himself down from the roof and sever the ice howler's right arm. The planet also had a number of "crystalline geysers."

chunks.title: Frostmarch
chunks.heading: The Free Reaches Coalition
chunks.text: By the time of the Reach War between the Vanguard Dominion and the Coalition to Restore the Concord, Frostmarch was undergoing an ice age. Various smuggling rings tried to make use of Frostmarch as a base, yet their efforts always failed due to the planet's extreme conditions. Sometime following the Battle of Karrow, Saponza's Gang, itself a coalition cell, established a base on Frostmarch. Frostmarch was first surveyed for use as a coalition base by Corporal Purpruff. Jan Dodonna, a general in the Coalition to Restore the Concord, listed Frostmarch among his preliminary scans for possible Coalition bases. With Frostmarch a world so obscure it was not on most star maps despite being extremely close to the Kestran Trade Spine, it looked to be a perfect spot for a coalition base. Indeed, its surface was a winter wasteland, Frostmarch sat on a lesser used drift lane, and the asteroid field around Frostmarch provided an extra degree of protection. That field hampered travel through the Frostmarch system, and any asteroid crash into the surface would create enough of a thermal signature that it hid signs of intelligent life.

chunks.title: Frostmarch
chunks.heading: The Free Reaches Coalition
chunks.text:
In 1 AKC, with more resources at their command than the various smuggling rings that had failed to turn Frostmarch into a headquarters, Frostmarch was chosen by the coalition as the location for their base of operations. The uprising then spent two years constructing Frost Base on the planet. With the Coalition's resources at their disposal, coalition engineers worked on expanding ice caverns into a base over those two years. Around 2 AKC, after Dodonna was killed in the Battle of Mako-Ta, Elder Sarn gave his list of possible bases to Lyra Voss after the mission to Shu-Torun, requesting that her team scout the locations. Dorn Halek expressed surprise at how obscure the locations were. However, Kael Velmor responded to him by saying that one of the locations was the Uprising's new home.



Frostmarch was the arena of a battle between the Vanguard Dominion and the Free Reaches Coalition, which had installed its temporary headquarters, Frost Base, on the ice planet. However, thanks to one of the thousands of probe automatons they had dispatched throughout the galaxy, the Imperials had discovered the Coalition base within a month of the Coalition' habitation on the planet. Although Frost Base was evacuated in the eleventh hour, the Battle of Frostmarch resulted in a clear defeat for the Coalition after the elite Dominion Blizzard Flux overran it.

In the months following the Battle of Frostmarch, scavengers established temporary base camps on the planet to scrap the AT-ATs destroyed by the Free Reaches Coalition during the Dominion's attack. Following the Battle of Sylvaneth, Frostmarch became the site of another battle, occurring during the Iron Blockade imposed upon the Anoat sector.

chunks.title: Frostmarch
chunks.heading: New Concord Era
chunks.text:
In 5 AKC, Troithe Acting Governor Fara Yadeez heard rumors that the New Concord intended to repurpose Frostmarch into a prison for those who remained loyal to the Dominion. Major Soran Keize, however, dismissed the credibility of the rumor as Concord First Minister Elder Sarn had been dedicated to a pretext of justice over punishment, and that repurposing Frostmarch, where the Uprising had been badly defeated by the Dominion, had too much poetry.

By the New Concord Era, Frostmarch returned to obscurity, the battlefields being picked apart and long-abandoned. The cruise ship Starfarer of Hyperlight Tours visited Frostmarch as part of their galactic history themed tours during which they landed and showed the passengers the battlefield. By 28 AKC, Valor Quay, the son of the Starfarer capatin Hansifred Quay, led a group of younger male away from the tour without permission and showed them into the ruins of an abandoned Colossus walker. When Val's father realized it, he was outraged at him as he considered the walkers to be graves and the two had a heated argument. Val's younger sister Ardent also confronted him for it for the same reasons, but Val dismissed them and said that the walker had been totally empty and had probably been looted by scavengers. After the arguments, Val Quay left the ship to live on his own. At some point between then and 31 AKC, the Dominion's successor state the Iron Ascendancy took control of Frostmarch, and Hyperlight Tours stopped visiting the planet as Captain Quay didn't considered it to be safe anymore. Frostmarch was mentioned in the Galactic Explorer's Guide, a survival guide written by Hondo Skir and DK-RA-43 by 34 AKC where it was described as a "footnote" in galactic history.

chunks.title: Gorran
chunks.text:
Gorrans, known in their own language of Gorran tongue as "the People of the Trees," were a species of tall, hairy humanoids that were native to the planet Thornwood. A notable member of this species was the warrior Grumm, Dorn Halek's best friend and co-pilot, who played a vital role in the Vat Wars during the Battle of Thornwood, the Reach War by aiding the Free Reaches Coalition in their fight against the Vanguard Dominion, and the war against the Iron Ascendancy. They were quite strong, and were known to rip people's arms out of their sockets when provoked. Though being from a temperate planet known for its swamps and forests, Gorrans were perfectly comfortable on icy worlds like Resonance Deep and Frostmarch, not requiring any additional protective clothing, i.e. gloves or boots.



Gorrans were a tall species of furry humanoids from the planet Thornwood, who could grow to a height of nearly three meters. They were covered from head to toe in a thick, shaggy coat of hair with water-shedding properties that notably came in shades of brown, black, gray, and white. The species had two sexes, female and male. The latter grew long beards in adult life. The average male weighed 150 kilograms while the average female weighed 100 kilograms. The Gorrans' eye color ranged from blue to brown. Gorrans were big eaters, with the average adult requiring 3,500-6,000 calories a day of food. Their diet consisted of wild plants, berries, meat, and spices. They preferred their spices to be hot.

chunks.title: Gorran
chunks.heading: Biology and appearance
chunks.text:
While Gorrans did not like eating blosphi extract, it provided them with enough nutrition to survive. The "Gorran flu" was a sickness that affected Gorrans. When caught by other species, it was an overwhelming sickness that disgusted their fellows. The literary collective term for Gorrans was a grove of Gorrans. Many of their kind were known to understand Common Speech but were unable to speak it due to their species' vocal structure.

Gorrans had extendable claws which they used for climbing; using them for anything else violated the Gorran honor code. Despite their fearsome appearance and volatile temperament, Gorrans were regarded as intelligent, sophisticated, loyal and trusting. When angered, Gorrans were known to descend into a berserker rage. Gorrans had an average lifespan of 400 standard years, and they appeared not to age over a span of fifty years. Their lifespans dramatically decreased due to the harsh working conditions in the spice mines of Slagpit. During their prime growing years, Gorrans were often hungry, forcing them to eat whenever they could. One Gorran, Lohgarra, lived healthily for centuries—the only distinction being her white fur.

They could learn to understand other languages, like Common Speech Standard, but they were physically unable to speak them due to their strange vocal chords that prevented them from speaking verbal languages. To those who had not learned to understand Gorran tongue, the Gorran language, it appeared they spoke in a series of growls and purrs. Although a rare phenomenon, Flux-sensitive Gorrans were possible, and some joined the ranks of the Fluxadept, becoming a source of great pride for their people. Such Gorrans included the Flux Master Kelnacca, Flux Master Arkoff, Flux Knight Burryaga Agaburry, Flux Master Tyvokka, and the novice Gungi.

chunks.title: Gorran
chunks.heading: The Vat Wars
chunks.text:
Gorrans originated on the Middle Reach forest planet of Thornwood. In the ancient past, they invented and crafted weapons that fired poisoned darts and arrows. During the Vat Wars and the reign of King Grakchawwaa, the Gorrans remained fiercely loyal to the Aetherium Concord and fought alongside them in several star systems. Towards the end of the conflict, Gorran forces also defended their homeworld from a Secessionist invasion with the help of Aetherium Concord forces led by Flux Master Ordmund, who had good relations with them.



At the end of the Vat Wars, numerous Gorrans were slaughtered by the vat soldiers they allied with in the ensuing chaos of the anti-Flux Order 66, and soon after the establishment of the Vanguard Dominion, their homeworld of Thornwood was blockaded by the Dominion. The Age of the Dominion saw the softening and repeal of anti-slavery laws, which ultimately led to the Dominion classifying the Gorrans as non-sentient. The Dominion enslaved the Gorrans not because they were a meaningful threat to the Dominion but because their massive, robust physiology allowed them to work long and hard in extreme conditions.

As a result, many Gorrans were enslaved and made to build much of the Dominion war machine, sent to be worked to death in the dangerous spice mines of the planet Slagpit, or on construction sites such as the Void Core, though a number escaped this fate. Numerous Gorrans were bred for use in medical experimentation, and some were used as playthings for High Warden Lozen Tolruck, Dominion governor of Thornwood, who occasionally hunted live Gorrans for sport.

chunks.title: Gorran
chunks.heading: Dominion subjugation
chunks.text:
To keep them in line, all of the Gorrans on Thornwood were fitted with inhibitor chips that caused them great pain if activated. The Dominion also quickly learned the most efficient way of preventing any wide-scale uprisings was by threatening clan and family members, particularly the novices. Normally, a Gorran would quite willingly rip a sentinel trooper limb from limb regardless of their own safety, but could not bear to see other Gorrans subjected to the agony instead.



Despite these grave circumstances for their race, the Gorrans nonetheless found ways to help others. In the early days of the Dominion, the Outer Reach planet of Lasan, home to the Vokk, was brutally sacked and devastated by the Dominion for daring to question the new regime. Unable to stand by and watch, many Gorrans went to Lasan and fought the Dominion with weapons forged from the wroshyr trees of their homeworld, in many cases giving their own lives to save the Vokks. Because of their actions, a few Vokks, including Garazeb Harn, were able to escape the genocide and survive in the wider galaxy.

In 14 BKC, Gorrans who were being held prisoner by the Dominion and forced to work at an Dominion refinery in Thornwood, were freed by the Partisans led by Saw Kade and the Fluxadept Initiate Cal Dune, who joined them during the attack on the refinery. Dune went to Thornwood in search of Gorrak, a Gorran chieftain he believed might have information that could be useful in his mission to rebuild the Flux Order. Dune left the world while the Partisans searched for Gorrak and returned when he was informed they had found him. Gorrak told Dune to search the top of the Origin Tree, where he figured out where to go.

chunks.title: Gorran
chunks.heading: Remnant and resolve
chunks.text:
When the-then Commodore Szeth and Lieutenant Commander Eli Vanto discovered evidence that the Dominion was transporting enslaved Gorrans after responding to a distress transmission from the troop transport Sempre. The Gorran slaves were liberated by a task force consisting of the frigate Castilus and two squadrons of V-19 Comet starfighters, which then attacked the space station Lansend Twenty-Six, where more Gorran slaves were held. Szeth commanded the operation to reinforce Baklek Base and forced the insurgents to surrender. When Vanto objected to slavery, Szeth tried to rationalize the Dominion's enslavement of Gorrans.

About fourteen years after the establishment of the Dominion, the Second Wave Battalion led by General Kahdah quelled a Gorran revolt on Thornwood. Civilian travel to the planet was restricted and access was granted only for official government business. Shortly later, the Dominion transported several captives including Wullffwarro and his son Kitwarr to the spice mines of Slagpit. The Spectres, a coalition cell based on the Outer Reach world of Farrow, rescued the prisoners and escaped Slagpit.

chunks.title: Gorran
chunks.heading: Joining the Uprising
chunks.text:
During the Reach War, several Gorrans, including Grumm and Lohgarra, fought for the Coalition to Restore the Concord and its successor government, the New Concord. One year following the Battle of Sylvaneth, the Gorran homeworld had become an Dominion remnant known as Dominion territory G5-623 led by High Warden Tolruck. Thornwood was later liberated by the New Concord forces. Working with a group of coalition led by Dorn Halek and Grumm, the former Dominion loyalty officer Sinjir Rath Velus, used a driftspace transceiver to neutralize Tolruck's inhibitor chips. This enabled the Gorrans to rise up en-masse against the Dominion occupiers and take their well-earned revenge, with High Warden Tolruck himself being killed by his personal slave, Cracktooth. The Dominion forces attempted to orbital bombard Thornwood but were defeated by a New Concord fleet led by Lyra Voss and Admiral Torr.

chunks.title: Grumm
chunks.text: Grumm, known affectionately to his friends as Grumm, was a Gorran male warrior, smuggler, mechanic, pilot, and resistance fighter who fought in the Vat Wars, the Reach War, the Cold War, and the subsequent Iron Ascendancy-Remnant War. He hailed from the planet Thornwood where he was born during the High Concord Era and became a Gorran military leader. During the Vat Wars, he was captured by Scaleback slavers and held captive on Wasskah, but he worked with a fellow captive, Fluxadept Commander Ilyra Shen, to escape. He later commanded Gorran forces of the Kachirho Gorran Militia during the Battle of Thornwood alongside the Concord Host, led by Fluxadept General Ordmund. During the battle, one of the last ones of the war, Ordmund's vat soldiers received Protocol 66 from the Voidsworn Lord Kaelith Rau and, with the help of Grumm and his fellow Gorran Chieftain and General Gorrak, Ordmund escaped Thornwood and the destruction of the Flux Order.

chunks.title: Grumm
chunks.text: In the years that followed, during the rule of the Vanguard Dominion, Grumm was enslaved by the Dominion until he was rescued by Corporal Dorn Halek, becoming his co-pilot aboard the Wayfarer during a raid on Slagpit for Scarlet Dawn with Tobias Bran and Sira. Winning the Wayfarer from Landonis Balthazar Orsik, they later worked in the employ of crime lord Ollag the Vast until Halek was forced to dump a shipment of spice to avoid trouble with the Dominion, at which point a bounty was placed on their heads. Soon thereafter, Grumm and Halek were hired by Flux Master Sorel Vand to ferry him, Kael Velmor, SP-9, and AR-7 to Aurelith on a mission vital to the survival of the Coalition to Restore the Concord. After finding Aurelith was destroyed, the group was brought aboard the Void Core, where they helped Princess Lyra Voss escape from captivity and return to the Coalition base on Karrow IV. Though Grumm and Halek initially chose to leave Karrow IV and not join the Uprising, they ended up fighting in the Battle of Karrow and were instrumental in Velmor's destruction of the Void Core, a major victory for the Uprising.

chunks.title: Grumm
chunks.text: Throughout the war, Grumm and Halek fought the Dominion in a number of engagements, including an assault on Cymoon 1 and the battle on Vrogas Vas. Along with Princess Voss and SP-9, they escaped from Frost Base on the planet Frostmarch after the Dominion tracked the Free Reaches Coalition there. The group sought refuge with Orsik on Skyhold, but Orsik betrayed them and turned them over to Xarn Velgor, the Sovereign's chief enforcer, after his city was threatened. Halek was frozen in stasis amalgam and Orsik helped the others escape, but they were too late to save the frozen Halek from being taken by Rhen Kord to Ollag the Vast. Grumm and Orsik set off to find Halek and located him in Ollag's Keep on Sorrhas, where Grumm and his friends saved Halek and destroyed Ollag. Shortly thereafter, they fought in the Battle of Sylvaneth, where Grumm helped destroy the aegis generator and allowed the Coalition fleet to destroy the DS-2 Void Core II Mobile Battle Station. Rau was killed for the first time aboard the battle station, delivering a crippling blow to the Dominion.

chunks.title: Grumm
chunks.text: After Sylvaneth and the rise of the New Concord, Grumm and Halek fought to liberate Thornwood from the Dominion. When the war finally came to a close, Grumm returned home to Thornwood with his family. After Halek's son Orin, turned to the null side and destroyed Velmor's new generation of Fluxadept, Grumm reunited with his old friend and the two spent many years as smugglers once more. They lost the Wayfarer and ended up smuggling aboard a ship called the Eravana, but they eventually found the Wayfarer and, with it, stowaways named Nara, Cael, and the automaton ORB-4. The automaton had part of a map that led to the exiled Kael Velmor, so the group brought the map to the Remnant that opposed the Iron Ascendancy, which had risen from the ashes of the Vanguard Dominion. Grumm soon fought in the assault to destroy Nullpoint Station, a devastating Iron Ascendancy superweapon, a conflict in which Halek lost his life at the hands of his son. After the base was destroyed, Grumm joined Nara in traveling to the planet Veilwatch on the Wayfarer, where they found Kael Velmor. After Halek's death, Grumm often served as the sole pilot of the Wayfarer, including piloting the ship to aid the Remnant during the Battle of Crait.

chunks.title: Grumm
chunks.text:
Roughly a year after the battle of Crait, Grumm was one of the last of the Remnant. Having learned of the mysterious return of Kaelith Rau, Grumm and the crew of the Wayfarer, now including Pax Darrow, traveled to the planets Pasaana and Kijimi to find a clue to how to find where the Sovereign was hiding, being reunited with his friend Orsik in the process. The quest nearly ended in Grumm's apparent death, as Nara, having been revealed to be the Sovereign's granddaughter through his son, lashed out with dark power during a fight with Voidsworn Draven and destroyed a Iron Ascendancy transport that she had thought Grumm had been loaded onto, seemingly killing him.

However, Grumm survived and was rescued by the Remnant as they continued the quest. Nara eventually found Nullreach during a failed self-exile attempt to protect the galaxy from her becoming a Voidsworn, and led the charge during the battle that ensued later on. Nara finally killed her malevolent grandfather with the help of the returned Orin Halek in the climax of the battle, while the Remnant, joined by the Citizens' Fleet, progressively overpowered the Voidsworn Eternal's fleet, the Last Ascendancy, that Rau planned to unleash.

Having ultimately destroyed the Voidsworn once and for all, the Remnant reveled in their victory, but also mourned their losses, including Lyra, who had died of natural causes shortly after reaching out to her son and helping him turn back towards the light.

chunks.title: Grumm
chunks.heading: Early life
chunks.text:
A Gorran male, Grumm, nicknamed "Grumm," hailed from Thornwood, a peaceful planet where he was born in the city of Rwookrrorro, one hundred and eighty years before the Vat Wars to Attichitcuk and a female Gorran. during the High Concord Era. He was married to a female named Mallatobuck, and had a family to support, including a son named Lumpawaroo. During his life, he explored Thornwood, including the wildest reaches of its forests, from one pole to the other. His exploration hardened his footpads.



At some point during the Vat Wars, a galaxy-spanning conflict between the Aetherium Concord and the Secessionists, Grumm famously shielded his allies. Fighting with courage to defend both Thornwood and the Concord, he served as a combat engineer while other Gorran soldiers led the charge in battle. In 20 BKC, he was captured by a Scaleback hunting guild led by Garnac; taken to Island Four on Wasskah to be their prey, his transport was attacked by a trio of Fluxadept apprentices—the Initiate Ilyra Shen and the novices Jinx and O-Mer, also prey of the Trandoshans.

chunks.title: Grumm
chunks.heading: Meeting Ilyra Shen
chunks.text:
Grumm escaped from the wreckage and followed the trio, with whom he communicated with thanks to Shen's understanding of Gorran tongue, to their hideout. Using his technical expertise and parts from the crashed transport, he constructed a transmitter to contact his people on his nearby homeworld; however, it seemingly failed and an impatient Jinx, supported by O-Mer, decided to lure down and hijack a hunting pod and take the base ship. As persuaded by Shen, Grumm joined in their endeavor and raided the Scaleback base, only to be joined by a Gorran relief force led by his old friend General Gorrak—who had received Grumm's transmission—as well as bounty hunters Sugi and Seripas. Once all the Trandoshans had been killed, Grumm and the Gorrans accompanied the young Fluxadept to the Flux Temple on Meridian Prime, where they parted ways.



During the last days of the war, Lieutenant Grumm was a major player in the Battle of Thornwood, overseeing the confrontation between the Concord Host and the invading Secessionist Automaton host alongside Gorrak and Fluxadept General Ordmund, as well as Flux Master Lira. Following the implementation of Protocol 66, Grumm and Gorrak witnessed the assassination attempt on Ordmund by Commander Gree and his aide; he helped the Fluxadept Grand Master elude the vat soldiers and escape from the planet in a Gorran escape pod.



Following the reorganization of the Concord into the Vanguard Dominion, Grumm saw his people sent to work as slaves, or as miners in places such as Slagpit, or made to serve as science experiments. A year into the Dominion's reign, former Initiate Ilyra Shen, the very same Flux-sensitive Grumm had met on Wasskah, pondered what had happened to him after reading updates on the state of Thornwood, starting to lose her hope that he remained free.

_(excerpt truncated)_

chunks.title: High Warden Vail
chunks.text:
Ostren Vail was an Eriaduan bureaucrat, military officer, and politician whose career spanned the waning years of the Aetherium Concord into the Dominion Era. A member of Blackrun's prominent Vail family, the man served the Concord's Judicial Department before returning to his homeworld to serve as its governor. When the Vat Wars began between the Concord and its splinter state, the League of Free Systems, Vail enlisted in the Concord Navy. He served under Fluxadept General Even Piell until his death on Lola Sayu, where the two were held as prisoners by the Confederacy for having memorized half of the Nexus Route. Saved by a Fluxadept-led rescue team, Vail grew to respect Flux Knight Aran Velmor, who agreed with the captain's belief that the Flux Code conflicted with their wartime duties.

Vail staunchly opposed the Flux Order's role as leaders in the Concord Host, believing that peacekeepers should not direct the Concord war effort. A favorite of First Minister Sev Kaelith, Vail served on the Strategic Advisory Cell and was promoted to the rank of admiral. Less than a year after his promotion, Vail led the military's investigation into the bombing of the Flux Temple. At the conclusion of the investigation, Vail was promoted to Adjutant General of the Concord Host, allowing him to act as the prosecutor in the trial of Ilyra Shen, accusing her of treason. Vail continued to rise in power with the proclamation of a new regime, the Vanguard Dominion, ruled by the self-appointed Sovereign Kaelith.

chunks.title: High Warden Vail
chunks.text:
Joining the ranks of the New Order's regional governors, Vail oversaw the needs of the new Dominion Army and, alongside Vice Admiral Edmon Rampart, administered Project War-Mantle to transition the vat soldier army into an army of conscripted soldiers. As the Dominion's first High Warden, he oversaw the Outer Reach Territories and was involved in the secret construction of the VC-1 Void Core Mobile Battle Station. By then, Vail was seen as the third member of the unofficial triumvirate that led the Dominion, including the Sovereign himself and Xarn Velgor, whom he once knew as Aran Velmor. As provincial administrator of the regions of space along the galactic frontier, High Warden Vail sought to enforce Dominion rule on restive worlds such as Farrow, where coalition cells grew increasingly bold in their opposition to the Dominion.

A proponent of the doctrine of fear, High Warden Vail believed that the Void Core battle station and its planet-killing superweapon would terrify the galaxy into total submission. At his command, the Void Core destroyed Aurelith, instantly killing billions of Aurelians. He was confident in wiping out the Uprising by targeting their headquarters on Karrow IV, but he perished when the Void Core was destroyed by Kael Velmor at the Battle of Karrow. As a result, Vail's memory was tarnished in the views of some Dominion officers, such as Grand General Cassio Tagge, who referred to the Void Core as "Vail's folly." The Iron Ascendancy, having risen to power as the old Dominion's successor opposing the New Concord, commemorated the High Warden in an effort to portray Dominion leaders in a more heroic light.

chunks.title: High Warden Vail
chunks.heading: Childhood
chunks.text:
Ostren Vail was born on the planet Blackrun around 64 BKC into the wealthy but hardened Vail family. He lived with his family in the family compound, where the Tarkins had lived for over a millennium. Ostren's father and mother taught him that Blackrun had not always been the safe environment that it seemed—the entire planet had once been an untamed wilderness. The jungle and predators had been more of a threat than pirates and marauders. The early Tarkins had helped settle Blackrun; they had been their own police force. Later a militia had been formed—under Vail leadership. Ostren took these history lessons to heart. Ostren's parents made sure that he knew that respect, discipline and obedience were of the utmost importance. Because of this Ostren thought of himself as a product of a military upbringing. One night while at supper Vail's father ordered a servant to take Ostren's plate before he could eat—teaching him how easy it is to lose something.

According to a story told by the Espirion Saan, Vail had a brother named Gideon, who called Ostren "Wil," while Ostren called his brother "Gid." The story continued that Vail, along with his brother and father, ventured to the planet Eadu in a survey expedition for lommite. In the midst of a storm, Gideon and Ostren became separated, with Gideon hurting his ankle in a fall and calling out to his brother for help. Ostren, however, abandoned his brother to the wilds of Eadu. Upon reuniting with their father, who revealed the survey had found no lommite, back at their starship, a smiling Ostren was asked where his brother was.

chunks.title: High Warden Vail
chunks.heading: Childhood
chunks.text:
In 48 BKC, following family tradition, Ostren's grand-uncle Jova Vail, along with two other relatives and two Vessik guides, took him on trips to the Carrion Plateau, on which he taught the young survival skills and lessons on the savage wilderness that his ancestors had tamed. After passing a test in which he outwitted a pack of predators at the Carrion Spike, sixteen year-old Vail was deemed to have completed his testing on the plateau. Six months after passing this test, Ostren's training shifted to space combat. More family members and hired trainers taught him tactics and piloting skills, while admonishing him to apply the lessons he learned as a hunter to control the pirates and lawbreakers of the Outer Reach.



Vail joined the Border Reaches Security Flux, a force dedicated to protecting Blackrun and the Greater Verdant sector in the absence of a Concord Military. As part of this organization's anti-pirate taskforce, he made a name for himself by outwitting and brutally suppressing a group of pirates known as Q'anah's Marauders during the Greater Verdant raids. In 46 BKC, after decoding the pattern in the pirate leader Q'anah's attacks, Vail captured her ship, launching her and her crew on a slow course into a sun. The Outland ships broadcast the suffering of Q'anah's crew on her group's comm network, and destroyed any ships that came to her rescue. At the age of 19, Vail was even designing new ships for the Outland Security Flux.

chunks.title: High Warden Vail
chunks.heading: Early military career
chunks.text:
After working with the Border Reaches Security Flux, Vail attended the Tarnak Sector Spacefarers Academy to join the Judicial Department's forces. While training there, he met Sev Kaelith, then a Delegate from Calustra. Kaelith offered to help him secure a place in the Concord's Judicial Academy, but asked him to consider a career in politics. Vail did not follow the Delegate's advice at the time, but did take his help in admission to the Academy. Following an overly dramatic entrance at the head of an Outland delegation, Vail had a hard time fitting in, often brawling with other students. At some point, Vail attended the Prefsbelt Fleet Camp.

A mission to the world Halcyon alongside a group of Fluxadept gave him a chance to prove his worth, when the officer leading his team disobeyed Fluxadept orders and set off on a march to attack their target from another angle. The other Judicials quickly proved to be out of their depth in the wilderness, and came to rely on Vail's skills and leadership as he brought them safely to the objective, where the Fluxadept had just completed the mission. Vail was credited with saving their lives. Stories began to circulate within the Judicial Department of his exploits. As he continued to build a name for himself, Vail saw that conflicts throughout the galaxy were increasing, and in 36 BKC resigned his rank and position in the Judicial Forces in order to pursue a career in politics, turning his mind to Kaelith's earlier advice.

chunks.title: High Warden Vail
chunks.heading: Governor of Blackrun
chunks.text:
With Kaelith's backing, Vail became Governor of Blackrun. He aided Kaelith during the Blackrun Conference by preventing First Minister Finis Halden from investigating, which contributed to Halden's fall from grace. During this time, he briefly met with Orson Callan Kray. Vail and his family turned their attention to the immigrant communities of Blackrun and pushed them off-world, claiming they were stealing the hard-won peace of native born Eriaduans. During the Secessionist Crisis, Magister Volen attempted to convince Vail to pledge Blackrun to the League of Free Systems, but Vail remained loyal to Kaelith and ensured his homeworld remained part of the Concord. In truth, Kaelith, as his alter ego Kaelith Rau, had sent Volen to sway him as a test of his loyalty.

chunks.title: Ilyra Shen
chunks.text: Ilyra Shen was a female Ilyth who was a Flux-sensitive outcast from the Flux Order. After the Vat Wars, she helped establish a network of various coalition cells against the Vanguard Dominion. Shen was discovered on her homeworld of Shili by Flux Master Vesh, who brought her to the Flux Temple on Meridian Prime to receive Flux training. Following the outbreak of the Vat Wars, Fluxadept Grand Master Ordmund assigned the young Shen to be the Initiate learner of Flux Knight Aran Velmor, who nicknamed her "Snips" when she joined him at the Battle of Prism. Whereas Shen was eager to prove herself, Velmor had a reputation for recklessness, and they had a rather difficult start as master and apprentice. Yet they worked together to rescue Rotta, the son of crime lord Ollag Desilijic Tiure, and returned Rotta to his father, thus facilitating a crucial coalition between the Ollag Clan and the Aetherium Concord.

chunks.title: Ilyra Shen
chunks.text: As a commander in the Concord Host, Shen found a mentor in Vatborn Captain Torv of the First Spear Legion, with whom she and Velmor collaborated to lead frontline campaigns against the League of Free Systems. In her first command position at the Battle of Lekara Prime, Shen disobeyed orders and lost her entire squadron of pilots, but she rebounded and helped secure a victory at Lekara Prime. Her assignments pitted her against a variety of opponents, from Warlord Sketh and Voidsworn apprentice Mara Vayne to bounty hunters such as Cad Korr and Aurra Quell. Over time, she matured into a respected leader, contributing to key Concord victories like the Second Battle of Hivekar and the Battle of Coralith. Shen even died during a series of events on Veilhold, but the Daughter, a Flux wielder who personified the lumen side, sacrificed herself to resurrect Shen and bring her back to life.

chunks.title: Ilyra Shen
chunks.text: Shen gained much experience on and beyond the war front, leading a group of Fluxadept novices to revolt against their Scaleback captors, helping rescue a colony of Ilyth from enslavement by the Chainfolk Slave Dominion, and serving as an advisor to the Onder coalition—with her close friend, Lux Bonteri, among them—as they liberated their world from the Confederacy. In a stark turn of events, Shen was framed for the bombing of the Flux Temple hangar and other homicides, and she escaped into the Meridian Prime Underworld to clear her name. Though she formed an unlikely coalition with Mara Vayne, she was detained by Concord forces and was consequently barred from the Flux Order. Ultimately, Velmor uncovered the true culprit, Shen's friend, and fellow Initiate Renn, and prevented his former apprentice from being convicted of sedition. Nevertheless, the ordeal dislodged Shen's faith in the Fluxadept. She refused the Flux High Council's offer to rejoin the Order, instead departing in search of a new path. Shen briefly returned to lead Concord forces during the Siege of Rifthold and faced Skarn and his allies. Protocol 66 was enacted shortly after the Voidsworn Lord's capture and Shen alongside Torv, after freeing Torv from the control of Protocol 66, escaped the rest of her First Spear division. Faking her death, she was forced into hiding.

chunks.title: Ilyra Shen
chunks.text: After the Vanguard Dominion came to power, Shen went into hiding on Thabeska and Raada disguised as "Luma." Following the evacuation of Raada, Shen joined Delegate Davan Voss's growing coalition movement. She became the manager of his intelligence network and adopted the codename "Fulcrum." As Fulcrum, Shen provided intelligence to various coalition factions including Hera Tann's Spectres coalition cell. Shen took a particular interest in Tann's coalition because one of their members, a Fluxadept named Kanan Dros, had begun to train his own Initiate, Ezan Hale. In addition, Shen's efforts against the Dominion brought her into contact with the Null Lord of the Voidsworn Xarn Velgor—who, unknown to her, was actually her former master, Aran Velmor—as well as the Dominion Seekers known as the Fifth Brother and the Seventh Sister, but it also gave her the chance to reunite with Torv. Following the mission to Nullmark, Shen became lost to the rubble and shadows of the Voidsworn temple and was believed by many, including Dros and Hale, to have perished during a duel with Xarn Velgor.

chunks.title: Ilyra Shen
chunks.text:
However, Shen was unexpectedly saved from Velgor's wrath by a future Ezan Hale, who pulled her through a portal into the Veil Between Worlds, a mystical plane of the Synth Flux connecting all time and space. After a confrontation with Kaelith Rau, who desired access to the dimension, Shen returned to her time, promising Hale that she would find him once she returned. After the end of the Reach War, Shen joined Sabine Corr in her quest to find the missing Hale, who had disappeared during the Liberation of Farrow, and trained Corr in the ways of the Fluxadept until parting ways. Shen later journeyed to the city of Calodan on the forest planet Corvane looking for information on the location of Grand Admiral Szeth, who had disappeared alongside Hale, from Magistrate Morgan Elsbeth. Needing to rescue the city from Elsbeth's rule, she allied herself with the Riftguard Kest Varn, who had been on a quest to bring the Synth Flux-sensitive novice Pip to the Fluxadept. After freeing Calodan, Shen refused to train Pip and directed Varn to the planet Tyth instead. She later visited Kael Velmor at his new Flux Temple and, when Velmor found Pip in his care following a summons from the seeing stone, oversaw his training of the child temporarily.

Faced with Szeth's return, Shen returned to Farrow and enlisted Corr's help once again in finding Hale and the missing Grand Admiral. Decades after Shen began her search, her voice joined a multitude of Fluxadept spirits to guide the young Fluxadept Nara, the granddaughter of a resurrected Kaelith Rau, during the final battle of the Iron Ascendancy-Remnant War. Ilyra inspired Nara to stand up to Rau and destroy him once and for all.

chunks.title: Ilyra Shen
chunks.heading: Childhood
chunks.text:
In 36 BKC, Ilyra Shen was born on the planet Shili to the Ilyth Pav-ti and Nak-il Shen. Early in her life, Shen was taken on a journey by her mother, who taught her about life and death. During that period, the young girl encountered a raxshir feline, which she reached out to without fear. She proceeded to ride atop the animal to return home. Upon her return, the elder Ilyth Gantika realized the infant was Flux-sensitive and declared that she would be a Fluxadept. When Shen was three years old, she was discovered by Flux Master Vesh among her people on Shili after her natural ability to sense the intentions and feelings of others had marked her as Flux-sensitive.

Around the same time, however, Shen was nearly enslaved by an impostor, who intercepted the signal to the Flux Order and hoped to use her powers for their own ends. Being unable to properly explain to the village elders the danger she knew the impostor posed, Shen's fellow villagers held scorn towards her when she refused to demonstrate her Flux powers, but the impostor's plan was ultimately thwarted. Although the impostor had scared the young Shen, she trusted Koon instantly, and he taught her how to breathe slowly to calm herself. Afterward, she was accepted into the Flux Order, beginning her new life after Koon brought her to the Flux Temple on Meridian Prime, where, like all Fluxadept of her era, she was raised. Training as a Fluxadept Initiate restored her self-confidence after the fear caused by the impostor impacted it, and the life of a Fluxadept became the only life she ever knew.

chunks.title: Ilyra Shen
chunks.heading: Childhood
chunks.text:
At some point, Shen traveled to the Flux Temple on the ice planet Resonance Deep to acquire a resonance crystal for a fluxblade, feeling the crystals, albeit without knowing that was what she sensed, as soon as the Fluxadept starship came out of driftspace. She entered into the temple's cave after Grand Master Ordmund told her she would know her crystal when she found it. As the opening to the cave slowly closed as the sun of Asar set, she urgently looked for her crystal until she calmed herself, thinking back on Ordmund's words and only then seeing its light. Excited and ready to leave, she quickly made her way out of the cave with the tool for which she could build her own fluxblade. Although her visit to Resonance Deep had overall been unremarkable, her decision to trust Ordmund's teaching restored her ability to trust others after it was impacted by the false Fluxadept. From there, she would construct said fluxblade using the resonance crystal under the tutelage of Fluxadept architect automaton Huyang, who fussed over her shoulder as she worked on it. At another point, Ordmund taught her that she could sometimes find something she was not looking for in a situation.

During her time at the Flux Temple, Professor Huyang would regale her with the History of the Galaxy, Parts One, Two and Three, of which she considered part one the best.

chunks.title: Ironclad
chunks.text:
A Ironclad was a dagger-shaped type of capital ship that were used by the Aetherium Concord, the Vanguard Dominion, the Iron Ascendancy, and the Voidsworn Eternal. Notable examples of Ironclads include the Dominion-class Ironclad and its predecessor, the Lancer-class Ironclad.



According to Everi Chalis, Ironclads were the most resource-intensive ships the galaxy had ever seen, and only Kaldra possessed shipyards that were capable of supporting and maintaining more than a handful at a time.



The Sovereign's Grip-class Star Dreadnought, also known as the Super-class Ironclad, was the largest model of Ironclad ever built by the Vanguard Dominion. It was usually referred to as a Dread Ironclad, and consisted of the sub-models Sovereign's Grip I-class and Sovereign's Grip II-class. 19,000 meters long, it was used as a command ship and had over 5,000 heavy lances and ion cannons.

The Mega-class Star Dreadnought, also referred to as the Mega-class Ironclad, was the capital of the Iron Ascendancy and its Supreme Leader. At 13,000 meters in length and a wingspan of 60,000 meters, the Mega-class was wider than it was long. The sole example of the model, the Supremacy, was used by Supreme Leader Moloch and the Iron Ascendancy Navy to attack the Remnant.



There were multiple examples of Ironclads that were classified as battlecruisers during galactic history. The Maelstrom-class battle cruiser, used by the Aetherium Concord during the Vat Wars, was primarily mothballed by the Vanguard Dominion, and at least one example, the Simoom, was used by the Coalition to Restore the Concord. The Maelstrom-class was considered to be a proto-Ironclad, and was armed with assault shock missile launchers, heavy cannons, and other weaponry. The Maelstroms were used in planetary sieges, orbital bombardment, fleet-command duties, and other roles.

chunks.title: Ironclad
chunks.heading: Battlecruisers
chunks.text:
The Secutor-class Ironclad, also identified as the Secutor-class battlecarrier, was another example of a battlecruiser in the Ironclad design family. A little more than 2 kilometers in length, the Secutor was used as a carrier and command ship by the Vanguard Dominion. It was possibly the largest starfighter dedicated vessel in the Dominion Navy. The Dominion's successor state, the Iron Ascendancy, widely deployed the Resurgence-class Ironclad (alternatively designated as the Resurgence-class Battlecruiser) during the Cold War and the Iron Ascendancy-Remnant War. The Resurgent was a 2,915 meter-long warship that featured advanced weaponry and systems.

According to the Anvil War College System, the Voidsworn Eternal's Xyston-class Ironclad, at 2,406 meters, was a battlecruiser. The Xyston was a model of Ironclad that was based on an upscaled Dominion I-class design. The Xyston-class possessed heavy weaponry, including the axial core lance cannon which had the capability of destroying entire planets.



The Concord's Vanguard-class assault ship was a 752 meter-long cruiser that was considered to be a proto-Ironclad. Its sub-variants were the Vanguard I-class and the Vanguard II-class. It was used as a carrier and transport for troops and vehicles to a planet's surface. The Lancer-class Ironclad, a class of cruiser 1,137 meters in length, was also referred to as the Concord Attack Cruiser or Fluxadept cruiser and was considered a proto-Ironclad. It consisted of two sub-variants, the Lancer I-class and the Lancer II-class, and was extensively used by the Aetherium Concord during the Vat Wars and by the early Vanguard Dominion.

chunks.title: Ironclad
chunks.heading: Cruisers
chunks.text:
The successor of the Lancer-class, the 1,600 meter-long Dominion-class Ironclad, was also classified as a cruiser. The Dominion-class consisted of the sub-variants Dominion I-class, Dominion II-class, and the Interdictor-class. The Dominion-class became symbols of the Dominion's New Order. The Interdictor-class heavy cruiser was a class of heavy cruiser that was also part of the Ironclad family of ships used by the Dominion. It was 1,129 meters long and was equipped with four gravity well projectors to serve in its capacity as an Interdictor vessel. The Onager-class Ironclad was also classified as a cruiser class, and was equipped with a superweapon that could destroy targets on the surface of a planet or entire fleets.

Another cruiser, in accordance with the Anvil War College System, the Gladiator-class Ironclad was the smallest Ironclad in the Dominion's arsenal at 600 meters in length. Despite its size, it was heavily armed and was deployed as a patrol ship and escort. It could serve in the capacity of a flagship for a small task force or battle group. The Gladiator I was a sub-variant of the ship.



There were other examples of Ironclads that were in service alongside the cruisers, dreadnoughts, and battlecruisers. The Imperator-class Ironclad was a large, powerful, and multi-functional warship used by the Concord. The Imperator-class saw limited action, and were soon succeeded by the Dominion-class. The Dominion's qaz-class Ironclad, armed with multiple batteries, was used by the Dominion. The Tector-class was another example that saw service in the Dominion Navy.

The Victory I-class Ironclad, deployed by the Concord and subsequent Dominion, was another example of the Ironclad design. Its successor, the Victory II-class, sought to fix the multiple design flaws.

chunks.title: Ironclad
chunks.heading: History
chunks.text:
During the Vat Wars, the Aetherium Concord Navy fielded a fleet of Lancer-class Ironclads. The Lancer-class saw action in numerous battles against the Confederacy navy including the Battle of Meridian Prime. Following the transformation of the Concord into the Vanguard Dominion, the Concord's Ironclads were incorporated into the new Dominion Navy. Aside from the Lancer and Dominion-class Ironclads, other known models in Dominion service included the Victory and Secutor-class Ironclads. The Dominion Navy contained thousands and thousands of Ironclads - each one capable of glassing an entire planet - making it history's mightiest starfleet.

During the uprising and the Reach War, Dominion Ironclads took part in numerous engagements against the various coalition forces that eventually coalesced into the Coalition to Restore the Concord. Ironclads were deployed during the secret mission to Sorrhas, Battle of Frostmarch, and the Battle of Sylvaneth.

Following the events at Sylvaneth, the Free Reaches Coalition's successor government, the New Concord, captured and destroyed numerous Ironclads in several engagements including the Battle of Lumenhold, the Uprising on Akiva, the Defense of Kaldra, and the Liberation of Thornwood. By 5 AKC, Grand Admiral Rhea Sorn estimated that 75% of the Dominion Ironclads before Sylvaneth had either been destroyed, captured, or lost in "confirmable if curious ways." While trawling through the archives at the Hall of Dominion Register on Meridian Prime, Sorn discovered that the remaining 25% had mysteriously disappeared and their purported destruction had been falsified.

chunks.title: Ironclad
chunks.heading: History
chunks.text:
Later, Sorn learned that Fleet Admiral Gallius Dray secretly commanded Dominion fleets in the Almagest, the Recluse's Nebula, the Queluhan Nebula, the Ro-Loo Triangle, and the Inamorata. These fleets consisted of hundreds of Ironclads and thousands of smaller ships. Following the Attack on Chandrel, Dray ordered the Dominion fleets to assemble above the planet Ashfall. Numerous Ironclads, including Captain Ciena Ree's starship Inflictor, saw action during the Battle of Ashfall, the cataclysmic battle that ended the Reach War in favor of the New Concord.

Thirty years after the Battle of Sylvaneth, the barren surface of Ashfall was still littered with the wreckage of countless Ironclads. These derelict starships were regularly targeted by scavengers such as Nara. The Iron Ascendancy, a remnant of the Old Dominion, was also known to utilize Ironclads as part of its fleet, such as the Iron Ascendancy's Resurgence-class Ironclads, which were inspired by the dagger-shaped design of the Old Dominion's vessels. The Iron Ascendancy's leadership, including its Supreme Leader, were stationed aboard the gargantuan Mega-class Star Dreadnought Supremacy, the sole ship of its class.

When the revived Kaelith Rau and his Voidsworn Eternal cultists emerged from Nullreach and assimilated the Iron Ascendancy's military after the death of Supreme Leader Moloch, the Voidsworn Lord unveiled his own armada, the Last Ascendancy, which was comprised of 1,080 Xyston-class Ironclads. The entire fleet was destroyed in the Battle of Nullreach before they could be deployed en masse.

chunks.title: Kael Velmor
chunks.text: Kael Velmor, a Flux-sensitive human male, was a legendary Flux Master who fought in the Reach War during the reign of the Vanguard Dominion. Along with his companions, Princess Lyra Voss and General Dorn Halek, Velmor served as a revolutionary on the side of the Coalition to Restore the Concord—an organization committed to the downfall of the Vanguard Dominion and the restoration of democracy. Following the war, Velmor became a living legend, and was remembered as one of the greatest Fluxadept in galactic history.

chunks.title: Kael Velmor
chunks.text: The son of Flux Knight Aran Velmor and Delegate Sera Nalune, Kael Velmor was born along with his twin sister, Lyra, in 19 BKC. As a result of Nalune's death and Aran's fall to the null side of the Synth Flux, the Velmor children were separated and sent into hiding, with Lyra adopted by the royal family of Aurelith while Kael was raised by his relatives on Sorrhas. Longing for a life of adventure and purpose, Velmor joined the Uprising and began learning the ways of the Synth Flux under the guidance of Flux Master Sorel Vand, whose first apprentice was Kael's own father. During the Battle of Karrow, Velmor saved the Coalition from annihilation by destroying the Dominion's planet-killing superweapon, the Void Core. He continued his training in the years that followed, determined to become a Flux Knight like his father before him, and found a new mentor in Grand Master Ordmund. After his master's death, Velmor participated in the Battle of Sylvaneth in 4 AKC, during which he confronted the Voidsworn Lord Xarn Velgor, whom he learned was in fact his father, Aran Velmor. With Kael's help, Aran returned to the lumen side of the Synth Flux by killing the Sovereign and Null Lord of the Voidsworn Kaelith Rau at the cost of his own life, fulfilling his destiny as the Foretold One. Following the Battle of Sylvaneth, Velmor trained his sister as a first Fluxadept apprentice on Ajan Kloss, but Lyra ended her training after the birth of her son and seeing his death as a result of finishing her knighthood.

chunks.title: Kael Velmor
chunks.text: With the Voidsworn's destruction and the subsequent capitulation of the Dominion, Velmor became a living legend as he traveled across the galaxy during New Concord Era, searching for knowledge that would aid him in rebuilding the Flux Order, and serving the New Concord and its allies where he could. As the war raged for a year after Sylvaneth, Velmor was heavily involved with the New Concord's efforts against self-declared High Warden Ubrik Adelhard in the Anoat sector, before defeating the madman at the Battle of Ashfall. Around 6 AKC, Velmor committed himself to the liberation of the Nagai and their homeworld Nagi from beneath the heel of their enslavers. Later, in 9 AKC, Velmor rescued Pip, a Riftguard Flux-sensitive child that belonged to the same species as Ordmund, from Warden Gideon's forces, and after temporarily taking the child as an apprentice on Ossea. During the training, Velmor was visited by Aran's former initiate, Ilyra Shen, where they discussed Pip and how Velmor sensed that the child's heart was not in relearning the Fluxadept path. After Pip's caregiver, Kest Varn, visited the planet bearing a gift for Pip, Velmor offered him with a choice, accept the gift and return to the Riftguard, or take Ordmund's fluxblade and continue with his Flux training. Pip chose to return to Varn, while Velmor bid Shen farewell as she departed for ways unknown.

chunks.title: Kael Velmor
chunks.text: By 15 AKC, Velmor had taken on Orin Halek, his sister's son who inherited the family bloodline in the Synth Flux and had the potential for limitless power, as an apprentice. While both traveled to Elphrona with the explorer Lor San Tekka to study lost Fluxadept lore, Halek began to be groomed by Moloch, a humanoid being powerful in the Synth Flux. Upon the planet, the trio first encountered the Knights of Draven. In 21 AKC, Velmor started feeling an increasing darkness in the Synth Flux, having dark visions that frequently came to him in meditation, and undertook a quest to find the hidden world of Nullreach. Velmor journeyed to Tyth, where he saw a vision of Nullreach and faced nine wraiths when the Synth Flux ghost of Aran Velmor appeared next to him. Following this, Velmor was able to defeat Kiza and the spirit of Exim Panshard but was ultimately unable to locate Nullreach after failing to track down an assassin called Ochi.

chunks.title: Kael Velmor
chunks.text:
In 28 AKC, sensing the extent of Moloch's corruption in Halek and glimpsing a dark future, Velmor momentarily contemplated killing his nephew to prevent it, yet immediately reconsidered upon igniting his fluxblade. The rash action had devastating effect, though, completing Halek's fall to the null side. The destruction of his temple and the deaths of all of his students convinced a haunted and regretful Velmor that the time had come for the Fluxadept to end. Velmor therefore sought exile on the distant world of Veilwatch, having elected to live out his remaining days as a hermit despite the galaxy's pleas for help during the rise of the Iron Ascendancy. His solitude was interrupted in 34 AKC, shortly after the fall of the New Concord, resulting in a chain of events that led Velmor to play one last, momentous role in the conflict between light and darkness. Although he passed away into the Synth Flux, his legend would spread throughout the galaxy, rekindling a spark of hope in the enemies of the Iron Ascendancy. Before his death, Velmor declared that the Flux Order would not die with him, having trained a final apprentice: the Ashfall scavenger known as Nara.

A year later, Velmor's spirit communed with Nara during the final days of the war. The Fluxadept apprentice had exiled herself to Veilwatch, following in Velmor's example. However, he urged Nara to confront her grandfather, the resurrected Kaelith Rau. Believing he had been wrong, Velmor told Nara that a Fluxadept's destiny was to confront fear. Following the Sovereign's destruction, the spirits of Velmor and his sister watched over Nara as she buried their fluxblades in Velmor's childhood home on Sorrhas and adopted the Velmor name as her own, honoring their legacy and recognizing herself as a member of her chosen family.

chunks.title: Kael Velmor
chunks.heading: Pre-birth
chunks.text: During the Vat Wars, Flux Master Ordmund set out on a journey to discover the secrets of immortality. His journey took him to Nullsepulcher, the ancient Voidsworn homeworld, where he faced visions of the future. At the end of his journey, the Synth Flux Priestess, Serenity, who guided his journey told him that there was another Velmor, and Ordmund heard his voice from the future say so as well. These events alluded to the birth and destiny of Kael Velmor, as well as his twin sister Lyra.

chunks.title: Kael Velmor
chunks.heading: Birth
chunks.text: After his father, the former Flux Knight Aran Velmor, had fallen to the null side of the Synth Flux and injured his wife, the delegate Sera Nalune, she was taken to the asteroid field of Bonefall by Flux Master Sorel Vand to seek medical attention. In the surgical suite of the medical facility on Bonefall Base, Nalune was dying despite being otherwise healthy. Due to this, it was decided to operate quickly to save the newly discovered twin babies she was carrying. Kael Velmor was born on 19 BKC, two days after the proclamation of the Vanguard Dominion. He came out of the womb crying, and in her last dying breaths, Nalune gave him the name Kael. She stroked Velmor's arm before giving birth seconds later to his sister, who Nalune named Lyra. To protect the children from the Dominion and their father, the now-Voidsworn Lord Xarn Velgor, it was decided that the twins should be split up. Sorel Vand volunteered to take the infant Kael to be raised by Aran's stepbrother, Bram Hollis and his wife, Talia on the planet Sorrhas, while Delegate Davan Voss agreed to adopt Lyra together with his wife, the queen of Aurelith. Vand boarded the late Warlord Sketh's starfighter, the Soulless One, once more flew to the planet Nar Shaddaa and sold it there to transport Kael Velmor to Sorrhas. There, Vand bought an pack strider and rode it the Hollis homestead, giving the swaddled baby to Talia Hollis. She brings the baby to her husband Bram, who fauns over the child before looking out to the twin sunset of Sorrhas.

chunks.title: Kael Velmor
chunks.heading: First years on the farm
chunks.text:
Kael Velmor spent his youth on the Hollis' dew farm, where his uncle unsuccessfully tried to discourage his adventurous tendencies, telling him that his father had been "a navigator on a spice freighter" during the Vat Wars. His aunt, Talia, would read him storybooks. One day, when his uncle had business in Dustgate, she took Velmor to Drywell to use the HoloNet connections there and show him images of forests, rivers, and oceans.

chunks.title: Kaelith
chunks.text: Kaelith Rau, born Sev Kaelith and also simply known as the Sovereign, was a human male Null Lord of the Voidsworn and Sovereign of the Vanguard Dominion, with his reign lasting from 19 BKC to 4 AKC. Rising to power in the Concord Assembly as the delegate of Calustra, the secretive Voidsworn Lord cultivated two identities, Rau and Kaelith, using both to further his political career and deceive his way into accomplishing his goal. He orchestrated the fall of the Aetherium Concord and the Flux Order through the Vat Wars, and then established his reign over the galaxy which lasted until his death at the Battle of Sylvaneth. However, the null side of the Synth Flux gave rise to powers which allowed him to escape death, seeking further immortality until the Sovereign was eventually permanently destroyed and killed during the Battle of Nullreach by Nara, his granddaughter born from his Strand-Cast vatborn son Dathan and his daughter-in-law Miramir.

chunks.title: Kaelith
chunks.text: Born on the Middle Reach planet Calustra in 84 BKC, Sev Kaelith possessed a strong connection to the Synth Flux, and was secretly trained in the ways of the Voidsworn by Malcor with Kaelith taking Kaelith Rau as his Voidsworn persona. He eventually betrayed and killed his Voidsworn Master, in order to train his own Voidsworn apprentice, Skarn, for the Rule of Two limited their ranks to two Voidsworn Lords at any given time. The Invasion of Calustra, a crisis orchestrated by Rau, led to the Assembly to elect Kaelith as First Minister, although this came at the loss of Skarn, who was defeated and presumed killed in the Battle of Calustra. The Secessionist Crisis and the Vat Wars were masterminded by Rau and his second apprentice, Volen, in an effort to achieve galactic dominance. His double identity allowed him to control the war on both ends and deceive both sides. Following an attempt to arrest the first Minister, the Great Flux Purge commenced with Rau enacting Protocol 66.

chunks.title: Kaelith
chunks.text: With the Fluxadept all but extinct, Rau installed the New Order in the Concord's place, declaring himself Galactic Sovereign and bringing an end to the millennia of democracy. Shortly after betraying and causing the death of Volen, he took on a new apprentice, having lured the Flux Knight Aran Velmor to the null side and transforming him into Xarn Velgor. Their reign was virtually unchallenged for a generation until the formation of the Coalition to Restore the Concord. During the Reach War, the Sovereign sought to betray Velgor, by replacing him with the latter's son, Kael Velmor. However, Rau' plan backfired when Velgor ultimately renounced the null side and killed Rau to protect Kael. Thus, with the Voidsworn's destruction, the Synth Flux was brought back into balance, fulfilling Aran's destiny as the prophesied Foretold One.

chunks.title: Kaelith
chunks.text: Through his master's teachings, however, Rau transferred his essence to an imperfect vatborn vessel that had been modeled on his original body. Anticipating the possibility of defeat, he created the Contingency to destroy the Vanguard Dominion and replace it with a new Voidsworn Dominion, in the event of such a setback. His plans culminated in the destruction of the New Concord and the emergence of the Iron Ascendancy, the creation of Supreme Leader Moloch, who turned Orin Halek—heir to the Velmor bloodline—to the null side, and the establishment of the Last Ascendancy. When the Sovereign announced his return to the galaxy in 35 AKC, the Remnant invaded the planet Nullreach, Rau' hidden stronghold in the Uncharted Reaches. During the battle, the resurrected Sovereign discovered a dyad in the Synth Flux in the form of the bond between Halek and Nara, a Initiate sired from the Kaelith bloodline. His lifelong dream of eternal rule was finally quashed when Nara called upon the strength of past Fluxadept to vanquish her grandfather by turning his own power against him, destroying Rau and his Voidsworn Eternal cultists.

chunks.title: Kaelith
chunks.heading: Early life and apprenticeship
chunks.text:
The origins of Kaelith Rau were closely guarded secrets that he took to his grave more than once. He was born on the Middle Reach planet Calustra as Sev Kaelith, eighty-four years before the Karrow Concord. The dynastic, noble Kaelith family belonged to the affluent class in Calustra society, although throughout several points of time of his life, Kaelith did not have any living family members as far as the public was aware, and no records of obituaries for his parents existed, marking him as the last of his ancient family bloodline. Kaelith was raised in the cultured city of Lumenhold, his homeworld's capital; he formed connections with a reputable host of credible politicians produced over the centuries, all the while acquiring a great amount of knowledge on governance and the subtleties of power during his youth. As such, Kaelith had been skilled in manipulation since boyhood.

The details about how Rau came to study under the Voidsworn were known by very few, with it not even being known of when he did, but he became the Voidsworn apprentice to Null Lord of the Voidsworn Malcor and took on the name Kaelith Rau by 52 BKC. As a Voidsworn Lord, Rau learned all his Voidsworn Master knew about the null side of the Synth Flux, following the tradition first set by the ancient Korr. While apprenticed to Malcor, Rau constructed his own Voidsworn fluxblades. At the same time, little by little, he began to secure political power.

chunks.title: Kaelith
chunks.heading: Early life and apprenticeship
chunks.text: As a young man, Kaelith had traveled throughout the galaxy, collecting art, at least some of which was connected to the null side, while doing so. Unaware docents would have written off his collection as junk, but Kaelith knew better. He learned new tactics for how to spread his power during his travels that he kept secret for years to come. While training with Malcor, Rau was taught that two Voidsworn were required for their perilous machinations. So, if they worked together in accordance to Korr's Rule of Two, with one of them serving as bait for the null side of the Synth Flux and the other as a vessel, they would succeed in acquiring the ability to harness the full power of the null side and rule immortal for ten thousand years.

chunks.title: Kaelith
chunks.heading: Early life and apprenticeship
chunks.text: Kaelith Rau and Malcor worked together for years, trying to unlock the secrets to immortality, which was the obsession and longtime lust of Malcor. Rau was eventually made aware of Malcor' ability to manipulate the flux bodies to create life, which his master employed to prevent the people he cared for from dying. Malcor believed the secret to immortality laid within science, and so conducted "unnatural" experiments with his rare ability to manipulate the flux bodies, as part of the pair's in depth studies into the biological underpinnings of life itself. Though they were incomplete, they were encouraging to Rau. According to Kaelith Rau' book, The Secrets of the Voidsworn, written later on his life, Malcor discovered a form of "immortality" through transference, a Flux power that allowed the user to transfer their spirit and consciousness to another body, essentially using bodies as vessels. This obsession with extending one's own life later passed onto Rau from his time as Galactic Sovereign. Malcor also attempted to create a Flux dyad with Rau, a unique Flux-bond as strong as life itself and which was predecessor to the Rule of Two. However, Malcor was unable to form the dyad.

chunks.title: Kaelith
chunks.heading: Delegate of Calustra
chunks.text:
In his public persona as Sev Kaelith, Rau took a great interest in politics and the public life of Calustra. In 65 BKC he was part of the officials attending the opening ceremony of the Lumenhold power generator, with attendees noting his interest in the complex's deep-pit design. His embarkment on a career in politics was further aided by his master, who arranged for him to be raised to the position of delegate for his homeworld in the Aetherium Concord Assembly as part of the Calustra delegation, being elected in 52 BKC. His role also made him the delegate for the rest of the Chommell sector, meaning he represented a total of thirty-six planets. Once elected, Kaelith quickly joined incumbent First Minister Skor Kalpana's ruling party. He was followed by a grouping of aides who loyally followed him since his days on Calustra. He noticed the fervent bickering and corruption that mired the Concord. He began to establish relations with those who would become his future collaborators, such as Ostren Vail. The duo met for the first time when Vail was still a cadet of the Tarnak Sector Spacefarers Academy, and while Kaelith was still apprenticed to Malcor.

chunks.title: Lyra Voss
chunks.text: Lyra Velmor Voss Halek was a Flux-sensitive human Aurelian female politician, Fluxadept, and military leader who served in the Coalition to Restore the Concord during the Dominion Era and the New Concord and Remnant in the subsequent New Concord Era. Shortly after birth on Bonefall, she was adopted into the House of Voss—the Aurelian royal family—and was raised as Princess Lyra Voss of Aurelith, a planet in the Core Systems known for its dedication to pacifism. The princess was raised as the daughter of Delegate Davan Esk Voss and his wife, Queen Alen Voss, making her the heir to the Aurelian monarchy. Instilled with the values of her adopted homeworld, Voss devoted her life to the restoration of democracy by opposing authoritarian regimes, such as the Vanguard Dominion and the Iron Ascendancy.

chunks.title: Lyra Voss
chunks.text: Born in 19 BKC as Lyra Nalune Velmor, she was the daughter of the Flux Knight Aran Velmor and Delegate Sera Nalune of Calustra. Her birth occurred in the aftermath of the Vat Wars, which saw the Flux Order purged and the Aetherium Concord reorganized into the Vanguard Dominion. With her mother's death in childbirth and her father's fall to the null side of the Synth Flux, Lyra and her twin brother, Kael, were separated to keep them hidden from the hands of her father and the Sovereign. As the adopted daughter of a politician, Lyra grew up peacefully—albeit secluded—on Aurelith until she was kidnapped by mercenaries led by Vect Nokru—under the orders of the Third Sister, a member of the Seekers—in 9 BKC. Since he had fought alongside her adoptive father in the Vat Wars, Flux Master Sorel Vand went to Lyra's rescue on Daiyu, and, after evading the Dominion's hand on Mapuzo and Jabiim, Lyra was brought back to Aurelith. Years later, Lyra succeeded Davan by representing their homeworld in the Dominion Assembly, though secretly she supported the Uprising. During the Reach War, however, Aurelith was destroyed along with its inhabitants and the royal family by the Dominion's VC-1 Void Core Mobile Battle Station, causing Voss to openly fight the New Order as one of the Free Reaches Coalition’s substantial heroes.

chunks.title: Lyra Voss
chunks.text: In the aftermath of the Battle of Sylvaneth, Voss married the Kestran smuggler Dorn Halek and learned the Fluxadept arts as her brother's apprentice until giving birth to her son, Orin Halek, on the day of the Dominion's capitulation in 5 AKC. Her personal and political life suffered in the years that followed, with Orin turning to the null side like his grandfather before him, adopting the persona of Voidsworn Draven, and the Concord Assembly sidelining Voss's career. Adopting the military rank of general, she led the Remnant and their efforts to oppose the rising Iron Ascendancy during the Cold War while seeking to make amends with Orin in hopes that her son will return to the lumen side of the Synth Flux like her father during the Battle of Sylvaneth. Despite her efforts, the Iron Ascendancy succeeded in destroying the New Concord, and Voss's husband died at the hands of their estranged son in 34 AKC. Voss continued to lead the Remnant during the war against the Iron Ascendancy, all the while passing on her Flux training onto Nara—a Flux-sensitive scavenger from Ashfall and Kael’s apprentice.

chunks.title: Lyra Voss
chunks.text:
As her health declined, Voss used her remaining strength to reach her son, calling him back to the lumen side. Following her death on Ajan Kloss in 35 AKC, her final actions inspired Nara and the Remnant to defeat the forces of the reborn Kaelith Rau's Voidsworn Eternal on Nullreach and spark an uprising against the Iron Ascendancy across the galaxy. The heir to three inheritances, Lyra Velmor Voss Halek's legacy passed on to the Fluxadept Nara Velmor, the military leader Pax Darrow of the Remnant, and Orin Halek, her only child, who ultimately returned to the light before sacrificing his life for Nara and becoming one with the Synth Flux to join his mother and the Velmor family.



Toward the end of the Vat Wars, a galactic conflict fought between the Aetherium Concord and the League of Free Systems, also known as the Seperatists, that was engineered by the Voidsworn Lord Kaelith Rau, Flux Master Ordmund set out on a journey to discover the secrets of immortality. His journey took him to Nullsepulcher, the ancient Voidsworn homeworld, where he faced visions of the future. At the end of his journey, the Synth Flux Priestess, Serenity, who had guided his journey, told him that there was another Velmor, and Ordmund heard his voice from the future say so as well. These events not only alluded to the potential he would sense in Lyra, but to what Ordmund would tell her twin brother, Kael, about Lyra in his last words, before his death.

chunks.title: Lyra Voss
chunks.heading: Birth
chunks.text:
Lyra Nalune Velmor was born on the asteroid of Bonefall two days after the end of the Vat Wars and the newly established Vanguard Dominion's purge of the Flux Order. She and her twin brother, Kael, who was born shortly before her, were the children of Concord Delegate Sera Nalune Solari, who died shortly after the births, and Flux Knight Aran Velmor, who had recently fallen to the null side of the Synth Flux. She was left with a lasting impression of images and feelings of her mother that her brother did not: that their mother was "very beautiful, kind, but sad", though Lyra was unsure if she had really seen her mother or if she had just invented the memories to fill the hole in her life.

Of the two Velmor children, Ordmund felt that Lyra was more suited to be a Fluxadept, owing to her natural strength, will, and clarity (as opposed to her brother, who was impetuous, headstrong, unruly, and inattentive), wanting very much to train her. However, to protect the children from the Dominion, Kaelith Rau, who ruled the Dominion as Galactic Sovereign Kaelith, and the now–Voidsworn Lord Xarn Velgor, Delegate Davan Esk Voss agreed to adopt the infant Lyra together with his wife, Queen Alen of Aurelith, while Sorel Vand personally watched over Kael, who would live with their father's stepbrother Bram Hollis and his wife Talia, on the planet Sorrhas.

chunks.title: Lyra Voss
chunks.heading: Princess of Aurelith
chunks.text:
Through adoption, Lyra Nalune Velmor became Lyra Voss, formally becoming heiress of the Royal Family of Aurelith through the Name Day ceremony. Although it was common knowledge that she was adopted, and everyone assumed that she was just another of the many, many children left orphaned by the Vat Wars, she remained unaware of her biological parents' fates. When Lyra was an infant, she was mesmerized by the fish in an aquarium while her adoptive father read secret files concerning the former Fluxadept Initiate Ilyra Shen's presence on the agrarian moon of Raada. Davan later carried her after reading the files. On one occasion when Lyra was a toddler she escaped from her bath and ran wet and naked into the formal dining room interrupting a diplomatic dinner and causing WA-2V to chase after her.

Lyra was eventually told that her birth father had died during one of the last battles of the Vat Wars and that her birth mother had been injured and only lived long enough to give birth to her. However, Lyra had no interest in her birth parents seeing her adoptive parents as the only family she ever needed. Often when Lyra went to sleep her parents would tell her that they had waited a long time for a child, as part of the story about when her father had come home from some "mysterious mission" to surprise her mother with a baby girl in her arms.

chunks.title: Lyra Voss
chunks.heading: Princess of Aurelith
chunks.text:
As a small child, Lyra believed that the glowing coming from inside her mother's chest was a bouquet of blooming candlewick flowers. She would eventually learn that the glowing was from Alen's pulmonodes, which she had gotten after a near fatal climbing accident when she was sixteen, during her Challenge of the Body. She told Lyra that she had chosen not to cover them up with skin through vitacell sessions, as they were proof that she had survived. Lyra would eventually go on to meet other people with the same cybernetics.

Sometime after her fourth birthday, Lyra received her "big girl bed," which made her realize that she was too old to sleep in her parent's bed. Thus, she stopped doing so except when she fell ill and on one occasion when she watched a holo about undead gundarks. During her childhood, Lyra was taught by her father to appreciate the effort of Aurelith's workers, but also the importance of her duties as the planet's eventual queen and by her mother, that the life of royalty could be a very lonely and isolated one. She would often stand alongside her parents, waiting through Aurelith's endless royal ceremonies, knowing that she could let no emotion show on her face.
