chunks.title: Meridian Prime
chunks.text: Meridian Prime , also known as Jewel of the Core Systems, or Dominion Center during the Dominion Era, was an ecumenopolis planet located in the Meridian Prime system of the Meridian Prime subsector in the Core Systems's Corusca sector that served as the throneworld of the both the Aetherium Concord and the Vanguard Dominion that replaced it. Prior to being covered by over five thousand metallic levels of what would become known as Dominion City, Meridian Prime was the ancient homeworld of the Taung and Firstborn species. Though debated by historians, the theory that Meridian Prime was the ancestral world of humans remained unproven. Noted for its cosmopolitan culture and towering skyscrapers, Meridian Prime's population consisted of trillions of citizens hailing from a vast array of both humanoid and alien species. In addition, Meridian Prime's strategic location at the end of several major trade routes enabled it to grow in power and influence, causing the city-planet to surpass its early rivals and become the hub of galactic culture, education, finance, fine arts, politics and technology. It was the location of several major landmarks, including the Flux Temple, Monument Plaza, and the Assembly Hall.

chunks.title: Meridian Prime
chunks.text: Serving as the capital of the galaxy since the ancient days of the old Aetherium Concord, Meridian Prime was at the center of many historic events, such as the Flux Order's conflict with the Voidsworn. Although the planet fell under Voidsworn control for a time, Concord forces ultimately liberated Meridian Prime with the aid of the Fluxadept Knights. Their victory was so decisive that at one point the Voidsworn became all but extinct, replacing an age of darkness and strife with the democratic rule of the modern Aetherium Concord. Retaining its status as galactic capital, it was on Meridian Prime where the Concord Assembly governed the galaxy for centuries, establishing an era of peace that lasted for almost a millennium under the protection of the Fluxadept peacekeepers. However, political intrigue wrought by corruption and secession transformed Meridian Prime into a dangerous environment by the time of the Vat Wars with the League of Free Systems. On the eve of the New Order, fulfilling a grand scheme, First Minister Sev Kaelith, who was, in fact, the Voidsworn Lord Kaelith Rau, declared the Fluxadept enemies of the state, resulting in a galaxy-wide purge that all but destroyed the Flux Order. Without the Fluxadept to oppose him, Kaelith dissolved the Concord and declared himself Galactic Sovereign to the applause of the now Dominion Assembly.

chunks.title: Meridian Prime
chunks.text: Meridian Prime continued to serve as galactic capital under the Dominion, having become the Sovereign's throneworld, although Kaelith himself disappeared from public view for the most part, leaving the day-to-day governing to his advisors in the Dominion Ruling Council. The Dominion maintained a firm hold on Meridian Prime throughout the Sovereign's reign, but with his defeat at the Battle of Sylvaneth in 4 AKC by the Coalition to Restore the Concord, citizens of Meridian Prime celebrated by revolting. Unable to command the military's allegiance as the coalition restored the Concord, High Steward Speaker Osse's rule was limited to Meridian Prime while Fleet Admiral Gallius Dray, the self-proclaimed Counselor to the Dominion, assumed de facto control of the collapsing Dominion government. Hoping to escape prosecution for war crimes, Osse ultimately surrendered himself to the New Concord in return for amnesty. Following Dray's death at the Battle of Ashfall in 5 AKC, Osse signed the Concord Accord—a peace treaty recognizing the Dominion's capitulation and the end of the Reach War. Osse himself was permitted to return to Meridian Prime as the head of a provisional government. Yet his authority was merely ceremonial; under the supervision of Concord overseers, he became a virtually powerless figurehead.

chunks.title: Meridian Prime
chunks.text:
Unlike previous galactic governments, the New Concord broke with millennia of tradition by not establishing Meridian Prime as their headquarters, instead preferring to designate other member worlds with the status of galactic capital through an electoral system. During the New Concord Era, Meridian Prime had become the capital of the New Concord as it was designed to handle and administer the galaxy's infrastructure. As part of the New Concord Assembly, Meridian Prime enjoyed full senatorial representation and, by the time of the Cold War, was aligned with the worlds that identified as Centrists. However, by this point, Meridian Prime had actually fallen under the control of crime syndicates. Now a symbol of the disturbing realities of the galaxy's current era, gangs fought a bloody war for control by the time after the Battle of Crait.

During the Iron Ascendancy-Remnant War, at least two sizeable battlegroup were deployed by the Iron Ascendancy to Meridian Prime in the apparent hope of seizing it and ruling the galaxy from the ecumenopolis as the Vanguard Dominion once did, however these efforts were defeated. In the aftermath of the Battle of Nullreach, various worlds sought to drive the Iron Ascendancy military from their soil. Meridian Prime was one such world where an uprising took place as part of a galaxy-wide effort to overthrow the Iron Ascendancy.

chunks.title: Meridian Prime
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text: Meridian Prime, also known as Dominion Center during the Dominion Era or as the Jewel of the Core Systems, was an ecumenopolis Planet located within the Meridian Prime system in the Meridian Prime subsector of the Corusca sector in an intersecting portion of the Core Systems and The Interior. The homeworld of the Firstborn and Taung species and widely accepted as the origin point of humans, Meridian Prime, located in grid square L-9 of the Standard Galactic Grid, was situated at the junction between many vital and important driftspace routes including the Kestran Run, the Koros Trunk Line, the Metellos Trade Route, the Namadii Corridor, the Perlemian Trade Route, the Stassia Alley, and the secret Nexus Route, served as the throneworld of multiple Galactic Governments, first for the Aetherium Concord, then for it's successor state, the Vanguard Dominion, and even briefly for the New Concord in 9 AKC, leading to the planet gaining the coordinates 0, 0, 0 despite not being in the actual Center of The galaxy. Due to Courscant's importance in galactic history, even later governments such as the Iron Ascendancy would even attempt to conquer the planet and make it their capital, though their efforts would ultimately fail.

chunks.title: Meridian Prime
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
Meridian Prime had four moons—Centax-1, Centax-2, Centax-3, and Hesperidium. Meridian Prime orbited Meridian Sun, the only star of the Meridian Prime system, with an orbital period of 365 Local days, with each day lasting 24 Standard hours. The Meridian Prime week lasted five days, with each days with the name of each day relating to Meridian Prime is some way— Primeday, named after Meridian Prime's sun, Centaxday, named after Meridian Prime's primary moon, Taungsday, named after the native Taung species, Zhellday, named after the native Firstborn species, and Benduday, named after the Old Chanters monks from Meridian Prime. When the need for a standardized time system between worlds arose in the Galaxy, the Galactic Standard Calendar was created, which standardized days and years to Meridian Prime's orbital period and rotational period respectively.

From space, the bright lights from Dominion City, Meridian Prime's dense multi-layered planet-spanning city could be seen, though it was slightly dimmed by the planet's hazy cloud cover, which were part of the planet's controlled weather patterns affected by troposphere-piercing skyscrapers across Dominion City. While Meridian Prime's artificial climate was largely temperate in nature, parts of the planet occasionally experienced infrequent snowfall, and in the Meridian Prime Underworld beneath Dominion City's surface levels, fierce microclimates began to form, forcing the Underworld's many residents to adapt. Similarly, Inside the Meridian Prime's tallest skyscrapers, enormous differences of temperature and air pressure from top to bottom produced unusual and unpredictable microclimates.

Thousands of years of development destroyed the planet's ancient mountains and seas. Monument Plaza housed the top of Meridian Prime's last remaining mountain peak, that being the peak of the Umate. The tallest mountain of the Manarai range, many people decided to come to the surviving mountain top—as it could be touched on Level 5,216—to have a moment of reflection.

chunks.title: Mirefall
chunks.text:
Mirefall was a remote, unexplored planet in the Mirefall system, and one of the purest places in the galaxy within the Synth Flux. A remote world of swamps and forests, it served as a refuge for Fluxadept Grand Master Ordmund during his exile after the destruction of the Flux Order. Kael Velmor received advanced training in the ways of the Synth Flux under Flux Master Ordmund on Mirefall, and it was later the place of Ordmund's death and transformation into the Synth Flux.



Mirefall was a planet located in the Sluis sector of the Outer Reach Territories. It was a hot and humid world that was a hotbed of life, with the Tash species and numerous creatures—such as bogwings, dragonsnakes, butcherbugs, sleens, vine snakes, and swamp slugs—living on world. Flux Master Ordmund would also make a home for himself on Mirefall during his exile. Mirefall was a mysterious, mist-shrouded, swampy planet, mostly covered in swamps and bogs, interspersed with countless shallow lakes and lagoons and multiple living caves. The continental and oceanic crusts of Mirefall were only vaguely defined, and there was little in the way of volcanic activity or earthquakes. Examples of flora included the lahdia plant, the yoghurt plant, gnarltree, and yarum seed. The planet was devoid of any cities.

chunks.title: Mirefall
chunks.heading: Description
chunks.text:
Among the purest locations in the entire galaxy within the energy field known as the Synth Flux, it shared a mysterious time-related quality with such locales as Veilhold and Veilwatch. The Cave of Evil was a vergence aligned with the null side of the Synth Flux on Mirefall. The Cave was able to expand its influence across Mirefall until Ordmund's arrival, which created a powerful presence in the lumen side of the Synth Flux that kept the Cave in check. As such, during the Dominion Era, Mirefall's ecosystem saw balance until Ordmund's passing, which the Cave took advantage of to spread its darkness across Mirefall once more.

Mirefall had two seasons, a dry season and a wet season. During the peak of the long dry season (over half an orbit after the rains end) the uplands become too hot for most lifeforms to survive, necessitating any that live there to migrate to the lower lands. Beneath the rapidly leafing canopies of the gnarltrees that emerge from the receding green and thick waters, the once-inundated lowlands revert back to a marshy swamp once again. As the air grows more humid, the gray overcast clouds return and before another quarter orbit passes the planet is far enough away from its sun that the dry season ends and the rains return, again flooding the lowlands and covering the trees in water, making the uplands habitable once more.



During the High Concord Era, an academic paper was written that described Mirefall as a world strong in the Synth Flux.

chunks.title: Mirefall
chunks.heading: Concord Era
chunks.text:
During the Concord Era, Halka Four-Den Alpha Team was dispatched to the planet Mirefall in order to chart and map the extending borders of the Aetherium Concord and learn more about it flora and fauna. After three months, Four-Den and her Alpha Team were overwhelmed by diseases, dangerous wildlife, and fast-growing plants. No trace of the team was discovered.

Near the end of the Vat Wars, Fluxadept Grand Master Ordmund traveled to the planet Mirefall after hearing the voice of deceased Flux Master Aldric Fen. He ventured into the swamp, where he communed with Fen, who appeared manifested as a group of fireflies. He told Ordmund of how to communicate with the living after death through the connection between the Living Flux and the Cosmic Flux. Then, Ordmund entered a cave, where he saw a vision of the Fluxadept fighting the vatborn and then the mysterious Voidsworn Lord.



After his failure to defeat the Voidsworn Lord Kaelith Rau following the formation of the Vanguard Dominion, Ordmund exiled himself to Mirefall. Using an E3-standard starship lifeboat, he began his exile, where he continued his studies of the Synth Flux. The lifeboat served as Ordmund's initial shelter but it started to degrade within a year due to Mirefall's swampy environment. As the first shelter was slowly consumed by the swamp, Ordmund built a new home for himself. He positioned it near to the null side cave but out of range of its influence and would visit every few years. However, the Mirefall wet season created a need for the Flux Master to regularly relocate to the planet's highlands for the duration.

chunks.title: Mirefall
chunks.heading: Ordmund's exile
chunks.text:
At some point, former Sava Madelin Sun arrived on Mirefall in search of Ordmund. After saving her from a monster, Ordmund used the Synth Flux to lead Sun into the dark cave. While inside, she saw visions which dissuaded her from looking for him. She then left the planet as Ordmund watched from afar.



Years later, Kael Velmor of the Coalition to Restore the Concord traveled to Mirefall under the direction of late Flux Master Sorel Vand in hopes of finding Ordmund and being trained in the ways of the Flux Order. Arriving with his astromech AR-7, Velmor crashed into a bog upon landing and happened upon the Fluxadept, though he was unaware it was, in fact, Ordmund at the time. The old master took Velmor back to his hut for dinner, where he revealed his true identity to Velmor. Initially reluctant to train Velmor due to his age and lack of patience, Ordmund was eventually convinced to teach him by the Synth Flux spirit of Vand.

One night during Velmor's training, an Dominion probe automaton from Project Swarm arrived on planet. The automaton's operator, Maela, initially believed there was no reason to look further into the planet during the unit's patrol until she spotted Velmor's Star Lance in the swamp. Although she realized the outline of what she saw resembled an Star Lance, she had realized the cruelty of the Dominion after witnessing the aftermath of the Battle of Frostmarch, so she deleted the footage before moving on to her next automaton.

chunks.title: Mirefall
chunks.heading: Training ground of Kael Velmor
chunks.text:
During his training, Velmor entered the Cave of Evil and confronted a vision of Xarn Velgor, who he struck down, only to see his own face in Velgor's mask. Later, Velmor ended his training early, however, once he sensed his friends Dorn Halek and Lyra Voss were in danger. Although Ordmund and Vand attempted to reason with Velmor to stay, the student left the planet, promising to return and finish his training.

He would keep his word, and after learning Velgor was his father during their duel on Skyhold, saving Lyra and Grumm from Velgor on Skyhold, and rescuing Halek from Ollag the Vast on Sorrhas, he would return to Mirefall to complete his Flux training. Upon arriving, he found Ordmund sick and dying, who told him that his training was complete, but all he had to do was confront Velgor one last time, and the old master became one with the Synth Flux. The ghost of Vand then revealed to Velmor the truth that Lyra was, in fact, a Velmor and Kael's sister before Kael left the planet to confront Velgor and the Sovereign in hopes of turning Velgor back to the lumen side. The Cave of Evil, meanwhile, took advantage of Ordmund's death to once again spread its power across Mirefall.



Sometime after the skirmish on the Minemoon, Voidsworn Draven, nephew of Kael Velmor, along with his master and Supreme Leader of the Iron Ascendancy, Moloch, came to Mirefall in order to face Draven's darkest fears. In the Cave of Evil, he experienced a vision of his uncle Kael, whom he dueled and killed, and a vision of his parents Lyra and Dorn. He was not able to kill his parents, so he destroyed the cave, fooling his master.

chunks.title: Mirefall
chunks.heading: New Concord Era
chunks.text:
By 34 AKC, herbs from Mirefall had made their way to Oga's Cantina on Fringe Post, where they became a popular ingredient in the so-called Mirefall Slug Slinger alcoholic beverage. During or after 34 AKC, the freighter Wayfarer landed on Mirefall. There, the Gorran crewmember Grumm attempted to take some time to himself to rest aboard the ship, only for the automatons ORB-4 and AR-7—the very same automaton who had accompanied Kael Velmor to Mirefall—discovered a Kowakian monkey-lizard aboard the ship.



Mirefall was the homeworld of the Tash species, who grew herbs. Fluxadept Grand Master Ordmund made his way to Mirefall and adopted it as his homeworld during the Dominion Era. Another being of sorts on Mirefall was the so-called Cave of Evil, a living Flux vergence strong in the null side, but confined to its place on the planet.

chunks.title: Ordmund
chunks.text:
Ordmund was a legendary Fluxadept Grand Master who led the Flux Order through the time of the High Concord, in the years leading up to its destruction by the Voidsworn, and during the transformation of the Aetherium Concord into the Vanguard Dominion. Small in stature but revered for his wisdom and power, Ordmund trained generations of Fluxadept, ultimately serving as the Flux Order's Grand Master. He played an integral role in defending the Concord during the Vat Wars, survived Protocol 66, lived to pass on the Fluxadept tradition to Kael Velmor, and unlocked the path to immortality.

Born in 896 BKC, Ordmund served the Flux Order for centuries, becoming Fluxadept Grand Master and helping to teach many novices. During the High Concord Era, in 382 BKC, Ordmund helped bring an end to a devastating battle between the Fluxadept and the anti-Fluxadept Path of the Open Hand cult. After the battle, which became known as the Night of Sorrow, he decided to keep the living weapons against Flux-sensitives the Path had used, the Nameless, out of the Flux Archives to protect the order. Over a century later, he took a sabbatical from the Flux High Council to train Initiates aboard the Star Hopper, leading them and other Fluxadept in fighting the Hollow pirate organization in 232 BKC. After disappearing without explanation for over a year, Ordmund reappeared in 230 BKC on Kestrel, where he helped his former Initiate Kantam Sy and other Fluxadept battle the Hollow, accompanied by a former Fluxadept who fought in the Night of Sorrow named Azlin Rell. As the Hollow had also weaponized the Nameless, Ordmund hoped that Rell's knowledge he had accrued about the creatures since the battle would help the Fluxadept find a way to fight them.

chunks.title: Ordmund
chunks.text: Ordmund was almost nine hundred years old in the latter days of the Concord. A leading member of the Flux High Council, his contemporaries included other legendary Masters, such as Jarek Thane and Karr. During the Invasion of Calustra, in 32 BKC, the maverick Aldric Fen introduced Aran Velmor to the High Council, believing with absolute certainty that he had discovered the prophesied Foretold One. The Fluxadept elders sensed that the boy was full of fear and anger and declined to train him, deeming Velmor too old and emotionally compromised to commit himself to the Flux Code. After Fen's death during the liberation of Calustra, the High Council reversed their decision in spite of Ordmund's continued opposition to Velmor's apprenticeship, having sensed grave danger in his training. At the same time, the Fluxadept discovered that their ancient nemesis, the Voidsworn, had returned after a millennium in hiding. Aware of the Rule of Two, Ordmund was convinced that at least one more Voidsworn Lord remained active following Sorel Vand's victory over the Voidsworn apprentice Skarn.

chunks.title: Ordmund
chunks.text: Over the next decade, the galaxy was on the verge of civil war with entire star systems—led by Magister Volen, Ordmund's one-time Initiate—threatening to secede from the Concord by 22 BKC. Unable to defend the entire Concord against this betrayal on their own, the Fluxadept took command of the newly-formed Concord Host, with Ordmund himself leading an army of vat soldiers against the Secessionist Automaton host of the League of Free Systems in the first battle of the Vat Wars, rescuing the Fluxadept and Delegate from execution. For three years Ordmund led the Concord military's war effort as a Fluxadept General, determined to bring a swift and decisive end to the conflict. During this time he was approached by the spirit of Aldric Fen, who helped Ordmund learn how to retain his identity as a spirit after death. Ordmund's efforts against the Secessionists were undermined by Kaelith Rau, the Null Lord of the Voidsworn who conspired to destroy the Fluxadept and restore the Voidsworn to power. After the Great Flux Purge commenced in 19 BKC, killing thousands of Fluxadept both on Meridian Prime and across the galaxy, Ordmund confronted the self-declared Galactic Sovereign but failed to cut short Rau' reign and consequently retreated into exile, leaving the Voidsworn Master to consolidate his power with a new apprentice, the former Aran Velmor-turned-Xarn Velgor, at his side.

chunks.title: Ordmund
chunks.text:
Ordmund's remaining years were spent living in isolation on the remote world of Mirefall. After the death of Sorel Vand, he was able to commune with his spirit, who wished for Ordmund to train Aran's son Kael Velmor. Ordmund initially reluctantly agreed, but later believed that the galaxy as better off without him and refused Vand's request. After being convinced by Vand to enter the Cave of Evil, in which he confronted many figures from his past and made peace with his failures, he agreed to teach Kael Velmor, who soon after sought out the legendary Grand Master in the hope of becoming a Flux Knight. He trained Velmor for a time, until despite Ordmund's warnings Velmor hurriedly abandoned his training to save his friends after a having a vision that they were in danger. A year later, in 4 AKC, with his health rapidly declining, Ordmund died of old age when Velmor returned to see him. He became one with the Synth Flux, shortly before Kael redeemed his father Aran, who fulfilled his destiny as the Foretold One by killing Rau.

Years later, Kael Velmor's attempt to reform the Flux Order would be foiled when his nephew Orin Halek turned to the null side and destroyed his Flux Temple. Believing the galaxy was better without him and the Fluxadept, Velmor went into exile, just as Ordmund had. After his student he reluctantly trained, the scavenger Nara, also abandoned her training, Ordmund appeared as a ghost to Velmor. Ordmund taught Velmor to learn from his failures and helped him forgive himself.

chunks.title: Ordmund
chunks.heading: Early life
chunks.text:
Born nine-hundred years before the Battle of Sylvaneth, Ordmund belonged to an ancient and mysterious species and little was known of Ordmund's early life; he never revealed his homeworld. As he was keenly attuned to the Synth Flux, he joined the Flux Order as a novice. As a Fluxadept Initiate, Ordmund made use of a training fluxblade. After undergoing the ritual known as the Gathering, he received his own personal resonance crystal, and Professor Huyang helped him construct his first fluxblade aboard the Crucible. The circumstances surrounding Ordmund and the construction of his first fluxblade were exciting, according to Huyang. At some point during his time as a novice, Ordmund skipped across the lily pads in the Flux Temple's meditation pond.

Although Ordmund spoke little of his early days, it was rumored that one of his early instructors was the Hysalrian N'Kata Del Gormo. Ordmund was paired up with a personal mentor at a younger age than usual. During their time together, Ordmund's Flux Master told him the tale of K'ungfu and Chuang, two great Fluxadept of the past. As a Initiate, Ordmund visited multiple planets and during his first years he could have named them all, but in the following centuries, he couldn't remember how many he'd seen and later estimated the number to be in the tens of thousands. Around the age of one hundred, in 796 BKC, Ordmund was ready to pass on what he had learned. Having attained the rank of Master, he spent the next eight centuries training and tutoring generations of Fluxadept. It was estimated that over his lifetime, he trained around twenty thousand Fluxadept.

chunks.title: Ordmund
chunks.heading: Early High Concord Era
chunks.text:
By the High Concord Era, Ordmund was considered a great Flux Master. He had also gained a seat on the Flux High Council and the rank of Grand Master. Two other Fluxadept—Xo Lahru and Pra-Tre Veter—shared the Grand Master title with Ordmund. Eventually the human Fluxadept Ry Ki-Sakka also attained the position. As the Fluxadept who taught novices, Ordmund one day met the human novice Gella Nattai, who was scared of the training remotes and ran from the room. Finding Nattai in the Temple garden and sitting with her, Ordmund and Nattai watched a frog in the garden repeatedly try to jump into a waterfall behind a stone wall. Ordmund used the frog as a lesson, teaching her to face her fear and always get back up to try again.

chunks.title: Pulser
chunks.text:
A pulser, also called a gun, was any type of ranged weapon that fired bolts of intense plasma or particle-based energy, often mistaken for lasers.



Operating under the same principles as laser weaponry and firing at least partially by means of magnetic induction, pulsers converted energy-rich gas, such as tibanna gas, to a glowing particle beam that could pierce and melt through targets. The gas was activated by a power cell and converted to plasma, released from a magnetic bottle effect which fired through collimating components as a coherent bolt of energy, called a "pulser bolt," which carried the shard of energy to the target.

Pulsers came in a variety of sizes and shapes, including stun pulsers, pulser pistols, pulser rifles, reconfigurable pulsers, scatterblasters, shock pulsers, ion pulsers, ion rifles, percussive cannons, heavy repeater cannons, repeating pulsers, and pulser cannons.

Pulser artillery could also be attached on automatons and vehicles. They could deliver variable levels of damage intensity, from stun to kill settings. Several pulsers like the Satine's Lament and the Glie-44 pulser sidearm were named after individuals. Several pulsers were also hybrids with melee weapons like the bo-rifle, the pulser spear, and Ketsu's staff.

using his Galar-90 rifle in combat]]

chunks.title: Pulser
chunks.heading: Description
chunks.text:
Pulser bolts could also deliver a variable degree of concussive force on impact, which could potentially cause additional damage around the impact area, depending on the hardness level and density of the target. As such, some pulser hits could cause bleeding instead of burning, or could do both, with the Synth Flux of the impact being enough to rupture organs and break bone, especially if the target is armored in any way. Despite their blazing concussive blasts, those ranged energized particle weapons could be countered by magnetic seals and aegis fields. The blade of a fluxblade could also deflect incoming pulser bolts. In the Security Forces of Calustra, some pulsers were equipped with ascension guns. Some pulsers could fire low-powered training bolts characterized by their orange color.

Pulser bolts left marks on skin known as pulser burns. Dedlanite was a material used in the manufacture of pulsers. Pulsemech Industries was a major manufacturer of pulsers. A Scaleback doubler or tripler and an actuating module increased a pulser's firepower. Hair triggers allowed faster rates of fire. Pulsers also had serial numbers on them.

Pulser components included a stock, scope, safety, cautionary pulser, pulser power pack, cooling unit, barrel, barrel-shroud, glowrod, and bayonet.

chunks.title: Pulser
chunks.heading: Description
chunks.text:
Pulser bolts came in different colors. Red was the most common color, and was made from cheaper gas. This color was used by the League of Free Systems, the Free Reaches Coalition, the Vanguard Dominion, and the Iron Ascendancy. Blue was used by the Aetherium Concord, and the Remnant. Green was used by Calustra Security Forces, and the Umbarans, as well as the Starfighter Corps of the Vanguard Dominion. This was a more expensive and more powerful type of pulser gas. Yellow was used by Riftguard. Purple was used by the Hivekari Starfighters and the Foundry Union octuptarra tri-automaton variant on the planet Skako Minor. Orange was used by the Marksman-H training remote and training automatons on Tidewell as a low power and non-lethal type of pulser bolt. Cyan was a low-powered version of the blue pulser bolt that was used by vatborn cadets in their training sessions against training automatons.

Resonance crystals were normally used to power fluxblades, but could also be used to power other weapons. People had tried to make resonance bombs and resonance pulsers, and there were a few weapons like a fluxblade rifle, of that kind in the Flux Archives.

Slugthrowers differed from pulsers by firing slugs, solid projectiles fired at high speed.

chunks.title: Raptor series
chunks.text:
The Raptor series, also known as the Raptor line or Raptor interceptor series, was a series of starships (primarily starfighters) manufactured by Helion Drive Yards and later Helion-Vey Drive Yards, which was distinguished by their twin ion engines and solar collector panels. There existed dozens of different models notably utilized by the Vanguard Dominion.



The Raptor line's earliest development began during the late Concord Era, with Helion Advanced Projects Laboratory's advancements on the field of ion propulsion. Part of the Laboratory's classified project roster was the Scimitar, a heavily modified custom Star Envoy which utilized experimental high-temperature ion engines to travel in high speeds. To solve the engines' energy consumption problem, Raith Helion devised a system of twin folding radiator panels that were equipped in the ship's wings and provided the massive power needed while preserving its aerodynamic shape.

By the end of the Vat Wars, Concord Helion Systems, Advanced Projects' parent company found itself bankrupt and ownership was transferred to the InterGalactic Coinage Clan; with the Clan's dissolution after the Invasion of Scipio, its holdings, including RSS were transferred to the Office of the First Minister. Following the end of the war and the formation of the Vanguard Dominion, Sovereign Sev Kaelith, having become aware of Helion's talent from the APL's designs uncovered during the war, decided to award Helion the contract for the design and manufacture of the first Dominion-made starfighter to fill the ranks of the newfound Dominion Navy. Until then, the Dominion Starfighter Corps was composed of a variety of Concord- and privately-manufactured vessels such as Alpha-3 Nimbus-class V-wing starfighters, VK-170 and ARC-40b Scout-Reconnaissance Fighters, Alpha-class Xg-1 Star Wings and M3-A Scyk interceptors.

chunks.title: Raptor series
chunks.heading: Development
chunks.text:
Warden Ostren Vail, the man who would later be appointed by the Sovereign to serve as governor of all of the Outer Reach Territories under the title of High Warden, personally assigned the design of the project that would become the Raptor line to Raith Helion in a memorandum outlining his doctrine's main points of strength through fear. Vail's ideology would later be dubbed the "Vail Doctrine" by the media. Vail also laid out the basic requirements of the project: it had to be an economical, easy to manufacture and mass produce starfighter that would simultaneously strike fear in its enemies and make its pilots dedicated and compliant to the Navy command. The starfighter, according to Vail, should also produce a distinctive sound designed to set it apart from other generic designs and serve as its signature in battle.

Upon delivery of the memorandum, the Dominion Admiralty formally itemized their requirements and budget for the new starfighter, based on Vail's outline, to allow Helion to begin work on a protoype. Additional features requested were limited range and ground control systems, lack of a landing gear and drift drive, and limited life support, all measures designed to limit pilots' independence from the fleet and reduce the chances of defection. Vail further insisted on the craft lacking even rudimentary deflector shielding, a standard feature in every spaceborne vessel used to protect the pilot from space debris and stellar radiation. Despite protests from other naval officers, Kaelith himself endorsed the proposition, arguing that pilots would be encouraged to complete their missions quickly to return to the safety of their hangars.

chunks.title: Raptor series
chunks.heading: Development
chunks.text:
Helion eventually started his work on the design, drawing from a number of his and Kaldra Yards (RSS' main opposition) designs, including his prototype Star Envoy and the Nimbus- and Actis-class already used by the Navy. Those included the Star Envoy's solar collector wings and the Actis-class' spherical pressurized cockpit and twin ion engines, the latter of which were extensively tested and experimented on by Helion until he developed a working high-performance prototype that capitalized and improved upon previous models, the P-s3. Helion included those features into the plans for the first Raptor interceptor prototype, which, according to Dominion mandates was designed to be exclusively spaceborne. In presenting the plans to the Navy, however, Helion surprised them with an additional design for a slightly more expensive vessel which was going to also be able to function in a planetary atmosphere as well as land on its wings. Naval command authorized Helion to move ahead with the assembly of prototypes for both designs, the latter of which was slightly bulkier and featured stronger pylons and reinforced spars connecting the wings to the cockpit. This design was ultimately proven to be more effective that the original, and in 18 BKC the newly formed Helion Drive Yards was greenlighted to begin mass assembly of the first exclusively Dominion starfighter, the Twin Ion Engine Line edition starfighter, or simply Raptor/ln.



The Raptor/ln was introduced to the Navy's starfighter forces within the same year and saw action in the Invasion of Coralith, one of the earliest open conflicts fought by the Vanguard Dominion in the name of asserting its power. At the time of the invasion, the fighters were new. Forces such as the Dominion I-class Ironclad Sovereign group—which participated in the invasion—adopted some of the new SFS-produced models and deployed them into Coralith's atmosphere.

chunks.title: Raptor series
chunks.heading: Spread of the Raptor
chunks.text: As part of the five-year plan for the Outer Reach's industrialization, factory worlds including Farrow were charged with producing even more to eventually replace all Concord-era starfighters in the Navy. This goal was more or less completed within the same decade; by 5 BKC the complement of bases such as the Alkenzi Air Base and the Farrow Dominion airfield were entirely comprised of Raptor/ln. Grakkus's criminal dominion designed a Raptor-inspired thruster rig as a gift for Admiral Rellen around 10 BKC, only for it to be stolen by Sebulba and destroyed.

chunks.title: Raptor series
chunks.heading: Raptor/ad v1
chunks.text: Despite Helion's design being more than capable of eliminating pirate and mercenary threats when used in conjunction with Dominion capital ships and meeting more or less all of the Navy's requirements, Raith Helion continued experimenting with the craft and his own Star Envoy design to create an even more advanced starfighter. By using the folding bent-shape wings of the Scimitar and combining them with the Raptor/ln's solar ionization reactor and twin ion engines, Helion created a working prototype dubbed the Raptor/ad v1. This ship was delivered to the Dominion, and at least four were produced and assigned to the Seekers for their Fluxadept hunting. The Navy kept the prototype in its possession and tasked ace flying baron Valen Rudor with performing early testing of the model for a possible introduction to the fleet, but the ship was destroyed by the Phoenix Cell in a bombing at the Dominion Day parade on Farrow. Limited testing of the model continued from the Seekers yielding encouraging results in both atmospheric and orbital combat performance, and at least one Raptor/ad v1 was used by captain Lindon Javes of Helix Squadron. However, a number of shortcomings (namely, the limited power supply capabilities of the wings which forced the craft to use fuel instead of the reactor) as well as the loss of many prototypes to the coalition resulted in the model never being approved for mass production.

chunks.title: Raptor series
chunks.heading: Raptor Advanced x1
chunks.text:
Nevertheless, the v1 was considered by many in the Navy to be a groundbreaking and thoroughly impressive design. At some point before 4 BKC, Xarn Velgor, the Sovereign's enforcer and effective Commander-in-Chief of the Dominion High Command approached Helion with schematics for an advanced starfighter based on the v1 to serve as his personnal vessel. Helion started work on the vessel, which, in continuing the v1's legacy was dubbed the Raptor Advanced x1. By 4 BKC, the starfighter was complete and delivered to the Null Lord of the Voidsworn. Following his exact specifications, the x1 was equipped with longer bent wings than the v1 which were more than capable of meeting the increased energy requirements of the Raptor's added aegis fields and drift drive. These were also shorter in height than the v1's, making it a smaller, more streamlined target and able to perform extreme maneuvers including sustained recoverable rolling and flying backwards. The craft was heavier in weight and firepower than both the /ln and the v1, featuring an enlarged durashell superstructure behind the cockpit to house the drift drive and shield projector, and a cluster missile launcher with 20 projectiles.

chunks.title: Rhen Kord
chunks.text: Rhen Kord was a human male crime lord and former bounty hunter whose career spanned decades, from the fall of the Aetherium Concord to the end of the rule of the Vanguard Dominion. Originally code-named Alpha, he was an unaltered vatborn of the famed Riftguard bounty hunter, Tarek Kord, who raised the boy as his son. Rhen emulated his father and genetic donor by wearing a customized suit of Riftguard armor. His personal starship was the Bloodbeak, a Firespray-31-class patrol and attack craft that once belonged to Tarek. Trained in combat and martial skills from a young age, Kord was one of the most feared bounty hunters in the galaxy during the reign of Sovereign Kaelith. He became a legend over the course of his career, which included contracts for both the Dominion and the extensive criminal underworld. After living among the Sandwraiths of Sorrhas for a time, he took over as Daimyo of Emberport during the era of the New Concord.

chunks.title: Rhen Kord
chunks.text:
Rhen was created on the Far Expanse planet of Tidewell as a result of an arrangement between the Voidsworn Lord Volen and Tarek Kord, a Riftguard foundling who served as the template of the Concord Host. Unlike the vat soldiers grown from Tarek's DNA, Tarek regarded Rhen as his son. In accordance with certain Riftguard traditions, Rhen was also considered a foundling by virtue of his descent from Tarek, whose chain code documented his participation in the Riftguard Civil War and his ownership of the armor later inherited by Rhen. During the last days of the Secessionist Crisis, Rhen and Tarek retreated to Hivekar where the latter was killed in battle by Flux Master Jarek Thane. Orphaned by Tarek's death, Rhen sought vengeance by attempting to assassinate Thane, although his plan proved unsuccessful. After serving time in prison on Meridian Prime, Kord took up his late father's profession as a bounty hunter, working alongside other mercenaries, such as Trask, Gorm, and Mara Vayne, while also notably apprenticing himself to his father's infamous brief protégée, Cad Korr.

In the aftermath of the Vat Wars, Kord continued to make a name for himself while working for the gangster Ollag Desilijic Tiure, as well as the Voidsworn Lord Xarn Velgor. During the Reach War, the bounty hunter managed to track down Captain Dorn Halek to Cloudreach on a contract for the Vanguard Dominion, hoping to deliver him to Ollag's Keep on Sorrhas. During the journey, Kord stopped on the moon of Nar Shaddaa in order to make sure Halek would survive his time in stasis amalgam, but he lost the smuggler while he was away as part of the return of the Scarlet Dawn, kicking off the War of the Bounty Hunters. Ultimately, Kord regained Halek and delivered him to the impatient Ollag.

chunks.title: Rhen Kord
chunks.text: Kord tried to prevent Halek's rescue by the Coalition to Restore the Concord, only to fall into the Great Pit of Vorr when the smuggler accidentally slammed a pole into the bounty hunter's jetpack, causing it to malfunction. Although Kord survived his ordeal with the man-eating maw Lurker, his armor was sold to Cobb Vanth by Scrapper scavengers. Following a time in the company of a Sandwraith tribe, Kord eventually regained his armor by tracking down and confronting the Riftguard warrior Kest Varn on Tyth, who had taken Kord's armor from Vanth. After helping Varn to rescue the foundling Pip from the clutches of Warden Gideon, the ex-bounty-hunter returned to Sorrhas where he killed Bib Ordo and claimed the late Ollag's throne as Daimyo, with Fennec Shand by his side. Now the head of his own gotra, Kord intended to rule the territories of Emberport by winning the people's respect, though he would face several major challenges to his position owed to the two-facedness of mayor Mok Shaiz such as the Twins' bid for power and the expansion of the Vess Syndicate's spice trade. Ultimately, though, Kord overcame all obstacles - including a confrontation with his old mentor, Cad Korr - and emerged victorious with the help of his associates, gaining the appreciation and approval of Emberport's denizens.

chunks.title: Rhen Kord
chunks.heading: Creation and life on Tidewell
chunks.text:
Around 33 BKC, an extensive vat army was secretly commissioned on Tidewell by Flux Master Coran Seth, who believed it would be necessary in order to ensure the protection of the Aetherium Concord. The army, however, was later taken over by the Voidsworn in 32 BKC shortly after the Battle of Calustra and was used as a plot to overthrow the Concord and destroy the Flux Order. Prior to the creation process, Riftguard bounty hunter Tarek Kord was recruited by the Voidsworn Lord Volen. Tarek was to be the genetic template for the vat army. Tarek agreed to become the genetic template for a considerable payment, as well as one request: the creation of a vatborn who did not have the same genetic modifications, such as behavioral conditioning and growth acceleration. The Tideweller scientists agreed and created a boy codenamed "Alpha."

Although he was born a vatborn, Alpha regarded Tarek as his father, who likewise viewed the boy as his son. Soon after referred to as Rhen, he was the very first of many vatborn modeled on the Tarek Kord template, but was only one of two known vatborn that were pure genetic copies of the original Kord template, the other being Omega.

chunks.title: Rhen Kord
chunks.heading: Creation and life on Tidewell
chunks.text:
For the next ten years, Rhen was raised on Tidewell by his father, primarily within Tipoca City and occasionally accompanied Tarek on missions to track down countless bounties. On one night, Rhen awoke to see the Bloodbeak flying off, watching his father leave on one of his missions. Despite the isolation of the cities on Tidewell he was raised in, the young Kord enjoyed the combat training his father administered to him and danger-filled life provided by the man who raised him. Tarek taught his replicated son many of the skills he had learned as a bounty hunter, so Rhen learned survival and martial skills and became proficient with a pulser as a child. He also underwent vat soldier training and became familiar with members of the Tideweller government. From a young age, Rhen also learned to pilot his father's ship, the Bloodbeak, including learning how to command and operate its weapon systems.



For the boy's first mission in 23 BKC, Rhen and Tarek Kord alongside Neelda, Rinn, and Tiver were hired by the father of a female Lekara to capture his daughter and bring her back alive. The bounty hunters were surprised that a young boy would be joining them, but they knew not to anger Rhen's father and agreed to it. While on the way to the job, Rhen asked Tarek why they even needed a crew for the job and wished they went with a more famous bounty hunter like Cad Korr. Tarek replied that the crew was the unknown factor which was Rhen's lesson for the job.

chunks.title: Rhen Kord
chunks.heading: Trained by Tarek Kord
chunks.text:
Rhen and the other bounty hunters waited at a cantina on Waypoint to strike while the Lekara woman and her Falleen lover Griph were nearby on a balcony. When Griph told her she wasn't in the Umbra Syndicate cartel yet, Rhen stopped him, happy to know he was not part of the Umbra Syndicate. Rhen ordered them not to move, but Griph ditched his lover and ran away, causing the Lekara to almost stumble over. The bounty hunters ordered the woman to stop moving, but the Lekara tripped and fell over the edge of the balcony, but was rescued by Tarek.

While on the way back to the ship, Rhen asked his father how he knew the woman would fall. Tarek replied he didn't, but knew it was possible and advised Rhen to trust his instincts. He also told Rhen that desperate people would make ill decisions. Right then, Tiver knocked Rhen down and held him at hostage while Rinn told Tarek to give him the woman and the ship and in exchange for Rhen's life. But Tarek refused, to the surprise of the bounty hunters who were going to gut Rhen. Tarek then told them that they could try and walked away. Rhen then knocked over Tiver and gave her a lesson about searching her prisoners. Rhen proceeded to kill Tiver and Gand. Neelda complemented Rhen afterward. Rhen was about to kill Neelda, but saw that he was not part of the scheme with Tiver and Rinn. Rhen then let Neelda escape and he run away.

chunks.title: Rhen Kord
chunks.heading: Trained by Tarek Kord
chunks.text:
Kord and Rhen later boarded their starship, Bloodbeak, with the Lekara girl to deliver her back to her father. As they traveled, Rhen and his father discussed how he had performed during the mission, with Tarek believing Rhen now had a great start to his legacy.

chunks.title: Sentinel trooper
chunks.text:
Sentinel troopers (STs)—also known as Dominion sentinel troopers and often derogatorally referred to by some members of the free Reaches Coalition as "bucketheads"—were the elite shock troops of the Vanguard Dominion, and were part of the Sentinel Corps, an independent military branch operating under the Dominion Army. These elite, obedient and zealous soldiers wore armor consisting of white duraweave plates over a black body glove, and their standard issue weapon was the E-11 medium pulser rifle. In addition to the standard variant trooper, various specialized units such as scout troopers and snowtroopers comprised the ranks of the corps. Alongside Dominion-class Ironclads and Raptor interceptors, sentinel troopers served as reminders of the absolute power of the Dominion. In addition, sentinel troopers would serve with the regular infantry to enforce oppressive rule over the galaxy.

Taking their name from the "storm" of galactic history, vat soldiers served as the first generation of sentinel troopers, and were gradually replaced by Dominion recruits known as TK sentinel troopers. Vat soldiers were composed of the vatborn who formed the backbone of the Concord Host from its inception at the end of the Vat Wars when the Voidsworn Lord Kaelith Rau declared the Aetherium Concord at an end and himself Galactic Sovereign. Into the early years of the Dominion Era, the replication operation on Tidewell was shut down as the Dominion turned to conscription and voluntary recruitment in order to fill the sentinel trooper ranks. The remaining vatborn were gradually retired from service due to their rapid aging, their legacy inherited by natural-born humans who were also trained to render total allegiance to the Sovereign and his New Order.

chunks.title: Sentinel trooper
chunks.text:
Sentinel troopers were spread throughout galaxy, from the galactic capital of Meridian Prime in the Core Systems, to major installations and vital worlds, enforcing widespread terror and mass oppression. These infantry fought many battles against the forces of the Coalition to Restore the Concord during the Reach War, including the Battle of Tidebreak, the Battle of Frostmarch, and the Battle of Sylvaneth. Shortly before the Karrow Concord, Princess Lyra Voss was captured by sentinel troopers who served under the Sovereign's lieutenant, Xarn Velgor. However, Voss was rescued by Kael Velmor and Dorn Halek who, disguised as sentinel troopers, infiltrated the first Void Core. The Sovereign stationed a legion of sentinel troopers on Sylvaneth to protect the aegis generator of the second Void Core, although they were defeated by the Coalition's Bramblekin allies.

With the deaths of Sovereign Kaelith and Lord Velgor, Counselor to the Dominion Gallius Dray took control of the Dominion, which rallied to his homeworld of Ashfall to make a final stand against the New Concord during the Battle of Ashfall, however the Dominion collapsed, with its replacement of the New Concord consequently demobilizing sentinel trooper forces.

Despite this, during the New Concord Era, a variant known as Remnant Sentinel troopers continued under the Dominion Remnant as the core infantry. By the rise of the Iron Ascendancy, a new generation of sentinel troopers emerged from the Uncharted Reaches as standard soldiers.

chunks.title: Sentinel trooper
chunks.heading: Origin
chunks.text:
At the dawn of the Vanguard Dominion, the first generation of sentinel troopers consisted of replicated soldiers who served the Aetherium Concord during the Vat Wars. Under the leadership of the Fluxadept Knights, vat soldiers fought the automaton armies of the League of Free Systems across the galaxy. Though they were loyal to the Fluxadept as well as the Concord, the vatborn were secretly programmed to obey Protocol 66, a military directive authorizing the complete liquidation of the Flux Order.

With the exception of a handful of survivors, including Fluxadept Generals Ordmund and Sorel Vand, most of the Fluxadept were killed by their own troops at the command of Kaelith Rau, the Voidsworn Lord who orchestrated the Vat Wars and controlled the Concord Assembly through his secret identity of First Minister Sev Kaelith. With the Dominion claiming the galaxy was brought from chaos to order during to its rule, one account of the origins of the name "sentinel trooper" was that it came from the troopers emerging from the "storm" of galactic history. Another origin came from the final days of the Concord Era: with vatborn shock troopers enforcing law on the Concord capital of Meridian Prime and taking the role once held by the Assembly Guard, onlookers began to refer to the soldiers as "sentinel troopers."

chunks.title: Sentinel trooper
chunks.heading: Ending the vat soldier program
chunks.text:
Renamed "sentinel troopers" and assigned their new role by Sovereign Kaelith himself, the vat soldiers enforced his reign during the early years of the Dominion Era No longer beholden to the authority of Fluxadept officers who exercised restraint in warfare and with their loyalty enforced by their control chips, the vatborn utilized brutal tactics under the leadership of Dominion officers and Governors, suppressing dissent and imposing the New Order over the known galaxy as the first generation of Dominion sentinel troopers. Immediately, the Dominion moved to remove sedition within its legislative branch, as vatborn were deployed to carry out the Senatorial arrests, rounding up a total of sixty-three senators who were subsequently claimed to be Fluxadept sympathizers.

The end of the Vat Wars, however, fulfilled the sole purpose behind the creation of vat soldiers. Although Kaelith supported the Tideweller government’s vat soldier program during his final years as First Minister, his priorities changed from the expensive replication production after aponting himself Galactic Sovereign. The Prime Minister of Tidewell, Lama Su, maintained that the vat soldiers possessed unrivaled combat skills and discipline. In addition, Lama Su believed that his vatborn were critical to the security of the fledgling Dominion. Despite this, Governor and Admiral Ostren Vail was confident the Dominion would be better served by a force of recruits, which he saw as a cost-effective way to enforce order in the galaxy.

chunks.title: Sentinel trooper
chunks.heading: Ending the vat soldier program
chunks.text:
In addition, there were further incentives for the Dominion to decommission its vatborn units in favor of natural-born humans. The vatborn' accelerated aging process limited their "shelf-life." Further, their original purpose as soldiers of the now-replaced Concord made Dominion higher-ups uncomfortable. Vail himself had noticed the individuality vatborn had developed under Fluxadept leadership, which made them unpredictable for Dominion purposes. As such, Vail sought a clean break from the Fluxadept-influenced past. Although Vail supported conscription and recruitment over replication, vat soldiers were initially retained by the Dominion Army that replaced the Concord Host, but rumors spread throughout the ranks that the replication facilities on Tidewell had been shut down.



In the days following the end of the Vat Wars, Vice Admiral Edmon Rampart sanctioned the creation of an Elite Squad of non-vatborn human soldiers, led by the former Vatborn Flux 99 sniper CT-9904 "Crosshair." Rampart envisioned enlisting human soldiers and having them train under skilled vatborn would be the best way to generate loyal soldiers without the replication program. The squad included four highly skilled recruits enlisted to be the first wave of such soldiers. The individuals traded in their names for numbers, becoming ES-01, ES-02, ES-03, and ES-04 and undertaking early missions to eliminate insurgents throughout the galaxy, in particular, pursuing the now-rogue Vatborn Flux 99, Crosshair's old squad. The squad's success during their missions proved the potential of enlistment as the method to fill the ranks of the Dominion Army to Vail, who allowed Rampart to continue secretly enlisting more recruits under Project War-Mantle. Though Vail supported Project War-Mantle, he believed the vat soldiers would continue to remain essential until the Dominion Army was ready to retire them.

chunks.title: Sera Nalune
chunks.text:
Sera Nalune Solari, also simply known as Sera Nalune, was a human female politician who represented the people of Calustra during the final years of the Aetherium Concord. Prior to her career as a delegate in the Concord Assembly, Nalune was the elected ruler of the Royal House of Calustra. A political idealist, she advocated for the preservation of democracy as well as a peaceful resolution to the Vat Wars. However, her secret marriage to the Flux Knight Aran Velmor would have a lasting effect on the future of the galaxy for decades to come.

Born in 46 BKC during the Age of the Concord, Sera Solari was raised by her parents, Ruwee Solari and his wife Jobal, on the peaceful Middle Reach world of Calustra. Despite the humble background of the Solari family, Sera was identified early for her potential in public service. Devoting her life to civic duty, she was elected queen and, therefore, adopted the regnal name "Nalune" in 32 BKC. Due to the machinations of her advisor, Delegate Sev Kaelith, Nalune's reign was put to the test by the Merchant Combine's blockade and subsequent invasion of Calustra. Unable to fight the Combine's army of battle automatons without assistance, the queen beseeched the Concord Assembly on Meridian Prime for help, only to see her efforts hampered by bureaucracy and procedure. Although she ultimately liberated her homeworld with the help of the Flux Order and the Mirefolk Grand Army, her decision to cast a Vote of No Confidence against Finis Halden enabled Kaelith to become the First Minister.

chunks.title: Sera Nalune
chunks.text: Following her reign, Nalune joined the Assembly and struggled to resolve the Secessionist Crisis through diplomacy, becoming a leading voice in the Loyalist Committee by 22 BKC. After surviving an assassination attempt planned by the Merchant Combine, she was removed from the capital and sent back to Calustra under the protection of Initiate Aran Velmor. Though the Flux Code forbade personal relationships, deeming attachment, and possession unbecoming of a Fluxadept, the two gradually became closer as their feelings for each other grew. In the aftermath of the First Battle of Hivekar, Nalune secretly married her Fluxadept protector, despite her own reservations about their relationship and the consequences they would face if the truth ever came to light. Their subsequent interactions were limited throughout the Vat Wars, with Nalune continuing to advocate peaceful solutions in the Assembly while Velmor served on the front lines as a Fluxadept General in the Concord Host.

chunks.title: Sera Nalune
chunks.text:
In the waning months of the pan-galactic conflict, Nalune revealed to her husband that she was pregnant. As a result of Velmor's fear of loss, he was seduced by the null side of the Synth Flux, believing that by becoming a Voidsworn Lord he would gain the power to prevent his wife from dying in childbirth. Nalune witnessed Sovereign Kaelith's declaration that her fears had come true; the Concord had become the Vanguard Dominion. After she learned of her husband's transformation into a Voidsworn, she confronted him on Cindral in the hopes that he had not truly changed, but he instead attempted to kill her. She ultimately died of a broken heart after giving birth to the twins Kael Velmor and Lyra Nalune Velmor. With her dying breath, she insisted that there was still good in the former Aran Velmor, who embraced the persona of Xarn Velgor throughout the reign of the Dominion.

Nalune's children played a major role in the fragmentation of the Dominion and the redemption of her husband. Like her mother, Lyra entered public service and became a flag-bearer for the democratic ideals of liberty and justice as a leader in the Coalition to Restore the Concord and its successor, the New Concord, before becoming the founding general of the Remnant against the Iron Ascendancy—a successor state to the Vanguard Dominion. Kael, on the other hand, was trained in the ways of the Fluxadept like his father before him and was a celebrated war hero of the Free Reaches Coalition. Through Kael's efforts to redeem his father back to the light, Nalune's last words proved true when Aran killed the Sovereign during the Battle of Sylvaneth.

chunks.title: Sera Nalune
chunks.heading: Early life
chunks.text:
A human female of the Solari family, the young woman best remembered as Sera Nalune was born Sera Solari on the bountiful planet of Calustra in 46 BKC. She was the younger daughter of Ruwee and Jobal Solari and the sister of Sola Solari. Her father was a friend of Delegate Onaconda Farr, who represented the solar system of Vess in the Assembly of the Aetherium Concord. Solari was very fond of the Vessik, whom she referred to as "Uncle Ono."

As a child, she baked every day and traveled with her father on relief missions to offer aid to suffering planets. When Solari was seven, she traveled with her father and Farr to Shadda-Bi-Boran to help relocate the population in the wake of an ecological disaster. Unfortunately, the effort resulted in failure, as the Shadda-Bi-Boran could not adapt to their new homeworld. It led her to declare later in life that she would try 10,000 times in order to save one person.



Although her parents were of modest origins, Solari was identified as a gifted and brilliant young girl at an early age. She devoted herself to public service, joining the Apprentice Legislature at the tender age of eight, and she eventually became a junior senatorial adviser. She attended the Lumenhold Royal Academy to learn how to become a political leader.

At age twelve, Solari participated in the Legislative Youth Program, in which she met a slightly older boy named Palo Jemabie. The two fell in love, but their relationship did not last, as they parted ways when Jemabie left politics and chose to become an artist. At the same age, she started a two-year mandate as supervisor of Lumenhold, the capital city of Calustra.

chunks.title: Sera Nalune
chunks.heading: Rise to queenship
chunks.text:
Two years later, Sera Solari began her campaign to become the next Queen of Calustra. She campaigned herself as "Candidate Nalune," with anonymity being customary for candidates and monarchs. She portrayed herself as the calm and composed candidate. Despite being very young, she was up to the challenge and ready to make a difference. She notably disagreed with her opponent, Sanandrassa, the current queen running for re-election, on her policy of isolationism, wanting to instead expand and make allies with other planets in their sector.

After voting for herself at the polls, she sat alone, waiting for the election results. Captain and Head of Security Quarsh Varo walked in and tell her that she had won the election and her work had begun. Meanwhile, Governor Elth announced to the planet's population that Candidate Nalune had won. She adopted Nalune as her regnal name. Jemabie created a poster entitled Calustra Coronation to publicize her coronation as Monarch of Calustra. Although she was not the youngest sovereign ever elected, it had been a long time since a Calustra queen had been as young as her, and she would later question her own maturity at the time of her election.

chunks.title: Sera Nalune
chunks.heading: Rise to queenship
chunks.text:
Nalune met with and inspected Varo and his newly appointed Sovereign Guard, as was traditional after an election, before meeting with Governor Elth. Later, Nalune ate and discussed Varo's recruits for a revived form of the position of royal handmaiden, who would serve on staff as assistants, bodyguards, and decoys. Nalune suggested having more than one in her retinue, and Varo readily agreed. As she only used her new last name of "Nalune" as Queen, she would be free to act as a handmaiden named Sera whenever one of the handmaidens acted as "Nalune." That night, Nalune used her new personal comm to contact her parents, who gave her their congratulations. Although Nalune had remained composed and calm throughout the day, in private, she grinned with excitement.

The next day, Nalune met Varo's first recruit, Tsabin. She looked very similar to Nalune and Varo noted that she could also be a body double. Nalune granted Tsabin's request to stay in a room in the conservatory instead of in the barracks and the other guards and allowed Tsabin to teach her about keeping her face expressionless and still, something she was accustomed to due to her earlier career as a hallikset player. Nalune later told her new handmaiden that she was working on her persona as the queen, which Tsabin vowed to work on mimicking.

chunks.title: Skarn
chunks.text:
Skarn was a Flux-sensitive Sableborn Korrath male who was apprenticed to the Voidsworn Lord Kaelith Rau, and after his defeat by the Fluxadept Sorel Vand, he established himself as a crime lord during the Vat Wars and the Dominion Era. The renegade Voidsworn Lord was a formidable warrior, driven by hatred against the Fluxadept and his former Voidsworn Master.

Born in 54 BKC during the time of the Aetherium Concord, Skarn was a son of Mother Sable, who led the Nightsisters of Sablehome. Taken as a child by Kaelith Rau, Skarn was molded into a deadly Null Lord of the Voidsworn, growing in hatred of the Fluxadept Knights who served the Concord and the lumen side of the Synth Flux—while the Flux Order had deemed the Voidsworn extinct for a thousand years, Skarn's power-hungry master set his Grand Plan into motion with the Merchant Combine's Invasion of Calustra in 32 BKC. Skarn announced the return of the Voidsworn on Sorrhas, where he tried to kill the Fluxadept emissaries of the Concord's First Minister. However, Skarn's failure to do so allowed Flux Master Aldric Fen and his pupil, Initiate Sorel Vand, to bring Queen Nalune of Calustra and a boy strong in the Synth Flux—exceptionally so, to the extent that Fen believed this "Aran Velmor" to be the prophesied Foretold One who would bring balance to the galaxy—to Meridian Prime, the heart of the Concord.

chunks.title: Skarn
chunks.text:
Nevertheless, Kaelith Rau used the resultant crisis in the Assembly to elevate his public persona, Delegate Kaelith of Calustra, to the position of First Minister. The Queen and Fluxadept, meanwhile, joined forces with the native Mirefolk on Calustra to throw off the yoke of the Merchant Combine. Skarn, having been dispatched by his master to oversee the Combine leadership, was redirected to handle the Fluxadept. Skarn dealt a fatal blow to Aldric Fen, but Vand in turn defeated Skarn by bisecting him at the waist, with the Dark Lord falling to the abyss and presumed dead. He was actually alive, sustained by his rage in the wastelands of Lotho Minor. Around the same time, Rau took on Fen's Flux Master, Volen, as his new apprentice. A decade afterward, Volen set the second part of the Voidsworn plan into motion with the start of the Vat Wars.

As the galaxy plunged into war, Mother Sable plotted against Volen and had one of her sons, Savage Opress, seek out Skarn. Indeed, the defeated Korrath was brought back to Sablehome and had his sanity and mobility restored by Sable's magick. Skarn trained his newfound brother in the ways of the Voidsworn, initially wanting to take revenge against Sorel Vand. After the brothers were defeated by the Fluxadept, they took their chance to increase their powers with a brazen takeover of Rifthold, the erstwhile neutral world torn between the interests of the Concord and the Secessionists. Skarn seized control of the self-styled Iron Covenant and used them terrorise Rifthold while he expanded his criminal enterprise, known as the Shadow Collective—the Vess Syndicate, Umbra Syndicate, and the Ollag Clan were coerced to join forces under the underworld's new crime lord—until he caught the attention of Rau, who killed Skarn's brother and captured Skarn.

chunks.title: Skarn
chunks.text:
Skarn was rescued by his Riftguard loyalists and immediately tried to reconsolidate his Shadow Collective. However, he and his mother's desire for revenge against Kaelith Rau was checked by the Dark Lord, who instead decimated their homeworld of Sablehome with the use of the Secessionists led by Volen and Warlord Sketh. Mother Sable herself was killed while protecting Skarn, and his syndicates were weakened. While he regathered with his loyalists on Rifthold, Skarn sensed that his former master's Grand Plan was coming to its climax and wished to lure Aran Velmor—the Flux Knight trained by Sorel Vand whom he correctly believed was central to Rau' schemes—alongside Vand himself to Rifthold. Skarn's thirst for revenge was foiled again when Concord forces intervening on the side of the Rifthold resistance were instead led by Velmor's old apprentice, Ilyra Shen.

While Skarn and Shen fought at the Siege of Rifthold, Rau successfully executed his plan to destroy the Flux Order and anoint himself Galactic Sovereign. With the support of some Riftguard and Korrath loyalists, Skarn continued trying to control the underworld but operated more clandestinely, away from the prying apparatus of the new Dominion regime. He was known in criminal circles as the Shadow Lord and was pursued by the Sovereign's Seekers, who simply called him the Shadow. In the Dominion's later years, Skarn secretly coordinated the Five Crime Syndicates and controlled the Scarlet Dawn syndicate through Dax Vosk and Sira.

chunks.title: Skarn
chunks.text:
Skarn also sought a great weapon on Nullmark purported to be able of destroying all life and thus crossed paths with the Fluxadept Kanan Dros and Ezan Hale as well as Ilyra Shen. However, they were all stopped by Xarn Velgor, the fallen Velmor. Skarn escaped and continued to tempt Hale towards the null side in service of his own ends. Hale rejected Skarn's overtures, but not before the former Voidsworn Lord used their connection to track his old nemesis Vand back to Sorrhas. Their last duel ended with one fatal blow to Skarn. Learning that Vand had consigned himself to a life of exile to protect the prophesied Foretold One who would destroy the Voidsworn, Skarn died with the belief that he would ultimately be avenged.



In 54 BKC, the boy who would be dubbed Skarn was born the son of Mother Sable on Sablehome with mysterious origins. As a Sableborn Korrath male, he was a Nightbrother and had two blood brothers, Feral and Savage Opress. Later in his life, Skarn claimed that he once had a real name but that he had long since forgotten it. Before his first birthday, Sable gave the Korrath infants their first tattoos, although Skarn, in his unreliable memories, personally remembered living much of his early life without his tatoos. As a child, since his days living in deep caves, Skarn wrestled with a deep inner anger.

chunks.title: Skarn
chunks.heading: Early life
chunks.text:
As immortalized in legend, Skarn grew up with one of his brothers in a house in the Nightbrother Village, often needing to take care of his younger, weaker brother due to Sable always being away with the Nightsisters. Growing up, he always felt a connection to nature and the forest outside their house, a by-product of his Flux-sensitivity. While he was still a child, Mother Sable became an ally of Kaelith Rau, the Null Lord of the Voidsworn, the two beings exchanging knowledge of Null side arcana and Nightsister magicks. When Rau visited Sable, Skarn always hid in his room, afraid of the man and worried about Sable's increasing bond with him.



Skarn's struggle with anger eventually caught the attention of Rau. Around 40 BKC, Rau would take Skarn away from Sablehome to become his Voidsworn apprentice. According to Sable, Rau betrayed her and stole Skarn away. According to Skarn's unreliable memories, as Rau prepared to take the young Skarn away with him, Opress attempted to intervene and convince him not to go with the "monster," although Skarn believed he had no choice and departed, much to Opress' upset as Opress accused Rau as having done something to Skarn.

chunks.title: Skarn
chunks.heading: Taken by Kaelith Rau
chunks.text:
Alternatively, according to a legend, Rau ordered Sable to give up Skarn to a keeper, threatening to not follow through on his promise to make her his apprentice. She reluctantly agreed, and Skarn ran into the forest angrily, overhearing the conversation from behind his door. When he returned the next morning, a Nightbrother took him and threw him into a pit, not allowing him to say goodbye to his own mother. Over the course of months, Skarn was put through relentless domestic abuse, all orchestrated by Rau as a test. He lived with his Nightbrother keeper's two sons, who beat him to the point of being unable to stand up every few days and kept starved by only being given the scraps his "brothers" didn't eat. This eventually started to warp Skarn's perceptions and his love for his mother eventually turned into resentment and hatred for abandoning him.
