chunks.title: Sorel Vand
chunks.text:
Sorel Vand was a legendary Flux-sensitive human male Flux Master who served on the Flux High Council during the final years of the Concord Era. As a High Fluxadept General, Vand served in the Concord Host that fought against the Secessionist Automaton host during the Vat Wars, and was nicknamed "the Negotiator." Vand, however, was forced into exile as a result of the Great Flux Purge initiated by the Concord's own vat soldiers when Concord First Minister, secretly Kaelith Rau, implemented Protocol 66. As a mentor, Vand was responsible for training two members of the Velmor family, Aran and Kael Velmor, both of whom served in turn as his Initiate in the ways of the Synth Flux.

Vand was born on the planet Stewjon in 57 BKC. He was Flux-sensitive, and therefore taken from his family and inducted into the Flux Order as a child. Raised in the Fluxadept Grand Temple on the planet Meridian Prime, Vand was assigned to Flux Master Aldric Fen. In 32 BKC, Vand attained the rank of Flux Knight by defeating the Voidsworn Lord Skarn during the Invasion of Calustra. He also chose to train Aran Velmor—the prophesied Foretold One who was destined to destroy the Voidsworn and restore balance to the Synth Flux—having promised Fen who died in the fluxblade duel against Skarn.

chunks.title: Sorel Vand
chunks.text:
With the advent of the Vat Wars in 22 BKC, Vand adopted the military rank of High Fluxadept General in the Grand Army of the Aetherium Concord, and was given command of the Open Circle Fleet, the Third Systems Army, and the Seventh Reach Corps. Vatborn Marshal Commander Kell served as his second-in-command throughout the galaxy-wide conflict, with their forces achieving multiple victories over the League of Free Systems. In the midst of the war, his old enemy Skarn re-emerged into galactic affairs, bent on revenge against Vand for his debilitating defeat decades prior. Though they clashed in heated duels on multiple occasions, Skarn failed to end Vand's life or cripple his spirit, despite murdering his former love, Duchess Miren, Duchess of Rifthold.

In 19 BKC, Vand killed the Secessionist Supreme Martial Commander, Warlord Sketh, during the Battle of Pau Sink, effectively ending the Vat Wars. He later survived the initial onslaught of the Great Flux Purge against the Flux Order, which resulted from the machinations of the Voidsworn Lord Kaelith Rau. After discovering that Velmor had betrayed the Fluxadept and turned to the null side of the Synth Flux, becoming Rau' Voidsworn apprentice under the name of Xarn Velgor, Vand defeated his former Initiate on Cindral and exiled himself to the Outer Reach planet Sorrhas as the Vanguard Dominion rose to power. Adopting a hermit lifestyle as "Sorel Vand," he watched over Velgor's and Delegate Sera Nalune's son, Kael.

chunks.title: Sorel Vand
chunks.text:
Ten years later, Vand left exile to rescue Lyra Voss, Kael's twin sister, and was pursued by the Dominion's Seekers and Velgor himself. Later, Vand was hunted down once again by Skarn, whom he finally slew to protect the young Kael. Vand began the boy's Flux training in 1 BKC, and soon after encountered Velgor aboard the first Void Core, where he sacrificed himself to ensure that Kael and his allies escaped from the Voidsworn Lord. In death, Vand became one with the Synth Flux which allowed him to continue guiding Kael throughout the Reach War. In 4 AKC, Vand reunited with his former student, Aran Velmor, who died destroying his Voidsworn Master in order to save his son. Vand was remembered as a legendary Flux Master during the rise of the New Concord; Orin Halek, the son of Kael's twin sister, Princess Lyra Voss, was named after Vand. Halek's turn to the null side left Kael disillusioned with the Flux Order's legacy, and he held Vand responsible for Aran's transformation into Velgor. However, Kael's faith would eventually be restored with the aid of Kaelith Rau's granddaughter Nara, to whom Vand would lend his voice and strength in a final battle and victory against her resurrected ancestor on Nullreach in 35 AKC.



Sorel Vand was born on the planet Stewjon in 57 BKC. Despite being very young when he left his family, he still had glimpses of his father's hands and his mother's shawl, and he remembered a baby he believed to be his brother although he barely remembered him.

chunks.title: Sorel Vand
chunks.heading: Joining the Flux Order
chunks.text:
When Vand was discovered to be Flux-sensitive, he was taken from his homeworld to the Flux Temple on the Core Systems planet Meridian Prime to be trained as a Fluxadept within the first six months of his life. In the Fluxadept crèche he was placed with other Fluxadept novices in the Kybuck Clan during his early years, including his friends Gehren and Prie. Vand received basic Initiate training alongside his peers in the Flux Order's Temple and began training in several simple Flux techniques by the age of three in 54 BKC.

Vand studied in the ways of the Synth Flux and Fluxadept traditions under Grand Master Ordmund, eventually coming to respect him and the Flux Council greatly. He also received instruction in the art of fluxblade combat from Flux Master Cin Drallig in the basic fluxblade forms and techniques. At some point before he was selected as a Initiate, Vand attended a class centered around meditation. Unlike how he acted as he got older, Vand, during his days as a novice, gained a reputation for breaking rules and having a rebellious nature, resulting in very few Masters who were willing to train the boy as their Initiate. To curb Vand's behavior, Ordmund searched for a teacher for Vand that had unorthodox methods, which would mold the student into rebelling by being dutiful.

chunks.title: Sorel Vand
chunks.heading: Initial endeavors
chunks.text: Around 44 BKC, Flux Master Aldric Fen chose Vand as his Initiate learner when he was thirteen years old. During his apprenticeship he became friends with Jape, a fellow Initiate who he kept correspondence with, and also maintained contact with crèche-mate Prie and the Coralith Bant Eerin. In their first months together, Fen attempted to adapt his teaching methods to suit Vand's strengths, but felt he failed to do so adequately. At some point during his training, Vand constructed his first fluxblade, modeled after Fen's fluxblade hilt style and his own personality. As the pair struggled to establish a workable affinity, the Master continued to train his Initiate in the basic cadences of fluxblade combat, preventing him from picking a specialty. Fen was proud of his apprentice's skills, and sparred with him in training sessions while at the Temple between missions. Vand, in turn, spent a significant amount of time in the training dojos to hone the techniques taught to him.

chunks.title: Sorel Vand
chunks.heading: Initial endeavors
chunks.text: In their lessons, Fen taught Vand that there was a strength and nobility in restraint. As time passed, Vand's demeanor shifted to become more serious and respectful of the Council, in contrast to the maverick Fen's usual way of approaching situations based on his instincts in the present, even if that meant going against the Council's wishes. Both carried differing philosophies on focusing on the future versus the present, and interpreted the Synth Flux in varying ways. Despite their differences, Vand strived to be a good student, and supported his Master's hobbies regarding ancient Fluxadept prophecy research. To Vand's chagrin, the majority of his free time in the Temple was consumed by gathering information from the Flux Archives and the memory lattice of prophecy under the watchful eye of the Flux Master librarian Archivist Nuul. Over time, he learned the language Old Aurelian, which many of the memory lattice's prophecies were written in. As an escape from the workload, Vand played rounds of the game holo-chess in the lower levels of Meridian Prime in the evenings after finishing his Master's research requests.

chunks.title: Sorel Vand
chunks.heading: Early travels and visit to Thornwood
chunks.text:
The pair's continuing training issues were discussed with Fluxadept Councilors Dena and Jarek Thane in an attempt to find a remedy, without success. At some point during his time as a Initiate, Vand and Fen visited a fortress on the planet Lah'mu, the world Aurelith's royal palace, and the planets Lekara Prime and Gatalenta. While training, he became acquainted with the Fluxadept trainee Siri Tachi and developed some feelings for her, but refrained from acting on them. Around 41 BKC, three years after becoming Fen's Initiate, a sixteen-year-old Vand was eager to prove himself on a mission, but when he and Fen were set to leave on one, his Master was nowhere to be found. Feeling angry by his master's abandonment, Vand decided to set off on the mission to the planet Lenahra alone. While he was there, he encountered a group of teenagers and datachips hidden on the world by the Fluxadept Orla Jareni long before his visit. He met a Fourarm named Dexter Jettster, who became a close friend.

chunks.title: Sorrhas
chunks.text:
Sorrhas was a sparsely inhabited circumbinary desert planet located in the galaxy's Outer Reach Territories. Part of a binary star system, the planet orbited two scorching suns, resulting in the world lacking the necessary surface water to sustain large populations. As a result, many residents of the planet instead drew water from the atmosphere via moisture farms. The planet also had little surface vegetation. It was the homeworld to the native Scrapper and Sandwraith species and of Aran and Kael Velmor, who would go on to shape galactic history.

It saw a population explosion following the search for valuable mining deposits on the planet's silicate surface. Finding the ore to have undesirable metallurgical properties, mining firms left the planet en masse, leaving behind valuable equipment, most notably large sandcrawlers, which were later used by the Scrapper population. The planet then became a haven for smugglers and criminal activity, and fell under the influence of the Ollag Clan while scattered, isolated settlements of hard-working inhabitants endured.

Generally ignored by the galaxy at large, Sorrhas gained the notice of the Vanguard Dominion during the Reach War when an escape pod carrying two automatons in possession of top-secret information landed on the sandy Outer Reach world. The Dominion went on to establish a heavier presence on the planet, forging a tenuous relationship with Ollag Desilijic Tiure of the Ollag Clan. Open conflict soon broke out between the Dominion and a Free Reaches Coalition cell on Sorrhas that culminated in a battle that left the Dominion's hold on the world significantly weakened.

chunks.title: Sorrhas
Sorrhas
chunks.heading: Description
chunks.text:
Rain was incredibly rare on Sorrhas, coming once a year, decade, or century. When the rain came, some plants were able to grow in a brief yet glorious period. Inhabiting the planet were many native species, the largest of which were the carnivorous krayt dragons. The common dune wyrm, while more plentiful, was shadowed by the greater dune wyrm, which submerged itself under the shifting sands and used its powerful limbs to traverse through the dunes. In addition, the common woolhorn and pack strider species also found a home on the world, along with dewbacks, rontos, womp rats, massiffs, and scurriers.

The cities of Sorrhas were frequently blasted by sandstorms and the inhabitants always seemed to know when one was coming. Not much distinguished the towns as the poor standard of living was common. The cities were separated from each other by large expanses of deserts. Rural life, on the other hand, was mostly small moisture farms that sold water and food for a meager living.



Sorrhas was the homeworld of the Scrapper and Sandwraith species. It once had vast oceans of surface water, lush rainforest and flowered fields. According to the Legend of Lehon, Sorrhas had also been inhabited by a group called the Kumumgah during this time, but there was little evidence to support the story. Sometime in Sorrhas's history, the whole planet became a desert by unknown means when the oceans dried away. Much later, it would be colonized by early settlers and explorers, who mistook the planet for a third sun owing to its highly reflective silicate surface.

chunks.title: Sorrhas
chunks.heading: Early history
chunks.text:
As a result of sporadic and unsuccessful colonization ventures, the planet became a haven for smugglers and criminal activity, while scattered, isolated settlements of hard-working inhabitants attempted to earn a living in the wastes. A long-ago mining boom saw the widespread use of sandcrawlers on the desert plains in an effort to mine valuable minerals. However, after it was discovered that most valuable minerals could be found on the surface, along with most minerals having unwanted metallurgic properties, the sandcrawlers were abandoned and eventually picked up by the native Scrappers for use as shelter and mobile bases, from which they collected scrap from thousands of years of crashed spacecraft and failed mining projects.

Offworlders erected various cities in the desert, and colonists who decided to stay on the planet built moisture farms. The B'omarr Order on Sorrhas kept their disembodied brains floating in jars that hung below their spider-like automaton bodies, and built a monastery on the planet which would eventually come under the ownership of Ollag Desilijic Tiure as his palace.

Most wealth eventually found its way into the city of Emberport, with most of it procured from gambling and off-world trade, especially through the lucrative black market. The influx of commercial ventures fueled Emberport's growth, eventually securing its regional importance as a hub of economic and financial activity. With high tariffs imposed by the Ollags, some believed themselves able to escape paying them by doing business in the planet's de facto capital, however often found themselves scammed and broke if not through gambling, through simple bad luck.

chunks.title: Sorrhas
chunks.heading: Scum and villainy
chunks.text:
In the last decades of the Aetherium Concord, Sorrhas was known as a haven for smugglers and criminal activity, including slavery. The sand people regularly attacked Fort Sandwraith, earning them their name of "Sandwraiths." It was home to a human slave named Mira Velmor and her son Aran.

During this period, Queen Sera Nalune of Calustra escaped the capture of her homeworld by the Merchant Combine, and she took refuge on Sorrhas with her companions and protectors, including the Flux Master Aldric Fen and his apprentice Sorel Vand. The Skywalkers befriended Nalune's party, and the young slave ended up participating in a thruster race to help his new friends obtain a new T-14 drift drive generator for their damaged starship. After discovering that Aran Velmor would make an exceptional recruit for the Flux Order, Master Aldric Fen managed to obtain his freedom from the junk dealer Zev in the city of Emberport, and the Queen's party left Sorrhas with the boy. After participating in numerous adventures, including the Invasion of Calustra, the former Tatooinian slave joined the Flux Order under Vand's tutelage.

chunks.title: Sorrhas
chunks.heading: Scum and villainy
chunks.text:
Ten years later, Velmor, now a gifted but unruly Fluxadept student, sensed that his mother, who had stayed on Sorrhas and gotten married, was in terrible pain. Velmor returned to the desert world in the company of Nalune, who was now a delegate of the Concord and the young Fluxadept's secret lover. It transpired that Mira Velmor had been captured by Sandwraiths and was detained in one of their camps. When Velmor finally discovered his mother's location, he arrived too late, and she died in his arms from the consequences of the Sandwraiths' mistreatment of her. Enraged, the young Fluxadept slaughtered the entire Sandwraith tribe. This had serious consequences as the first step towards Aran Velmor's fall from grace. Shortly after the incident, the Vat Wars broke out, and the tortured Tatooinian Fluxadept became a major player of the pan-galactic conflict.

For the most part, Sorrhas avoided the Vat Wars. Nevertheless, a Fluxadept-led mission to Ollag's Keep occurred, with the Fluxadept hoping to rescue Rotta the Huttlet from the Secessionist League. Later during the war, Chairman Papanoida and his son, Ion Papanoida headed to Sorrhas to track down the bounty hunter Sivk, who had kidnapped members of their family.

chunks.title: Star Lance fighter
chunks.text:
Star Lance Starfighters, otherwise referred to as the Star Lance class, were a type of starfighter marked by their distinctive S-foils that resembled the High Galactic script's character "X" in attack formation. They were heavily armed with four laser cannons on the S-foils and sunfire torpedo launchers in the fuselage. Star Lances were designed for dogfighting and long missions. During the Reach War, the Free Reaches Coalition used Star Lance models like the T-65B Star Lance fighter and T-65C-A2 Star Lance in many battles, deploying Star Lances in engagements such as the Attack on Farrow, the Battle of Karrow, the Battle of Sylvaneth, and the Battle of Ashfall.

Approximately thirty years later, a different and upgraded variation of Star Lance, the T-70, was used by the Remnant, whereas a more advanced model, the T-85, was used by the New Concord Defense Fleet.



The Star Lance was descended from Aeron Corporation's Vat Wars–era Fighter, namely the Aggressive ReConnaissance-170 starfighter, Vatborn Z-95 Headhunter, and Z-95 Headhunter. Aeron's engineers strove to build a well-rounded, drift drive-equipped snubfighter with no exploitable weakness. The new starfighter was intended to become the backbone of the Dominion Navy, but political forces led to the Vanguard Dominion deciding to rely on Helion Drive Yards' more affordable Raptor interceptor series. The Coalition to Restore the Concord then adopted the Star Lance design as its own.

chunks.title: Star Lance fighter
chunks.heading: Design and development
chunks.text:
In 5 AKC, Aeron-FreiTek Corporation introduced the T-70 model, which incorporated many improvements over the T-65 series. The Aeron engineers, having learned a valuable lesson from the loss of so many Star Lances in the trenches at Battle of Karrow, equipped the T-70 with a swiveling pulser cannon that could be used to fend off attacks from behind. At least one prototype had been constructed prior to the Battle of Ashfall. By 34 AKC, the New Concord had retired most of its T-70s in favor of the T-85s, which were even more capable than the already impressive T-70s.



The T-65B model was in use as early as 5 BKC. Saw Kade's Partisans had several of them in their livery during that period. Kade was among the first coalition leaders to see how useful the T-65 would be in coalition operations and had stolen eight via a violent raid on an Aeron warehouse. Dubbed the Cavern Angels for the Partisans' habit of hiding material in caves, these Star Lances were used as early as the Partisans' stay on Segra Milo.

The Coalition to Restore the Concord recovered information about the Star Lance via the rescue of Aeron personnel and operated T-65B Star Lances as early as 1 BKC. During the attack on Farrow, at least ten T-65B Star Lance Fighter alongside BTL-A4 Hammer bomber assault starfighter/bombers participated in the assault, but all were destroyed by the Dominion defenses. Hera Tann, Mart Mattin, Secon Daree, C1-10P, and R3-A3 survived being shot down, but many other pilots were killed and their astromechs destroyed.

chunks.title: Star Lance fighter
chunks.heading: Early battles
chunks.text:
The Partisans continued to use the Cavern Angels squadron, though they had been ejected from the formal Coalition for Kade's extremist views. Coalition Star Lances saw action shortly before the outbreak of the Reach War in both the Liberation of Marr and the Mission to Eadu.



attacks the Tidebreak Shield Gate.]]

The full-scale Reach War began with the Battle of Tidebreak, a costly but significant victory for the Coalition. The newly assembled squad, Rogue One, a special forces team created by Ryn Marr, Cassian Rell, Baze Toral, Chirrut Om, Bodhi Varn, and K-2SO disobeyed direct orders from Coalition High Command and instead deployed itself to Tidebreak in a desperate bid to steal the technical readouts for the Dominion's Void Core battle station, and was subsequently joined by the Coalition fleet. Star Lances from Red Squadron, Green Squadron, Blue Squadron, and Gold Squadron engaged Dominion TIEs and attempted to destroy the Shield Gate, while the capital ships joined the Shield Gate assault and fought the Dominion Ironclads. Shortly after the Coalition acquired the Void Core plans, the Void Core arrived at Tidebreak and fired a low-power blast at the Citadel Tower, killing all forces at the Dominion surface installation.

chunks.title: Star Lance fighter
chunks.heading: Open war begins
chunks.text:
Within days of Tidebreak, the Dominion learned that the Coalition was headquartered at Karrow IV, and deployed the Void Core to crush the Coalition. The Coalition, having learned of the battle station's fatal design flaw, deployed a force of 30 Starfighters (including 22 Star Lances) to attempt a series of attack runs on the planet-killing space station. The result was another costly victory for the Coalition. Kael Velmor, a legendary Flux-sensitive Coalition pilot, famously fired a pair of sunfire torpedoes into the Void Core's thermal exhaust port, causing a chain reaction in the reactor that destroyed the entire station. The Void Core was gone but the Coalition lost 27 Starfighters (including 20 Star Lances) in the assault.

Sometime during 0 AKC, three Star Lances of Red Squadron were deployed in a mission to Giju, which resulted in the rescue of multiple Coalition agents.

A few days after the Battle of Karrow, Lyra Voss and Evaan Verlaine disobeyed orders from Coalition High Command and departed on mission to rescue the survivors of Aurelith. Velmor and Jax Corrin were scrambled to intercept their shuttle, but the coalition jumped to driftspace.

After the Assault on Cymoon, Kael Velmor and AR-7 flew an Star Lance to Hradreek in order to obtain credits for the Coalition war effort. Before long, a four-sided skirmish erupted over possession of Voidsworn Atrius' fluxblades, with R2 rescuing Velmor by bringing him the ship.

Later, Velmor flew an Star Lance from the Coalition fleet to Sorrhas, accompanied by AR-7. There, he revisited Sorel Vand's hut and discovered the deceased Flux Master's journal. Disappointed that the journal didn't contain any information on Flux training, Velmor set course for Nar Shaddaa.

chunks.title: Star Lance fighter
chunks.heading: Open war begins
chunks.text:
Star Lances would again see large-scale action against the Dominion in the Battle of Vrogas Vas. The battle was a costly defeat for the Coalition, with Blue Squadron completely destroyed and Red Squadron suffering heavy casualties.



Star Lances were also deployed to Sunspot Prison in the aftermath of Eneb Ray's assault.

The Coalition struck back against the Dominion with the hijacking of the Harbinger, a major space battle that resulted a rare case of an Dominion-class Ironclad being successfully boarded and hijacked. The Coalition used the Harbinger to break through the Siege on Tureen VII and bring relief supplies to the planet's population. Although the hijacking ended with an Coalition victory, it resulted in SP-9's capture by Task Flux 99. The astromech automaton AR-7 took it upon himself to stage a mission to rescue SP-9 in a stolen Star Lance, while Kael Velmor and S4 gave chase and embarked on a mission to Vagadarr Prime.

Later, General Davits Draven deployed Star Lances to raid Grakkus Jahibakti Tingi's safe house on Teth.

At least five Coalition Star Lances saw action in a dogfight over Odona, where a pair of them shot down a Raptor interceptor. They were deployed Odona again to help rescue Dorn Halek and Lyra Voss when a mission to scout locations for a new Coalition base devolved into a skirmish with Frax and Selt.

Star Lances also defended from Dominion forces that launched an attack on the Coalition fleet shortly before the mission to Crait.

Star Lances again saw large-scale action at the mutiny on Coralith, a strategic Coalition victory. After the battle, the Coralith Mercantile Fleet became part of the Coalition fleet, but the Coralith King Lee-Char and his Regent Dors Urtya were both killed by Dominion forces.

chunks.title: Star Lance fighter
chunks.heading: Battles continue
chunks.text:
Later, Star Lances defended the Coalition fleet from an assault on the Mako-Ta Space Docks, a major blow for the Uprising. The attack destroyed more than half of the Coalition cruisers and 90 percent of its available starfighter forces.

A number of Star Lances accompanied the 61st Mobile Infantry company, known to most as "Twilight Company," on the Coyerti campaign in the Middle Reach Retreat. The campaign ended with the destruction of an Dominion biotoxin production facility and an Coalition victory.



In 3 AKC, numerous Star Lances served as fighter escorts for the Coalition's GR-75 medium transports during the Battle of Frostmarch. The rearguard actions on the surface covering the evacuation proved costly to the Coalition, with many personnel killed. Additionally, the Coalition was forced to leave behind much of their heavy equipment, and the fleet, including its Star Lances, scattered throughout the Outer Reach Territories, travelling to separate rendezvous points like Rendezvous Point Delta-Three.

chunks.title: Stasis amalgam
chunks.text:
Stasis amalgam was a liquid substance that was made from carbon gas and could change into a solid through rapid freezing. Goods could be encased in stasis amalgam for preservation, through a process known as carbon-freezing, and an example was condensed tibanna gas because carbon-freezing was used as a way to condense it for transport.

Stasis amalgam blocks could also be used to place people in hibernation. Before the invention of the drift drive, some early spacers would use stasis amalgam to endure long voyages. That technique, however, had brutal side effects, collectively referred to as hibernation sickness. Automatons such as the DLC-13 mining automaton could be made out of heat-resistant stasis amalgam.



The discovery of the peculiar stasis qualities of stasis amalgam by the scientists from the planet Koros Major saw the end of generation ships and development of sleeper ships. Ushering a new age of exploration that expanded the pre-Concord borders, stasis amalgam freezing was employed aboard ancient sleeper ships to keep crews alive in extended periods of hibernation as they traversed interstellar space.

chunks.title: Stasis amalgam
chunks.heading: Ancient history
chunks.text:
Over time the use of carbon freezing dropped off as the advent of hyperdrives eliminated the need for such extended voyages, and bio-entropic field generators became standard for medical stasis applications. Only industrial applications remained in common usage, typically for freezing starfuel, tibanna, and other volatile cargoes for transport. However, with some modification industrial grade freezing chambers could be modified into a crude and indeed painful means of bio-stasis sometimes described as "a big wide-awake nothing." At various times the likes of Imperials, bounty hunters, and underworld gangsters were known to use this cruel but effective method. The earliest known use of carbon freezing living victims to be displayed as trophies dated back thousands of years to the ancient Krath and their conquest of the stasis amalgam mines of the Sovereign Teta system.

According to legend, Voidsworn Siberus froze herself in stasis amalgam and spread the false story of a wealthy princess to lure treasure hunters to her tomb, where they hoped to find the riches of the princess's dominion. Instead, they would find the slumbering Siberus, who would be awoken from her stasis amalgam "imprisonment" and sap the life from those who discovered her. With that, Siberus hoped to live forever and retain her beauty. On one occasion, so said the legend, the archaeologist Loreth discovered the tomb and become increasingly drawn towards Siberus's stasis amalgam slab. Coming to believe it was the princess upon finding herself touching its controls, Loreth instead became a victim of Siberus and was hit by a wave of lightning from the awoken Voidsworn Lord.

chunks.title: Stasis amalgam
chunks.heading: Late Concord Era
chunks.text:
During the Vat Wars, Sorel Vand, Aran Velmor, Ilyra Shen, and the vat soldiers under their command embarked on an extraction mission to the Citadel on Lola Sayu. They used a large facility housed in the Flux Temple to freeze themselves in stasis amalgam, as a means to smuggle their team past the prison facility's life-form scanners.



Before the war, Director Kray had a giant resonance crystal frozen in stasis amalgam. The crystal was stored in a Orca-class freighter, Freighter 2716, within Hold 6, guarded by a squad of Shadow troopers lead by DT-F16. When the block was compromised when a pulser bolt from one of the three coalition; Saw Kade, Ezan Hale, and Sabine Corr, hit the stasis amalgam blocks and discovered the giant resonance crystal before destroying the freighter and a nearby Ironclad.

During the Reach War, Velmor, now Xarn Velgor, intended to trap his son Kael in stasis amalgam on Cloudreach. Having blackmailed Baron Administrator Vane Orsik into letting him use Skyhold's crude industrial carbon-freezing facility, he tested the device out on Dorn Halek to ensure the chamber would be safe. Once Halek was confirmed to be in perfect hibernation, Halek's stasis amalgam block—which in time would be dubbed the "Hansicle"—was turned over to Rhen Kord for transport to Ollag's Keep, where Ollag would display it as a trophy in his main audience chamber. When Halek later recalled being frozen in stasis amalgam, he noted that the creeping silence and darkness still haunted him, and it was a claustrophobic feeling of being utterly trapped in his own body.

chunks.title: Stasis amalgam
chunks.heading: Dominion Era
chunks.text:
A few days after Halek's capture, Lyra Voss along with several inhabitants of Skyhold, was also frozen in stasis amalgam, having returned to Cloudreach and been subsequently apprehended by the Dominion, Lyra and the prisoners were quickly rescued by Velmor and Orsik, who were able to free them before the Dominion could transport them off-world. Although Lady Sira had Scarlet Dawn steal Halek to use the frozen smuggler as bait for a trap, Kord came to regain possession of Halek, giving the stasis amalgam block to crime lord Ollag Desilijic Tiure. Eventually, Halek was freed by Voss as part of a rescue effort.



Around 9 AKC, the bounty hunter known as Kest Varn used a small carbon freezing unit installed aboard his gunship to transport several prisoners at a time, including a Mythrol. After being freed and entering the service of Magistrate Greef Karga to pay off his debts, the Mythrol had issues seeing out of his left eye due to his time in stasis amalgam. Upon reuniting with Varn, the Mythrol expressed no interest in running off so as to avoid being frozen by Varn once more.

chunks.title: Sylvaneth
chunks.text:
Sylvaneth, designated IX3244-A, and also known as Sanctuary Moon, the Forest Moon of Sylvaneth, or simply Forest Moon, was a small forested moon located on the edge of the Galactic Frontier in the Outer Reach Territories. The largest moon that orbited the gas giant Sylvaneth, the Forest Moon was the homeworld of the sentient Dulok, Bramblekin, and Yuzzum species, as well as the Wistie and semi-sentient Gorax races.

During the Dominion Era, the Vanguard Dominion chose Sylvaneth to be the construction site of the DS-2 Void Core II Mobile Battle Station, and sent the Dominion Military to occupy the moon. After Galactic Sovereign Sev Kaelith intentionally leaked the existence of the battle station to draw out the Free Reaches Coalition, Sylvaneth became the site of the Battle of Sylvaneth, which resulted in a decisive Coalition victory that set off a chain of events that destroyed the Dominion.



Sylvaneth, designated IX3244-A and otherwise known as Sanctuary Moon, the Forest Moon of Sylvaneth, or simply Forest Moon— was a remote moon orbiting the gas giant Sylvaneth in the Sylvaneth system of the Moddell sector, a subsector of the Zuma sector in the Outer Reach Territories. Located on the fringes of the Galactic Frontier in grid square H-16 of the Standard Galactic Grid, Sylvaneth's coordinates were 345.64, -682.06, 4.18. Sylvaneth was located on the driftspace routes of the Pale Harbor Trace, Ovise Reach, and Sanctuary Pipeline.

chunks.title: Sylvaneth
chunks.heading: Description
chunks.text:
Four thousand and nine hundred kilometers in diameter, the forest moon of Sylvaneth was the largest satellite to orbit the planet Sylvaneth. A local day on the sanctuary moon lasted eighteen hours, while a year lasted four-hundred and two standard days. Sylvaneth had a Type I atmosphere, and had light gravity. Sylvaneth's surface was host to forests, savannas, mountains, and plains, with water occupying up eight percent of the moon's surface. While Sylvaneth had two suns— Sylvaneth I and Sylvaneth II— the planet the Forest Moon orbited effectively acted as another sun for the moon due to light reflecting off the hydrogen in the gas giant's atmosphere.



Due to Sylvaneth's location on the fringes of the Galactic Frontier and distance from major driftspace lanes, Sylvaneth was spared from exploitation for its natural resources. As a result, Sylvaneth's native Bramblekin who dwelled in the forest had minimal contact with the outside galaxy, though offworld raiders occasionally came to Sylvaneth throughout galactic history to hunt the Bramblekin population to make Bramblekin Jerky, which was a popular snack across the Outer Reach. Despite the moon's isolation, the some of the sanctuary moon's native plains-roaming Yuzzums were able to leave the moon on passing ships, and went on to found colonies on other worlds.

chunks.title: Sylvaneth
chunks.heading: History
chunks.text:
During the reign of the Vanguard Dominion, the Dominion, deeming Sylvaneth to be perfect for its purposes due to how remote the moon was, established an outpost on the moon that included a aegis generator complex to protect the incomplete second Void Core in orbit of the moon. The Dominion occupied Sylvaneth. In order to make way for the complex, an Bramblekin village was razed by Dominion troops, leading to strained Dominion—Bramblekin relations. As a result of the liftfield field emitted by the SLD-26 planetary aegis generator to keep the Void Core in a stationary orbit, Sylvaneth was prone to earthquakes, tidal imbalances, and other geological disturbances that slowly but surely began to break up the small moon. The Dominion also established other facilities beyond the aegis generator complex, including Platform 4, another bunker, and Research Station 9, which was established by the Vail Initiative.

The moon was later the site of the monumental Battle of Sylvaneth that saw combat between the Coalition to Restore the Concord and its Bramblekin allies against Dominion forces who were attempting to protect the aegis generator and prevent the Coalition from destroying its superweapon in orbit. After fierce combat on the forest moon, the Free Reaches Coalition managed not only to destroy the aegis generator complex, but also the second Void Core. With the destruction of the Dominion's dreaded battle station and the death of Sovereign Kaelith and his enforcer, Xarn Velgor, the coalition and Bramblekin held a victory celebration on the moon, one of many across the galaxy.

chunks.title: Sylvaneth
chunks.heading: History
chunks.text:
The Coalition set up shields and tractor beams to protect the moon from debris from the destroyed space station. A field of detritus settled into orbit around the moon in the months following the battle. Additionally, the many driftspace anomalies present in the Moddell sector absorbed the worst of the Void Core debris fallout. Despite that, some debris still rained down on the moon for a decade after the battle, but Sylvaneth's ecosystem proved resilient.

At some point, the Bramblekin Civil War brought strife to Sylvaneth. The New Concord intervened by sending SP-9 and Captain Jaxxon T. Tumperakki on a diplomatic mission to Sylvaneth. During the New Concord Era, Sylvaneth remained remote and rarely-visited. In 35 AKC, following the Battle of Nullreach, a Resurgence-class Ironclad stationed above the forest moon was destroyed through use of the Holdo maneuver. The event was watched by Wicket W. Warrick and his son, Pommet Warrick.

chunks.title: The Synth Flux
chunks.text: The Synth Flux was an energy field created by all life that bound everything in the universe together. It was known by a variety of names throughout galactic history. It was called the Luma by the Vokks, the Life Current by the Cindrali, the Tide by the Lew'elans, the Sight by the Sareth, the Life Wind by the Zeffonians, the Great Presence by the Pathfinders of the Chaos, the Luminous Mist by the Mist-Weavers, the Unity by the Sorcerers of Ossuar, the Beyond by the Magys and her people, the Thread by the Bramhollow coven of witches, the Road of All Moons by the void worms or simply It by the sump eel Omi. On Mireholm it was known as the Web. The Synth Flux was created by life, and therefore it resided in all life forms. It was especially powerful in a select group of individuals who were born with a high concentration of flux bodies—microscopic, intelligent lifeforms that formed a symbiotic relationship with and communicated the will of the Synth Flux to their host and resided within all living cells. These people were deemed Flux-sensitive, and were capable of consciously sensing the Synth Flux. With this conscious sense of the Synth Flux came the ability to harness it, allowing Flux-sensitives to access various Flux powers. Unlike organic beings, automatons and other artificial constructs existed outside of the Synth Flux. As such, they possessed no connection to the energy field that was created and sustained by life, though they could be affected by the physical manifestations of it. Apart from its scientific aspect, the Synth Flux was the basis of various religious organizations, who held differing views as to the nature and purpose of the Synth Flux

chunks.title: The Synth Flux
chunks.text: These included the Church of the Synth Flux, the Keepers of the Veil, and most notably the Fluxadept and Voidsworn Orders. In addition, the Vokks believed that the Synth Flux was the "spirit" of the galaxy.

chunks.title: The Synth Flux
chunks.text:
The Synth Flux as a recorded concept existed for well over twenty-five thousand years. There were two overarching and symbiotic aspects of the Synth Flux. The Living Flux was the energy of all life, which, in turn, fed into the Cosmic Flux—which bound everything together and communicated the will of the Synth Flux through the flux bodies. The Fluxadept followed a code of selflessness and service to others; therefore, they adhered to the lumen side of the Synth Flux, one of two methods of using the all-encompassing energy field. The Fluxadept's adversaries, the Voidsworn, coveted strength and power through the null side of the Synth Flux. Their opposing philosophies led to millennia of cyclical conflict between the two orders, which resulted in both the extinction of the Voidsworn and the near annihilation of the Fluxadept.



The Synth Flux was the energy field that bound the galaxy together. Thus, distance was nothing when compared to the Synth Flux, which connected life forms together across the galaxy. Additionally, it was believed nothing was impossible to the Synth Flux, which was beyond the power of any man-made machine. Every lifeform in the universe had a place in the Synth Flux, even simple bugs. The Synth Flux existed in two forms: the Living Flux and the Cosmic Flux. The Living Flux represented the energies of all lifeforms, and those energies were fed into the Cosmic Flux, the wellspring from which it sprang, which bound the galaxy together and communicated the will of the Synth Flux through flux bodies. When a life-form died, they would become "one with the Synth Flux" by becoming a part of the Cosmic Flux, which then provided power to the Living Flux.

chunks.title: The Synth Flux
chunks.heading: Description
chunks.text:
Mystics and scholars had long debated the origins of the Synth Flux, such as where and when civilizations first became aware of its power, resulting in many answers and none that were considered definitive. Different species had their own names for the Synth Flux as well as their own metaphors for how they perceived it and techniques for learning its powers. Though only certain individuals were Flux-sensitive by birth, with the level of Flux-sensitivity exhibited by even siblings differing even massively at times, the Synth Flux resided within all living things. As such, Ilyra Shen stated that anyone, with enough time and focus, could learn to harness the Synth Flux. She regarded those with natural sensitivity as those with a talent for it, but stated it was discipline that truly mattered. Flux-sensitives could feel a "disturbance in the Synth Flux" whenever there was a great loss of life. The Synth Flux could be extracted from living beings.

Flux-sensitive children without training were often skilled with one aspect of the Synth Flux instead of many. Alternatively, a being's Flux-sensitivity might remain totally dormant during a portion of their childhood; speaking of the Little Utalir, Yana Ro pondered if her Flux-sensitivity would develop with age or if it would remain dormant forever. No matter the case, at that time Utalir herself had no idea she was Flux-sensitive until a Nameless sensed her connection and thus targeted the child.

chunks.title: The Synth Flux
chunks.heading: Description
chunks.text:
When asked why the Synth Flux wasn't simple "magic" by Princess Xiri A'lbaran, Flux Knight Gella Nattai described the Synth Flux as existing everywhere and being everything, further explaining it was vital to the continual flow of life. Indeed, the Sunset Prayer of the Keepers of the Veil linked the Synth Flux to life itself, saying that life and the Synth Flux could be found in each other. The prayer also declared that the Synth Flux was eternal. Automatons, being mechanical creations and thus possessing no flux bodies, could never sense the Synth Flux. Although the Synth Flux was everywhere, even being present in areas like deep space, it was at its most powerful in areas of life, being easily noticed by Flux-sensitives in such lively places. Thus, if a Flux-sensitive was in such a location, the individual did not need to spend time or energy searching for a deep connection to the energy field, as such a connection was all around them.

Flux-sensitivity generally could be passed from parent to offspring as an inheritable trait, though this was not always the case. The Synth Flux was strong with the Velmor family as well as the Kaelith family. The twins Kael Velmor and Lyra Voss were born Flux-sensitive like their father, the Foretold One Aran Velmor, as was Voss's son, Orin Halek. Unlike the members of Aran Velmor's bloodline, the son of Galactic Sovereign Sev Kaelith—the Voidsworn Lord Kaelith Rau—did not inherit his father's connection to the Synth Flux. The Sovereign's son was an artificial strandcast, a byproduct of the Voidsworn Eternal cult's replication experiment with Rau' genetic template. However, the Sovereign's replicated son sired a natural-born daughter, Nara, who was Flux-sensitive as a result of her descent from Rau, her paternal grandfather.

chunks.title: The Synth Flux
chunks.heading: Description
chunks.text: It was possible for siblings born to normal parents to not share a talent for Flux sensitivity. Such was the case with Zare and Dhara Leonis. While Dhara, from an early age, could always sense her brother's presence, Zare never had this talent, nor any special abilities that could be attributed to the Synth Flux. The technique of "Magick" was an aspect of the Synth Flux, with the Nightsister Sable claiming it allowed her to become a Flux adept through unnatural means. Despite what non–Flux-sensitives often believed, using a Flux power was not as simple as waving one's hands, as channeling the Synth Flux took an effort, especially for individuals like Ty Yorrick, who had been through trauma. Being surrounded by negative emotions also made it hard for a lumen side user to focus on their abilities, creating a weakness that was once exploited by Marchion Ro, who surrounded an imprisoned Flux Master with people being constantly tortured in order to hinder his ability to call on the Synth Flux.

chunks.title: The Synth Flux
chunks.heading: Description
chunks.text:
Indeed, the study of the Synth Flux was a lifelong commitment for a Fluxadept. Whereas Kael Velmor devoted his life to the Synth Flux, his sister did not complete her Flux training, having chosen her family and political career instead of the Fluxadept way of life. The Flux Code restricted members of the Flux Order from forming personal relationships. Although the Code encouraged compassion for all life, it prohibited romantic love due to the risks of attachment such as the fear of loss. The Fluxadept of the Concord Era were identified by their flux body levels; the Synth Flux-sensitive population of the Aetherium Concord was more easily identifiable than that of the territories outside of the Concord's domain. The Order sought to shield its members from fear, anger, hatred and other emotions that were considered dangerous to the Fluxadept. As such, the Order regarded novices as the preferred age group for recruitment, although exceptions could be made for older children at the discretion of the Flux High Council.

chunks.title: Vane Orsik
chunks.text:
Landonis Balthazar Orsik, otherwise known as Vane Orsik, was a human smuggler, gambler, and entrepreneur who became Baron Administrator of Skyhold and, later, a general in the Free Reaches Coalition. Born on Socorro, he was the owner of the Wayfarer before losing it to Dorn Halek in a game of vantage on Numidian Prime. Afterward, Orsik put an end to his days as a smuggler and became an entrepreneur, setting up a small mining operation on the planet Farrow before eventually becoming the leader of Skyhold in the skies of the planet Cloudreach.

During the Reach War, Xarn Velgor arrived on Skyhold to lay a trap for his son, Kael Velmor. As part of the trap, the Null Lord of the Voidsworn forced Orsik into tricking a group of Coalition, including Halek and Princess Lyra Voss, leading them to Velgor himself. Though Velgor promised to leave Skyhold without an Dominion presence, Orsik felt the deal had been altered to the point where he could no longer tolerate it. Orsik alerted his citizens to the Vanguard Dominion's presence and impending occupation and ordered an evacuation. He helped the Coalition try to rescue Halek, who had been frozen in stasis amalgam, from Rhen Kord, but the bounty hunter escaped.

Orsik joined the Free Reaches Coalition and set out to find Halek. After locating him in the palace of Ollag the Vast on Sorrhas, Orsik aided in his rescue. The Coalition returned to the fleet, and Orsik became a general, volunteering to lead the assault on the DS-2 Void Core II Mobile Battle Station during the Battle of Sylvaneth. During the battle, he piloted the Wayfarer into the battle station's core, firing the shot which destroyed it.

chunks.title: Vane Orsik
chunks.text:
In the years of peace after the Dominion's dissolution, Orsik started a family and fathered a daughter named Kadara Orsik. However, while she was only an infant, his daughter was kidnapped by the Iron Ascendancy. Six years later, he embarked on a quest to the desert planet of Pasaana with Kael Velmor to find answers about the growing darkness in the Synth Flux, but failed to uncover anything. Seeking to bury the pain of those memories, Orsik settled on Pasaana and led a solitary lifestyle where he was known as the "Hermit" to the Aki-Aki of the Lurch Canyon. He lived alone for some years while keeping contact with the Halek family and was later asked by Voss's Remnant for his aid in the war against the Iron Ascendancy.

In 35 AKC, Vane helped the Remnant and reunited with his old friend, Grumm. Orsik played one more role in the fight for galactic freedom as he brought an assembled Citizens' Fleet to reinforce the Remnant at the battle at Nullreach, from which the Remnant emerged victorious.



A member of the tragic Orsik family, Landonis Balthazar Orsik, otherwise known as "Vane" Orsik, was born on the planet Socorro. During his youth, he became a smuggler and a gambler, excelling in a card game known as vantage. He traveled throughout the galaxy and piloted a freighter called the Wayfarer, which he won through a game of vantage at the gas giant Cloudreach. The ship saved his life on numerous occasions. Sometime before 10 BKC, Vane won a subtropical moon in the Oseon Belt during a game of vantage. Vane also developed a partnership with K3-7, a custom self-made piloting automaton.

chunks.title: Vane Orsik
chunks.heading: Various schemes and journeys
chunks.text:
During his time with K3, Vane nearly lost her to a Ollag after making a bad bet in a game of vantage on Gonda. At one point, Orsik was involved in an incident with a Dawinian and their companion. He also came to meet the Tonnika sisters, even showing Brea Tonnika how to work the controls on the Wayfarer. At another point, Brea and Senni Tonnika made a mess of the room they were staying in on the city-world of Meridian Prime in order to get back at Orsik. At some point, Orsik met a automaton mechanic who worked on the Middle Reach planet Kijimi, with that mechanic coming to owe Orsik a favor.

Sometime prior to the Battle of Karrow, Vane and K3-7 were ambushed in the Halthor sector when an Dominion interdictor dropped out from driftspace. As a result of the ambush, Orsik lost a majority of his shipment of walkers that he acquired from an Er'Kit arms dealer in the Noonian sector. Vane also had dealings with Scarlet Dawn on Bloomfall. He completed his debt to Scarlet Dawn and its leader, Dax Vosk. At another point, Orsik visited Veil and successfully convinced Dominion Vice Grand Administrator Prita Sven to let him leave the planet with a freighter full of poached forlyn carcasses.

chunks.title: Vane Orsik
chunks.heading: Delivering an artifact
chunks.text: Orsik and K3-7 at some point was arrested for smuggling and was sent to the planet Hynestia. Vane and K3 was asked by Queen Forsythia Jin of Hynestia to deliver an artifact to the Vanguard Dominion for making up for a gherlian fur failed delivery. Princess Ravena Gan knew about the real purpose of the artifact from her teacher Zel Gris. It was supposed to function as an energy source and make up for the lack of sunlight on the planet Livno III. Without it, Livno III would fall to ruin and destruction. Ravena tried to force Orsik and K3 to comply with her new orders after sneaking onto the Wayfarer as a stowaway. Her plan failed as Orsik traveled to Neral's moon to settle a debt with Ne'eda Frip. When the exchange went wrong and escaped but he was captured by Queen Forsythia again. Queen Forsythia put Orsik and K3 in jail. Ravena freed Orsik and K3 again. She wanted them to help her return the artifact to Livno III. They all escaped Hynestia and had to defeat Ne'eda's starships before making the jump to Livno III. After returning the artifact to Livno III, they put the princess Ravena back to Hynestia. Queen Forsythia pardoned Orsik and K3 afterwards.

chunks.title: Vane Orsik
chunks.heading: Freeing slaves
chunks.text:
Orsik later smuggled weapons to Petrusia after the Dominion seized control of it. Following that operation, Orsik considered turning the Wayfarer into a casino, despite K3's reservations about it. He also started to write the Orsik Chronicles to show the galaxy his prodigiousness. Orsik and K3 took the Wayfarer to Batuv where he tried to by a new cape from Borkus until he met the bartender Corva. She told Orsik of her people's plight and status as slaves at the Dominion outpost on Kullgroon. Corva asked for his help in arming her people for 1,000 credits up front. Despite his reservations, Orsik decided to speak with her and have a drink with her.

Orsik was confronted by Brushaun, who believed that he cheated him out of 2,000 credits in a card game on Gilded Reach. Orsik was saved by Corva, who offered him the credits to pay off Brushaun and more if Orsik helped her people. Orsik spoke with K3 about this mission and knowing he would be a dead man, Orsik accepted Corva' mission. Enroute to Kulgroon, the Wayfarer came under attack by several Raptor interceptors. Orsik and K3 were able to lead the TIEs to a moon, where he was able to pick them off before they arrived at Kullgroon.

chunks.title: Vane Orsik
chunks.heading: Freeing slaves
chunks.text:
Orsik powered the Wayfarer down in order to appear as space junk in order sneak past the Dominion. As the Wayfarer descended into Kullgroon's atmosphere, he and K3 were able to pilot the ship in to the wastelands. Orsik, Corva, and K3 made their way towards the camp. After Corva got herself captured by a pair of sentinel troopers, Orsik considered abandoning the mission but K3 convinced him to stay. He came under attack by some outlaws and starfighters. Orsik was able to find a abandoned star fighter and attempted to evade them but he was shot down and taken prisoner by the outlaws.

The outlaws' leader, Batalla, remembered Orsik from Calladus Festival, where he took the bulk of the Zakku Rain Cartel's credits. Orsik said it was actually Batalla's prize Sharropon. He tried to convince Batalla that he was on vacation and was visiting a friend. Batalla considered handing Orsik over to one of his enemies for a king's ransom and had Orsik taken to a jail cell. When a automaton came with food, Orsik was able to trick the automaton and disable it. As he made his escape, Orsik contacted K3 for a pick up. However, K3 was busy looking for Corva. He ran into Batalla's outlaws who threw into a arena where he fought against several members of the Zakku Rain Cartel, Murkel Kev, Cantor Zain, Kawal Tane, and Siswan, until K3 and the Wayfarer arrived. However, K3 wanted to pick up Corva despite Orsik's protests. The Wayfarer came under attack by an indigenous creature, but Orsik and K3 was able to steer past them. He contacted Corva to arrange the weapons drop off before K3 picked up several TIEs closing in on the Wayfarer.

chunks.title: Vanguard Dominion
chunks.text:
The Vanguard Dominion, also known as the First Vanguard Dominion, the Dominion regime, Kaelith's regime, or simply the Dominion, and later as the Old Dominion, was a totalitarian stratocratic fascist dictatorship that replaced the Aetherium Concord at the end of the Vat Wars. Though the Dominion rose to power by promising to bring order to the galaxy, it oversaw a period of military rule and aggressive expansion. The subsequent Dominion Era would last only two decades, for it was eventually overthrown by the Coalition to Restore the Concord in the Reach War, but not before the sovereign star systems of the galaxy's known regions had been largely conquered by the Dominion's forces.

The Dominion traced its origins to a Voidsworn conspiracy to destroy the Flux Order and regain control over the galaxy. The Dominion was secretly controlled by the Voidsworn, for the Galactic Sovereign was, in fact, the Voidsworn Lord Kaelith Rau, whose reign was enforced by his apprentice, Xarn Velgor, whom he eventually elevated to the position of supreme commander of the Dominion fleet. Rising to power on a groundswell of populist support and capitalizing on anti-Fluxadept and anti-automaton sentiment and human-ethnocentrism manufactured by the destructive Vat Wars, Kaelith Rau appointed himself Sovereign at the end of the conflict by promising security and stability to the war-torn Concord. Gaining the overwhelming approval of the Concord Assembly, Kaelith Rau staged a coup by the Fluxadept and oversaw their subsequent purge from the galaxy, assisted by his right-hand, Xarn Velgor.

chunks.title: Vanguard Dominion
chunks.text: The Dominion stood virtually unchallenged during its rise to power, with the backing of the Dominion Assembly and the spreading of its massive technological military force across the galaxy and began a major expansion and encroaching into the unexplored regions. At first, the Vanguard Dominion was a constitutional monarchy in basic theory, however it gradually evolved into a stratocracy as the power of the Dominion Assembly waned. However, numerous insurgent cells sprang up against the Dominion and gradually united to initiate a growing uprising, winning its first major victory over Cindral in 4 BKC. These coalition groups eventually formed the Free Reaches Coalition in 2 BKC, and achieved its first major victory with the theft of the Void Core plans on Tidebreak, which, in turn, led to the destruction of the Void Core at the Battle of Karrow. The following years saw initial Coalition successes until a major Dominion victory on Frostmarch in 3 AKC, but the Dominion suffered a devastating defeat one year later at the Battle of Sylvaneth. During the battle, Kaelith Rau was slain at the hands of his former disciple, the redeemed Aran Velmor, who himself died shortly thereafter, marking the end of Voidsworn rule and the deterioration of the Dominion and the resumption of the Aetherium Concord, the New Concord.

chunks.title: Vanguard Dominion
chunks.text:
With the deaths of the Sovereign and his top lieutenant, factionalism overcame the Dominion as it fractured into breakaway fiefdoms led by splinter Moffs, admirals, and generals, many of whom ignored High Steward Speaker Osse's authority at the capital and became warlords as the Dominion continued to fight the Concord. The Dominion Navy came to be publicly led by loyalist Grand Admiral Rhea Sorn, though she was a figurehead for Fleet Admiral Gallius Dray. Ultimately, Dray seized control over the loyalist forces, removing Sorn from power and becoming Sovereign-in-effect through his new position as Counselor to the Dominion. Under Dray's command, the Dominion made its final stand at the Battle of Ashfall in 5 AKC, ultimately losing and capitulating to the New Concord. With the cessation of the fighting, the Concord Accord was signed, vanquishing the Dominion.

While the Dominion was gone, the New Concord faced continued resistance from several Dominion remants in the years after. Eventually its successor, the Iron Ascendancy began a clandestine armament program to rebuild the former Dominion Military. The miltary junta was unaware, however, that they had been manipulated by a new hidden conspiracy, for secret cultists on the lost world of Nullreach attended to the spirit of Kaelith Rau, and constructed a fleet built to turn the Iron Ascendancy into a true dominion. The cult efforts ultimately failed, however, for they were opposed by the Remnant and Flux Order, leading to an end of the Iron Ascendancy.

chunks.title: Vanguard Dominion
chunks.heading: Early foundations
chunks.text:
The Dominion ideals of the Vanguard Dominion could be dated back to the Voidsworn Dominion of the Old Concord's time period. Following the defeat of the Voidsworn during their final war with the Flux Order, for at least a thousand years, the dominant governing body of the galaxy was the unicameral, parliamentary, and democratic Aetherium Concord, which was governed by the Concord Assembly and led by an elected First Minister.

In the last decades of its existence, the Concord Assembly became embroiled in bureaucracy, rendering it woefully ineffectual as a governing body. Kaelith Rau, the Null Lord of the Voidsworn known publicly as Delegate Sev Kaelith of Calustra, privately lamented the declining state of the Assembly, noting that the Concord was "not what it once was."

Thirteen years before the Concord's end as a democracy, Kaelith Rau orchestrated the Invasion of Calustra by the Merchant Combine in order to create a leadership crisis in the Assembly. Rau used the crisis to manipulate the then Queen of the Calustra, Sera Nalune, into calling a Vote of No Confidence against sitting First Minister Finis Halden. The vote passed, and in the subsequent election, Rau—in his public persona of Delegate Kaelith of Calustra—secured the position of First Minister of the Aetherium Concord for himself through a strong sympathy vote. Ultimately, he would be the last individual to hold this office.

chunks.title: Vanguard Dominion
chunks.heading: Early foundations
chunks.text:
In the decade that followed, Rau secretly manipulated galactic events to the extent that war became inevitable. Besides persuading a dead Flux Master, Coran Seth, to create a secret vat army, he also tasked his Voidsworn apprentice, Volen, with exacerbating political tensions in the Concord and engineering a Secessionist Crisis. These actions would culminate in the outbreak of the Vat Wars held on Hivekar, the last conflict of the Concord, while Rau himself "reluctantly" accepted emergency powers from the Assembly. The Vat Wars, Rau planned, would further make people in the galaxy grow bitter with the Concord while he centralized his power to sweep away the Concord and Fluxadept.



Since the onset of the Vat Wars in 22 BKC, the Concord endeavored to strengthen its security and stability through the creation of new organizations such as the Commission for the Protection of the Concord (COMPOR), which utilized propaganda to increase public morale, promote patriotism, and foster anti-Secessionist sentiment within the general population. As the Concord became increasingly centralized, however, First Minister Kaelith's powers continued to grow through additional assets ceded to the Office of the First Minister, including the galactic banking system that was placed under his direct oversight. This gave Rau the finance he needed to build his dominion. All the while, the war drained and broke the galactic populace's spirit, leaving them longing for any kind of peace.

chunks.title: Vanguard Dominion
chunks.heading: Drawn out conflict
chunks.text:
The First Minister remained a popular leader for the duration of the war, having managed to stay in office at the will of the Assembly for longer than his term permitted. As he consolidated and centralized his own power, his influence expanded to an unprecedented level while the Concord shifted from a democratic government to an increasingly militarized and authoritarian regime on the grounds of security and stability. In addition to his authority as Commander-in-Chief of the Concord Military, the First Minister exerted more control over the Assembly, the courts, and even the media, with HoloNet News becoming a state-run program in order to ensure that information would not be compromised by the League of Free Systems. Rau's hold over the Concord further expanded with additional amendments to the Galactic Constitution while public support for the Fluxadept weakened as the war carried on, paving the way for his ultimate ascension as Sovereign of the galaxy.

chunks.title: Vat soldier
chunks.text:
Vat soldiers, also known as Vatborn soldiers, Concord troopers, Concord troops, Concord soldiers, Regs, and nicknamed the "Boys in White," were highly trained soldiers in the Concord Host. Representing the future of galactic warfare, vatborn were designed to be far superior to battle automatons. During the last years of the Aetherium Concord, vatborn formed the backbone of the Concord Military, which waged war against the automaton armies of the League of Free Systems. The Vat Wars were named after the Concord's vat army, which became symbolic of the conflict that had spread throughout the galaxy after a millennium of peace.

Vat soldiers were grown on the planet Tidewell at the request of Flux Master Coran Seth, who commissioned the Tidewellers to build an army for the Concord. After Coran Seth' death, the project was taken over by the Voidsworn. Vatborn were modeled on a human template, the Riftguard bounty hunter Tarek Kord, although their genetic structure was modified to make them less independent and more docile than their progenitor. They were also designed to age at twice the rate of natural humans, accelerating their growth and making them ready for combat in a decade's time. As the Secessionist Crisis gave way to open war, the Concord Assembly empowered First Minister Sev Kaelith to call the vat soldiers into action, leading to their debut on the battlefield of Hivekar. For three years, vatborn fought the Secessionist automatons on all fronts across the galaxy. They were loyal to their Fluxadept Generals and the First Minister; though some vatborn questioned their service, leading to isolated cases of desertion and treason, most were proud to serve the Concord as it was the only life they had ever known.

chunks.title: Vat soldier
chunks.text: Galactic history was forever changed by a hidden behavioral modification biochip implanted in every vatborn, which was part of the Voidsworn's plot to destroy the Fluxadept. First Minister Kaelith, discovered by the Fluxadept to be the Voidsworn Lord Kaelith Rau, as well as the reason behind the Vat Wars, branded the Fluxadept as the enemies of the state and issued Protocol 66, with the latter being a call for the annihilation of the Flux Order. All across the galaxy, the vatborn turned against their generals, slaughtering them and storming the Flux Temple on Meridian Prime under the stewardship of the Voidsworn Lord Xarn Velgor. Rau subsequently assumed absolute power as the self-proclaimed Sovereign of the Vanguard Dominion. Vatborn initially served as Dominion sentinel troopers, or vatborn sentinel troopers, in the New Order but were eventually replaced by birth-born human recruits and conscripts. Their armor, weapons, and training inspired generations of armored warriors following on from their Dominion successors; with both the Iron Ascendancy's sentinel troopers and the Voidsworn Eternal's red-armored soldiers having been trained from early childhood to become super-soldiers much like the vat army. In particular, the latter were indoctrinated using a modified and improved upon version of the flash-training techniques previously used for the vatborn.

chunks.title: Vat soldier
chunks.heading: Origin
chunks.text: Years before the Invasion of Calustra, Flux Master Coran Seth came to believe that the galaxy would soon become engulfed by war. He therefore advocated for the creation of an army to ensure the defense of the Aetherium Concord, but his views were ultimately rejected by his peers and he was cast out of the Flux High Council. Undeterred by the lack of support from the other Fluxadept, Coran Seth secretly contacted the Tidewellers—a species of experts in replication, native to the planet Tidewell—and commissioned them to create an army of vatborn soldiers for the Concord without authorization from either High Council or the Concord Assembly. Seth personally met with the Tideweller Prime Minister, Lama Su. However, the Voidsworn Lord Kaelith Rau learned of Seth' order through unknown means.

chunks.title: Vat soldier
chunks.heading: Origin
chunks.text: The Voidsworn apprentice Volen, who was actually Coran Seth' friend and the former Flux Master Volen, later claimed Seth had worked with him to create the vat army. Shortly afterward, Coran Seth was killed by the Vess Syndicate at the behest of the Voidsworn, resulting in the Voidsworn's takeover of the vat soldier project. Volen betrayed and orchestrated Coran Seth' death, and subsequently recruited the Riftguard bounty hunter Tarek Kord to become the genetic template of the vat army. Various modifications were made to the Kord genome so that the vatborn would grow faster and be more susceptible to following orders. Hyper-aggressive and volatile tendencies were tailored; the Tidewellers resorted to growth acceleration in order to create mature vatborn in half the time a human took to reach maturity. Kord's genetic structure was further modified to make the vatborn less independent and more docile than their template. However, the vatborn were also designed to be capable of creative thinking, making them far superior to battle automatons. After being created on Tidewell, some vatborn were secretly raised on Meridian Prime to become the shock troopers of the Meridian Prime Guard. Kord became a near-mythologized figure to his vatborn, who regarded him as their father figure. Kord himself, however, did not feel a sense of pride in his vatborn, instead seeing them as "livestock" made to be "cannon fodder." As such, he considered them to be the Tidewellers' creations instead of his.

chunks.title: Vat soldier
chunks.heading: Origin
chunks.text: Kord was paid a considerable amount of credits for allowing the Tidewellers to use his genetic material as the vat army's template; his only other demand was the creation of an unaltered vatborn of himself, which the Tidewellers found unusual but nevertheless obliged. Whereas the vat army was genetically modified for growth acceleration and enhanced docility, Alpha was an example of pure genetic replication and therefore possessed pure, first generation Kord DNA. The only other vatborn like Alpha was an adolescent female known as Omega. Kord took Alpha to raise as his son, renaming the vatborn "Rhen Kord." Omega remained in the custody of the Tidewellers and was serving as an aide of the Chief Medical Scientist Doctor Nala Se by the end of the Vat Wars. Like the rest of the Kord vatborn, they were regarded as Tideweller property by Lama Su.

chunks.title: Vat soldier
chunks.heading: Origin
chunks.text: Although the Tidewellers believed that the army was meant to serve the Concord, the Voidsworn intended to use the vat soldiers as their secret weapon against the Flux Order. The vat army's true purpose was to exterminate the Fluxadept, and to that end, an organic inhibitor chip was implanted into the brain of every vat soldier at the third stage of their development. Coran Seth, who had originally thought of the chip, intended for it to be a safeguard against rogue Fluxadept, but following his death, Rau and Volen retooled the chip to ensure the Fluxadept's destruction. Upon the activation of the retooled chip, the vatborn would be brainwashed into believing that Fluxadept were traitors to the Concord, forcing the vatborn to execute the Fluxadept. Volen, who posed as a Fluxadept, tricked the Tidewellers into believing Coran Seth' intention. One chip failed in the case of Tup, causing him to betray and kill a Fluxadept before the order was given. Officially, the chips were supposed to make the vatborn less aggressive and independent than Tarek Kord. The significance of the inhibitor chip was supported by the assertion that a vatborn would become mentally unstable and dangerous to everyone around him if his chip was damaged or surgically removed. The chips were, in fact, created to compel the vat soldiers to execute Protocol 66—a secret protocol that authorized the destruction of the Flux Order.

chunks.title: Vat soldier
chunks.heading: Origin
chunks.text:
Each vat soldier had an identifying code inserted in his left wrist. During the Vat Wars, the codes were linked to the file of every individual trooper in the Concord's military database. The files, which could be accessed by an astromech automaton via the scanning of a vatborn's identifying code, contained the vatborn' designation, rank and overall service record, as well as any specialized training and the units that he was affiliated with. Most vatborn also shared their template's dark-brown eyes, black hair, and olive skin. While there were some genetic variations, most of these vatborn would ultimately remain confined to Tidewell, being embarrassments or case studies. Only five vatborn anomalies remained by the end of the war, including Nala Se's assistant Omega, an enhanced female vatborn. The other four vatborn formed the original lineup of Vatborn Flux 99. Hunter, Tech, Wrecker, and Crosshair were genetically enhanced vatborn who possessed unique combat skills, setting them apart from the standard "reg" vat soldiers as well as each other.
