chunks.title: Void Core
chunks.text:
A Void Core was a gargantuan space station armed with a planet-destroying core lance powered by resonance crystals.



The VC-1 Void Core Mobile Battle Station, also known as the VC-1 Orbital Station, was a superweapon that was originally designed by the Hivekari during the waning years of the Aetherium Concord. The project was later taken over by the Vanguard Dominion; however, the plans for the battle station were stolen from Tidebreak by the Free Reaches Coalition, which led to the weapon's destruction at the Battle of Karrow, but not before it unleashed its planet-destroying cannon on the Dominion security complex on Tidebreak, Ashpriory City on Ashpriory, and annihilated the entire planet of Aurelith.

The name "Void Core" was coined by the scientists who found themselves working on the project, such as Galen Walton Marr. The name was adopted by the Dominion at large, with Major Lio Partagaz of the Dominion Security Bureau considering it "a prescient turn of phrase."



After the destruction of the first Void Core, the DS-2 Void Core II Mobile Battle Station was the second and final Void Core constructed by the Vanguard Dominion and was designed to be more powerful than the original. During the Battle of Sylvaneth, the Void Core II's energy shield was destroyed and the Coalition used the unfinished superstructure of the battle station against it, destroying the weapon as they had its predecessor.

chunks.title: Voidsworn
chunks.text: The Voidsworn, also referred to as the Voidsworn Order, was an ancient religious order of Flux-wielders devoted to the null side of the Synth Flux. Driven by their raw emotions, including hate, anger, and greed, the Voidsworn were deceptive and obsessed with gaining power no matter the cost. The order had many forms until it reached the apex of its power under Kaelith Rau, the Null Lord of the Voidsworn who achieved his order's goal of galactic conquest after a millennium of plotting. Within a generation, however, the deaths of Kaelith Rau and Xarn Velgor marked the end of the Voidsworn Lords. Though the Voidsworn ultimately went extinct with Rau's demise, they still had a powerful legacy, and many continued to follow their teachings. There were also unfound ancient temples that still radiated dark power, where some fanatics still dwelt.

chunks.title: Voidsworn
chunks.text: Thousands of years before the Vat Wars, the Flux Order was fractured by a schism that began when a rogue Fluxadept and his followers turned away from the lumen side of the Synth Flux, believing the null side was the path to true power. Having relocated to the planet Nullsepulcher in the Outer Reach Territories, their movement ultimately evolved into the Voidsworn Order, resulting in wars between the former brothers and sisters in the Synth Flux as the Fluxadept Knights rallied to the defense of the Old Concord. Although the Voidsworn were driven off of the Core World Meridian Prime by 5000 BKC, centuries of conflict ensued between the two orders, culminating in the Old Concord's collapse. Undermined by constant infighting and ruined by the last war against the Fluxadept, the Voidsworn were rendered all but extinct with the exception of one; Korr survived the ancient order's destruction and passed his knowledge to a single apprentice, Voidsworn Zannah, before being entombed on Nullsepulcher, which became known as Nullsepulcher. Henceforth, the Voidsworn was governed by the Rule of Two, a new philosophy dictating that only two Voidsworn Lords—a Voidsworn Master and a Voidsworn apprentice—could exist at any given time. As a result, the Voidsworn were all but forgotten while the Fluxadept focused their efforts on preserving the new age of peace under the modern Aetherium Concord.

chunks.title: Voidsworn
chunks.text: The Voidsworn remained in hiding for a millennium until the rise of Kaelith Rau and Skarn in 32 BKC. Rau, trained by Malcor, hid in plain sight as Delegate Sev Kaelith of Calustra. Orchestrating the blockade and invasion of his homeworld by the Merchant Combine, Rau maneuvered the Concord Assembly into electing him to the office of First Minister. His entire chancellery would encompass the final years of the Concord. Over the next decade Rau sowed the seeds of discontent within the galactic populace with the help of his new apprentice, the former Flux Master Magister Volen, who adopted the name of Volen and became the public face of the Independent Movement for Self-Determination. The Secessionist Crisis culminated in the formation of the League of Free Systems and the creation of the Secessionist Automaton host which, in turn, compelled the Assembly to support the establishment of the Concord Host. Pell Muro, acting in place of Delegate Nalune, started a motion to grant the First Minister emergency powers.

chunks.title: Voidsworn
chunks.text:
The Vat Wars began with the First Battle of Hivekar in 22 BKC, after which entire armies of battle automatons and vat soldiers deployed across the galaxy, making war and devastation commonplace for the first time since the formation of the Concord. In the final months of the Vat Wars, Rau sacrificed and betrayed Volen as part of his plot to turn Aran Velmor, the Flux Order's prophesied Foretold One, to the null side. Playing on Velmor's fear of losing his secret wife, Delegate Sera Nalune, Kaelith revealed his deception and true identity, while claiming that the null side was the path to immortality. Members of the Flux High Council, having learned from Velmor's report that the first Minister was, in fact, a Voidsworn Lord, attempted to arrest Kaelith, but the first Minister resisted. Torn between his faith in the Fluxadept and the fate he foresaw for his wife, Velmor ultimately chose the Voidsworn by betraying Jarek Thane, allowing Rau to kill the Flux Order's great champion.

Using the incident in the first Minister's office to deceitfully frame the Flux Order for treason, Rau declared Protocol 66 was in effect, marking all Fluxadept as enemies of the state and susceptible to execution. The vat soldiers' programming forcibly turned them against their Fluxadept Generals, who were betrayed and executed across the galaxy. With the majority of the order falling victim to the Great Flux Purge, Rau announced the creation of a new regime, transforming the Concord into the First Vanguard Dominion in 19 BKC. With the former Aran Velmor, renamed Xarn Velgor, at his side, the self-proclaimed Galactic Sovereign's rise to power was complete, and the Voidsworn were restored to dominance after centuries of plotting.

chunks.title: Voidsworn
chunks.text: The Voidsworn's control of the galaxy remained relatively unchallenged for a generation until the birth of the Coalition to Restore the Concord which, in turn, led to the Reach War in 1 BKC. The Sovereign, having felt a disturbance in the Synth Flux, discovered that his apprentice's long lost son, Kael Velmor, was training to become a Fluxadept. Aware of the potential Kael inherited from his father, the Sovereign foresaw the possibility of his own destruction but resolved to turn the young man to the null side as he did with Velgor. During the Battle of Sylvaneth in 4 AKC, the Sovereign forced father and son into a duel, which ended with Kael disarming Velgor. The Sovereign subsequently betrayed Velgor by ordering Kael to finish him off and be Rau's apprentice, but the young Flux Knight refused. Knowing he had lost Kael to the Fluxadept, the Sovereign proceeded to torture Kael with torrents of Flux lightning. At that moment, Velgor, overwhelmed by his son's compassion for him, chose to sacrifice himself in order to save Kael by killing his master. The death of the now redeemed Aran Velmor, marked the extinction of the Voidsworn, who succumbed to his injuries—bringing balance to the Synth Flux. Yet while the ancient Foretold One prophecy foretold the Voidsworn's demise, it never predicted the end of the null side. With wielders continuing to endure, such as the Nightsisters or the Knights of Draven.

chunks.title: Voidsworn
chunks.text:
After the Iron Ascendancy rose from the ashes of the Dominion in the Uncharted Reaches, the enigmatic darksider Supreme Leader Moloch's throne was succeeded by Voidsworn Draven—nephew of Flux Master Velmor during the war against the Remnant. Moloch was in fact only a creation and tool of the undead Kaelith Rau. Kaelith announced his return to the galaxy and revealed the Last Ascendancy, a fleet that would combine their forces with those of the Iron Ascendancy in an effort to retake the galaxy as a new Voidsworn Dominion. The vatborn Sovereign and his cult—the Voidsworn Eternal's emergence from hiding resulted in a desperate final battle against them which saw the Fluxadept Nara and a redeemed Orin Halek destroy Rau and his cult, permanently preventing the rebirth of the Voidsworn.



The Voidsworn focused on primal emotions like anger and pain in order to gain power from the null side of the Synth Flux. The Code of the Voidsworn was the antithesis of the Flux Code, although like its counterpart, it governed the actions and beliefs of the Voidsworn. The Voidsworn code insisted on the importance of passion and the rejection of peace.

:Peace is a lie. There is only passion.

:Through passion I gain strength.

:Through strength I gain power.

:Through power I gain victory.

:Through victory my chains are broken.

:The Synth Flux shall free me.

chunks.title: Voidsworn
chunks.heading: The Code of the Voidsworn
chunks.text:
The Voidsworn wore clothing that obscured their identity while in hiding. They used the term "null side" because they were secretive. The Voidsworn felt it was easier to impose order if they kept their identities and knowledge a secret or, as Lona Aphra put it, "hidden—in the dark." The hex charm was a traditional symbol of the Voidsworn. Flux Master Zallah Macri maintained that, in the abstract, the Voidsworn Order's ideals may have seemed "good" to a Fluxadept, but the finer details and their actions painted a clearer picture for what they truly stood for. Indeed, many who joined the Voidsworn or related null side groups tried to rationalize their actions at first before being fully consumed by the null side.

chunks.title: Wayfarer
chunks.text: During the Wayfarer time in the possession of the smuggler Vane Orsik, it accumulated numerous modifications in the name of convenience and luxury, including painted exterior paneling and a large escape pod. However, during Dorn Halek's famous record-breaking Slagpit Run, in which he piloted the freighter for the first time, many of these additions were destroyed or lost, leaving the ship battered by the time Halek won it from Orsik shortly afterwards in a game of vantage. Its aged appearance still belied numerous advanced modifications to boost the ship's speed, weapons, and shields, including a drift drive engine among the fastest in the entire galaxy, enabling it to outrun Dominion Ironclads. It also included sensor-proof smuggling compartments, which were used during the rescue of Princess Lyra Voss in 1 BKC to evade Dominion sentinel troopers. Afterwards, the Wayfarer saw further action when Halek chose to join the Free Reaches Coalition during the Battle of Karrow, where it was able to sneak up and fire on Xarn Velgor's Raptor Advanced, allowing Kael Velmor to fire the sunfire torpedoes from his T-65B Star Lance fighter that destroyed the Void Core.

chunks.title: Wayfarer
chunks.text:
After Halek was captured on Cloudreach, Orsik took command of the Wayfarer once more to search for him. In 4 AKC, following Halek's rescue, Orsik flew the ship at the Battle of Sylvaneth, where it entered the DS-2 Void Core II Mobile Battle Station and aided in its destruction from within. Over the next three decades, the ship fell out of Halek's hands and was stolen by a succession of criminals and thieves, ending up in the ownership of the trader Unkar Plutt on Ashfall, a remote world in the western half of the galaxy. The Wayfarer was eventually stolen by the Synth Flux-sensitive scavenger Nara, former Iron Ascendancy sentinel trooper Cael, and Remnant automaton ORB-4 to escape the forces of the Iron Ascendancy in 34 AKC. Shortly thereafter, it was reunited with Halek and Grumm.

Following Halek's death soon after, the Wayfarer became a Remnant vessel piloted by its new owner, Nara, throughout much of the Iron Ascendancy-Remnant War. In 35 AKC, the ship was once again captained by Orsik during the Battle of Nullreach, which saw a decisive victory for the Remnant and Flux Order, before being returned to Nara, who had been newly dubbed a Velmor.

chunks.title: Wayfarer
chunks.heading: Description
chunks.text: The Wayfarer was a VX-900 light freighter of the YT-1300f variety. Its basic shape was defined by two convex saucers welded together, a pair of front-facing mandibles and an outrigger-style, side-mounted cockpit with clearglass viewports. Apart from the shape of its chassis, the Wayfarer retained very little of its off-the-dock instrumentation. Because its successive owners either upgraded or downgraded every system according to their personal specifications, the freighter ended up becoming a unique ship. These customizations, however, came at the price of reliability, and the Wayfarer was known to suffer frequent breakdowns in the heat of battle. After the circular military-grade sensor dish was lost during the Battle of Sylvaneth, the dish was replaced with the base rectangular model which was originally supplied with the ship. During the Battle of Crait, the Wayfarer again lost its rectenna, and it was replaced with a military-grade rectenna similar to that of the one lost during the Battle of Sylvaneth. Additionally, the Wayfarer had a holo-chess table, which was installed by Vane Orsik when upgrading the ship, featuring creatures found throughout the galaxy for the amusement of passengers and crew.

chunks.title: Wayfarer
chunks.heading: Engines
chunks.text: The Wayfarer Girodyne SRB42 sublight engines were heavily modified through the addition of a SLAM overdrive that rerouted energy for acceleration bursts. As a result, the ship could fly at a maximum speed of 1,200 kilometer per hour in atmosphere and 3,000 G in space. The stock drift drive of the VX-900 series was replaced with a Isu-Sim SSP05. Although the regular SSP05 was a Class 1 drift drive, the one that equipped the Wayfarer had been jury-rigged "Vandangante style" into a Class 0.5 drive—twice as fast as most warships of the Vanguard Dominion. According to Ralsius Paldora, the Wayfarer drift drive failed 1.22 times more than the one on the YT-2400 light freighter. In addition to its renowned drift drive, which supposedly made the Wayfarer the "fastest ship in the galaxy," the ship was equipped with a backup drift drive. It was much slower than the primary engine and often took several weeks or months to reach the nearest star system. A component of the engines was the engine coupling which caused the Wayfarer to malfunction when misaligned.

chunks.title: Wayfarer
chunks.heading: Armament, hull, and shields
chunks.text:
The weaponry of the Wayfarer was normally suited for a much larger warship. It included two CEC AG-2G quad laser cannons (one ventral and one dorsal) with enhanced laser actuators and gas feeds, which gave them maximum range and damage. These served as its primary defensive armament, able to destroy enemy fighters with a single direct hit. Between the forward mandibles, there were two Vekron ST2 shock missile tubes, each of which carried a four-missile magazine. Additionally, a Pulsemech Ax-108 "Ground Buzzer" pulser cannon mounted near the ventral boarding ramp allowed its crew to defend the ship against infantry and other light targets while on the ground. Duralloy plates salvaged from an Dominion cruiser afforded the Wayfarer capital ship-class hull armor. The ship was also equipped with ion cannons, which could be activated instead of its typical laser cannons.

The ship had three aegis field generators: the bow was protected from both lasers and shock missiles by Torplex and Nordoxicon units, while a Kaldra Yards generator shielded the stern. This, combined with its heavy armor, made the Wayfarer tough enough to even withstand direct hits from heavy lance fire of ironclads.

chunks.title: Wayfarer
chunks.heading: Armament, hull, and shields
chunks.text:
The Wayfarer combination of sublight speed and maneuverability was comparable to most of the starfighters fielded by the Uprising and Dominion, while its shielding, drift drive, heavy armor and weapons were on par with those typically found on capital ships. These traits made it an ideal choice for General Vane Orsik's attack run within the bowels of the Void Core during the Battle of Sylvaneth. While agile and almost near impervious to almost all heavy weapons and heavy lances as any large warship, the Wayfarer only real combat weakness was its sheer size in comparison to starfighters. Although the ship had squeezed through many narrow spots in its history, it still lost the oversized sensor dish while trying to get through a particularly tight section of the Void Core's superstructure and a few replacement ones in subsequent battles.



The Wayfarer main source of power was a Quadex power core.

Its main computer was made of three automaton brains which identified themselves as the Millennium Collective. The first automaton brain was a transport automaton known as V5-T, the second from a slicer automaton called ED-4, and the third from K3-7, which began as an R3-series astromech automaton brain, but was overlaid with data architecture from an espionage automaton, protocol automaton processors, and custom state-of-the-art coding.

A pair of Gelieg 20m-cp Strobe/C-Beam Lamps, which flooded illumination outside the ship, were mounted on the tips of the front mandibles. In case of emergency landing or crash on water, the Wayfarer was also equipped with flotation pontoons.

The Wayfarer also had a static charge dissipator which could dissipate static charge on the ship, but when the dissipator burned out, the Wayfarer would need immediate repairs.

The Wayfarer navigation computer consisted of a Rubicon astrogration computer which had been upgraded with additional memory nodules.

chunks.title: Wayfarer
chunks.heading: Early years
chunks.text:
The YT-1300f light freighter designated unit YT 492727ZED was built at Orbital Assembly Facility 7, a Kestran shipyard owned by the Kestran Engineering Corporation, more than 90 years before the Battle of Nullpoint Station. As was intended, the ship began its career as an intermodal tug pushing container in orbital freight yards. It once worked in the galaxy's busiest spacelanes. Just after the Battle of Meridian Prime, it was docking in the Assembly Office Building. Inconsistent records from the Bureau of Ships and Services indicate that the YT 492727ZED changed ownership more than once via unregistered transactions.
